metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: incompatible with these kinds of self-replicating systems with faster OODA loops.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: For one final time putting your alien flash god hat on and you look at human civilization,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: do you think about the 7.8 billion people on earth as individual little creatures, individual

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: little organisms, or do you think of us as one organism with a collective intelligence?

body.input: What's the proper framework through which to analyze it again as an alien?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So that I know where you're coming from, would you have asked the question the same way before

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: the Industrial Revolution, before the Agricultural Revolution when there were half a billion people

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: and no telecommunications connecting them?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: I would indeed ask the question the same way, but I would be less confident about your conclusions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: It would be an actually more interesting way to ask the question at that time, but I was

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: nevertheless asked it the same way, yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Well let's go back further and smaller then.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Other than just a single human or the entire human species, let's look at a relatively

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: isolated tribe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: In the relatively isolated, probably sub-Dunbar number, sub-150 people tribe, do I look at

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: that as one entity where evolution is selecting for it based on group selection or do I think

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: of it as 150 individuals that are interacting in some way?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Well could those individuals exist without the group?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: No.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: The evolutionary adaptiveness of humans was involved critically group selection and individual

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: humans alone trying to figure out stone tools and protection and whatever aren't what was

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: selected for.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And so I think the or is the wrong frame.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: I think it's individuals are affecting the group that they're a part of.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: They're also dependent upon and being affected by the group that they're a part of.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And so this now starts to get deep into political theories also, which is theories that orient

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: towards the collective at different scales, whether a tribal scale or an empire or a nation

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: state or something, and ones that orient towards the individual liberalism and stuff like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And I think there's very obvious failure modes on both sides.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And so the relationship between them is more interesting to me than either of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: The relationship between the individual and the collective and the question around how

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: to have a virtuous process between those.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So a good social system would be one where the organism of the individual and the organism

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: of the group of individuals is they're both synergistic to each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So what is best for the individuals and what's best for the whole is aligned.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: But there is nevertheless an individual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: They're not, it's a matter of degrees, I suppose, but what defines a human more, the social

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: network within which they've been brought up, through which they've developed their

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: intelligence or is it their own sovereign individual self?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: What's your intuition of how much, not just for evolutionary survival, but as intellectual

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: beings, how much do we need others for our development?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: I think we have a weird sense of this today relative to most previous periods of Sapien

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: I think the vast majority of Sapien history is tribal, like depending upon your early

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: human model, 200,000 or 300,000 years of Homo sapiens in little tribes where they depended

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: upon that tribe for survival and excommunication from the tribe was fatal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: I think they, and our whole evolutionary genetic history is in that environment and the amount

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: of time we've been out of it is relatively so tiny.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And then we still depended upon extended families and local communities more and the big kind

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: of giant market complex where I can provide something to the market to get money, to be

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: able to get other things from the market where it seems like I don't need anyone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: It's almost like disintermediating our sense of need, even though your and my ability to

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: talk to each other using these mics and the phones that we coordinated on took millions

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: of people over six continents to be able to run the supply chains that made all the stuff

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: that we depend on, but we don't notice that we depend upon them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: They all seem fungible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: If you take a baby, obviously that you didn't even get to a baby without a mom.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Was it dependent, or we depended upon each other, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Without two parents at minimum and they depended upon other people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: But if we take that baby and we put it out in the wild, it obviously dies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So if we let it grow up for a little while, the minimum amount of time where it starts

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: to have some autonomy and then we put it out in the wild, and this has happened a few times,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: it doesn't learn language and it doesn't learn the small motor articulation that we learn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: It doesn't learn the type of consciousness that we end up having that is socialized.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So I think we take for granted how much conditioning affects us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Is it possible that it affects basically 99.9 or maybe the whole thing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: The whole thing is the connection between us humans and that we're no better than apes

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: without our human connections.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Because thinking of it that way forces us to think very differently about human society

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: and how to progress forward if the connections are fundamental.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: I just have to object to the no better than apes because better here, I think you mean

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: a specific thing, which means have capacities that are fundamentally different than I think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Apes also depend upon troops.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And I think the idea of humans as better than nature in some kind of ethical sense ends

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: up having heaps of problems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: We'll table that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: We can come back to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: But when we say what is unique about homo sapien capacity relative to the other animals

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: we currently inhabit the biosphere with, and I'm saying it that way because there were

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: other early hominids that had some of these capacities, we believe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Our tool creation and our language creation and our coordination are all kind of the results

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: of a certain type of capacity for abstraction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And other animals will use tools, but they don't evolve the tools they use.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: They keep using the same types of tools that they basically can find.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: that a sharper rock will cut it better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: I don't want to go all the way back to the aliens who've seen all of civilization, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: to just recognize that for all of human history, as far as we're aware, there were existential

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: risks to civilizations and they happened.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: There were civilizations that were killed in war, tribes that were killed in tribal

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: warfare or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So people faced existential risk to the group that they identified with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: It's just those were local phenomena.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: It wasn't a fully global phenomena.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So an empire could fall and surrounding empires didn't fall.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Maybe they came in and filled the space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: The first time that we were able to think about catastrophic risk, not from like a solar

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: flare or something that we couldn't control, but from something that humans would actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: create at a global level was World War II and the bomb.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Because it was the first time that we had tech big enough that could actually mess up

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: everything at a global level.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: It could mess up habitability.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: We just weren't powerful enough to do that before.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: It's not that we didn't behave in ways that would have done it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: We just only behaved in those ways at the scale we could affect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: It's important to get that there's the entire world before World War II where we don't have

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: the ability to make a nonhabitable biosphere, nonhabitable for us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Then there's World War II and the beginning of a completely new phase where global human

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: induced catastrophic risk is now a real thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: That was such a big deal that it changed the entire world in a really fundamental way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: which is when you study history, it's amazing how big a percentage of history is studying

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: war.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: In the history of wars, you study European history and whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: It's generals and wars and empire expansions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: The major empires near each other never had really long periods of time where they weren't

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: engaged in war or preparation for war or something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Humans don't have a good precedent in the post tribal phase, the civilization phase

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: of being able to solve conflicts without war for very long.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: World War II was the first time where we could have a war that no one could win.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: The superpowers couldn't fight again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: They couldn't do a real kinetic war.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: They could do diplomatic wars and Cold War type stuff and they could fight proxy wars

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: through other countries that didn't have the big weapons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Mutually assured destruction and coming out of World War II, we actually realized that

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: nation states couldn't prevent world war.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: We needed a new type of supervening government in addition to nation states, which was the

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: whole Bretton Woods world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: The United Nations, the World Bank, the IMF, the globalization trade type agreements, mutually

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: assured destruction that was how do we have some coordination beyond just nation states

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: between them since we have to stop war between at least the superpowers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And it was pretty successful given that we've had like 75 years of no superpower on superpower

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: war.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: We've had lots of proxy wars during that time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: We've had Cold War.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And I would say we're in a new phase now where the Bretton Woods solution is basically over,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: almost over.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Can you describe the Bretton Woods solution?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: The Bretton Woods, the series of agreements for how the nations would be able to engage

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: with each other in a solution other than war was these IGOs, these intergovernmental organizations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: and was the idea of globalization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Since we could have global effects, we needed to be able to think about things globally

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: where we had trade relationships with each other where it would not be profitable to

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: war with each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: It'd be more profitable to actually be able to trade with each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So our own self-interest was going to drive our non-war interest.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And so this started to look like, and obviously this couldn't have happened that much earlier

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: either because industrialization hadn't gotten far enough to be able to do massive global

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: industrial supply chains and ship stuff around quickly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: But like we were mentioning earlier, almost all the electronics that we use today, just

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: basic cheap stuff for us is made on six continents, made in many countries.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: There's no single country in the world that could actually make many of the things that

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: we have, and from the raw material extraction to the plastics and polymers and the, you

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: know, et cetera.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And so the idea that we made a world that could do that kind of trade and create massive

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: GDP growth, we could all work together to be able to mine natural resources and grow

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: With the rapid GDP growth, there was the idea that everybody could keep having more without

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: having to take each other's stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And so that was part of kind of the Bretton Woods post-World War II model.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: The other was that we would be so economically interdependent that blowing each other up

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: would never make sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: That worked for a while.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Now it also brought us up into planetary boundaries faster.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: The unrenewable use of resource and turning those resources into pollution on the other

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: side of the supply chain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So obviously that faster GDP growth meant the overfishing of the oceans and the cutting

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: down of the trees and the climate change and the mining, toxic mining tailings going into

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: the water and the mountaintop removal mining and all those types of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: That's the overconsumption side of the risk that we're talking about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And so the answer of let's do positive GDP as the answer rapidly and exponentially obviously

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: accelerated the planetary boundary side.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And that was thought about for a long time, but it started to be modeled with the Club

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: of Rome and limits of growth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: But it's just very obvious to say if you have a linear materials economy where you take

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: stuff out of the earth faster, whether it's fish or trees or oil, you take it out of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: earth faster than it can replenish itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And you turn it into trash after using it for a short period of time, you put the trash

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: in the environment faster than it can process itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And there's toxicity associated with both sides of this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: You can't run an exponentially growing linear materials economy on a finite planet forever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: That's not a hard thing to figure out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And it has to be exponential if there's an exponentiation in the monetary supply because

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: of interest and then fractional reserve banking and to then be able to keep up with the growing

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: monetary supply.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: You have to have growth of goods and services.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So that's that kind of thing that has happened.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: But you also see that when you get these supply chains that are so interconnected across the

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: world, you get increased fragility because a collapse or a problem in one area then affects

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: the whole world in a much bigger area as opposed to the issues being local.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So we got to see with COVID and an issue that started in one part of China affecting the

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: whole world so much more rapidly than would have happened before Bretton Woods, before

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: international travel supply chains, that whole kind of thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And with a bunch of second and third order effects that people wouldn't have predicted,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: okay, we have to stop certain kinds of travel because of viral contaminants, but the countries

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: doing agriculture depend upon fertilizer they don't produce that is shipped into them and

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: depend upon pesticides they don't produce.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So we got both crop failures and crops being eaten by locusts in scale in Northern Africa

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: and Iran and things like that because they couldn't get the supplies of stuff in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So then you get massive starvation or future kind of hunger issues because of supply chain

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: shutdowns.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So you get this increased fragility and cascade dynamics where a small problem can end up

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: leading to cascade effects.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And also, we went from two superpowers with one catastrophe weapon to now that same catastrophe

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: weapon is there's more countries that have it, eight or nine countries that have it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: and there's a lot more types of catastrophe weapons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: We now have catastrophe weapons with weaponized drones that can hit infrastructure targets,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: with bio, with...

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: In fact, every new type of tech has created an arms race.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So we have not, with the UN or the other kind of intergovernmental organizations, we haven't

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: been able to really do nuclear deproliferation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: We've actually had more countries get nukes and keep getting faster nukes, the race to

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: hypersonics and things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And every new type of technology that has emerged has created an arms race.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And so you can't do mutually assured destruction with multiple agents the way you can with

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: two agents.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Two agents, it's much easier to create a stable Nash equilibrium that's forced.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: But the ability to monitor and say, if these guys shoot, who do I shoot?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Do I shoot them?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Do I shoot everybody?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Do I?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So it's a three body problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: You get a very complex type of thing when you have multiple agents and multiple different

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: types of catastrophe weapons, including ones that can be much more easily produced than

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: nukes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Nukes are really hard to produce.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: There's only uranium in a few areas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Uranium enrichment is hard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: ICBMs are hard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: But weaponized drones hitting smart targets is not so hard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: There's a lot of other things where basically the scale at being able to manufacture them

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: is going way, way down to where even non-state actors can have them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And so when we talk about exponential tech and the decentralization of exponential tech,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: what that means is decentralized catastrophe weapon capacity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And especially in a world of increasing numbers of people feeling disenfranchised, frantic,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So we could say, in a way, humans were being domesticated by those groups.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: They were learning how to have certain rules to participate with the group without which

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: you'd get kicked out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: But that's still the wild state of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And maybe it's useful to do as a side statement, which I've recently looked at a bunch of papers

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: around Dunbar's number, where the mean is actually 150.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: If you actually look at the original paper, it's really a range.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So it's actually somewhere under a thousand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So it's a range of like two to five hundred or whatever it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: But like you could argue that the I think it actually is exactly two to the ranges two

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: to five hundred and twenty, something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And this is the mean that's taken crudely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: It's not a very good paper in terms of the actual numerical numerically speaking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: But it'd be interesting if there's a bunch of Dunbar numbers that could be computed for

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: particular environments, particular conditions, so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: It is very true that they're likely to be something small, you know, under a million.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: But it'd be interesting if we can expand that number in interesting ways that will change

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: the fabric of this conversation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: I just want to kind of throw that in there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: I don't know if the 150 is baked in somehow into the hardware.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: We can talk about some of the things that it probably has to do with up to a certain

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: number of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And this is going to be variable based on the social technologies that mediate it to

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: some degree.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: We can talk about that in a minute.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Up to a certain number of people, everybody can know everybody else pretty intimately.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So let's go ahead and just take 150 as an average number.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Everybody can know everyone intimately enough that if your actions made anyone else do poorly,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: it's your extended family.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And you're stuck living with them and you know who they are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And there's no anonymous people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: There's no just them and over there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And that's one part of what leads to a kind of tribal process where what's good for the

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: individual and good for the whole has a coupling.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Also, below that scale, everyone is somewhat aware of what everybody else is doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: There's not groups that are very siloed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And as a result, it's actually very hard to get away with bad behavior.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: There's a forced kind of transparency.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And so you don't need kind of like the state in that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: But lying to people doesn't actually get you ahead.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Sociopathic behavior doesn't get you ahead because it gets seen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And so there's a conditioning environment where the individual is behaving in a way

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: that is aligned with the interest of the tribe is what gets conditioned.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: When it gets to be a much larger system, it becomes easier to hide certain things from

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: the group as a whole as well as to be less emotionally bound to a bunch of anonymous

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: I would say there's also a communication protocol where up to about that number of people, we

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: could all sit around a tribal council and be part of a conversation around a really

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: big decision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Do we migrate?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Do we not migrate?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Do we do something like that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Do we get rid of this person?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And why would I want to agree to be a part of a larger group where everyone can't be

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: part of that council?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And so I am going to now be subject to law that I have no say in if I could be part of

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: a smaller group that could still survive and I get a say in the law that I'm subject to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So I think the cleaving and a way we can look at it beyond the Dunbar number two is we can

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: look at that a civilization has binding energy that is holding them together and has cleaving

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: energy and if the binding energy exceeds the cleaving energy, that civilization will last.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And so there are things that we can do to decrease the cleaving energy within the society,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: things we can do to increase the binding energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: I think naturally we saw that had certain characteristics up to a certain size, kind

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: of tribalism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: That ended with a few things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: It ended with people having migrated enough that when you started to get resource wars,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: you couldn't just migrate away easily.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And so tribal warfare became more obligated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: It involved the plow and the beginning of real economic surplus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So there were a few different kind of forcing functions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: But we're talking about what size should it be?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: What size should a society be?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And I think the idea, like if we think about your body for a moment as a self-organizing

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: complex system that is multi-scaled, we think about-

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Our body is a wonderland.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Our body is a wonderland, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: You have-

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: That's John Mayer's song.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: I apologize.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: But yes, so if we think about our body and the billions of cells that are in it-

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Well, you don't have, like think about how ridiculous it would be to try to have all

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: the tens of trillions of cells in it with no internal organization structure, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Just like a sea of protoplasm.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: It wouldn't work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Pure democracy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So you have cells and tissues, and then you have tissues and organs and organs and organ

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And so you have these layers of organization, and then obviously the individual and a tribe

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: and the ecosystem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And each of the higher layers are both based on the lower layers, but also influencing

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: I think the future of civilization will be similar, which is there's a level of governance

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: that happens at the level of the individual, my own governance of my own choice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: I think there's a level that happens at the level of a family.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: We're making decisions together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: We're inter influencing each other and affecting each other, taking responsibility for the

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: idea of an extended family.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And you can see that for a lot of human history, we had an extended family.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: We had a local community, a local church or whatever it was.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: We had these intermediate structures.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Whereas right now there's kind of like the individual producer, consumer, taxpayer voter

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: and the massive nation state global complex.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And not that much in the way of intermediate structures that we relate with and not that

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: much in the way of real personal dynamics, all impersonalized, made fungible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And so I think that we have to have global governance, meaning I think we have to have

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: governance at the scale we affect stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And if anybody is messing up the oceans, that matters for everybody.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So that can't only be national or only local.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Everyone is scared of the idea of global governance because we think about some top down system

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: of imposition that now has no checks and balances on power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: I'm scared of that same version.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So I'm not talking about that kind of global governance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: It's why I'm even using the word governance as a process rather than government as an

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: imposed phenomena.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And so I think we have to have global governance, but I think we also have to have local governance

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: and there has to be relationships between them that each, where there are both checks

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: and balances in power, flows of information.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So I think governance at the level of cities will be a bigger deal in the future than governance

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: at the level of nation states, because I think nation states are largely fictitious things

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: that are defined by wars and agreements to stop wars and like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: I think cities are based on real things that will keep being real, where the proximity

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: of certain things together, the physical proximity of things together gives increased value of

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: those things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So you look at like Jeffrey West's work on scale and finding that companies and nation

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: states and things that have a kind of complicated agreement structure get diminishing return

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: of production per capita as the total number of people increases beyond about the tribal

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: scale, but the city actually gets increasing productivity per capita, but it's not designed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: It's kind of this organic thing, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So there should be governance at the level of cities because people can sense and actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: have some agency there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Probably neighborhoods and smaller scales within it and also verticals, and some of

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: it won't be geographic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: It'll be network based, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Networks of affinities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: So I don't think the future is one type of governance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Now what we can say more broadly is say when we're talking about groups of people that

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: inter-effect each other, the idea of a civilization is that we can figure out how to coordinate

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: our choice-making to not be at war with each other and hopefully increase total productive

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: capacity in a way that's good for everybody.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Coordination of labor and specialty so we all get more better stuff and whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: But it's a coordination of our choice-making.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: I think we can look at civilizations failing on the side of not having enough coordination

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: of choice-making so they fail on the side of chaos and then they cleave and an internal

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: war comes about or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Or they can't make smart decisions and they overuse their resources or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: Or it can fail on the side of trying to get order via imposition, via force.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And so it fails on the side of oppression, which ends up being for a while functional-ish

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: for the thing as a whole, but miserable for most people in it until it fails either because

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: of revolt or because it can't innovate enough or something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191

body.input: And so there's this like toggling between order via oppression and chaos.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Schmachtenberger: Steering Civilization Away from Self-Destruction | Lex Fridman Podcast #191
