metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: But I remember standing on the day of the competition, you know, watching the car with Mike.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And cars are completely empty, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: They're all there lined up in the beginning of the race.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And then, you know, DARPA sends them on their mission one by one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: So they leave and like you just they had these sirens.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: They all had their different silence, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: Each siren had its own personality, if you will.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: So, you know, off they go and you don't see them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And then every once in a while, they come a little bit closer to where the audience is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And you can kind of hear the sound of your car.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And it seems to be moving along.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: So that gives you hope.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And then, you know, it goes away and you can't hear it for too long.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: You start getting anxious, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: So it's a little bit like, you know, sending your kids to college and like, you know, kind of you invested in them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: You hope you build it properly, but it's still anxiety inducing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: So that was an incredibly fun few days in terms of, you know, bugs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: As you mentioned, you know, one that was my bug that caused us the loss of the first place.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: It's still a debate that occasionally have with people on the CMU team.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: CMU came first, I should mention that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: CMU haven't heard of them, but yeah, it's a small school.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: It's really a glitch that, you know, they haven't succeeded something robotics related.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: Very scenic, though.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: Most people go there for the scenery.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: Yeah, it's a beautiful campus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: I apologize.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: Unlike Stanford.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: So for people, yeah, that's true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: Unlike Stanford.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: For people who don't know, CMU is one of the great robotics and sort of artificial intelligence universities in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: CMU Carnegie Ballon University.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: OK, sorry. Go ahead.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: Good, good PC.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: So in the part that I contributed to, which was navigating parking lots and the way that part of the mission work is you in a parking lot,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: you would get from DARPA an outline of the map.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: You basically get this giant polygon that define the perimeter of the parking lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And there would be an entrance and maybe multiple entrances or exits to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And then you would get a goal within that open space, XY heading where the car had to park.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: It had no information about the obstacles that the car might encounter there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: So it had to navigate a completely free space from the entrance to the parking lot into that parking space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And then once it parked there, it had to exit the parking lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: While, of course, in counting and reasoning about all the obstacles that it encounters in real time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: So our interpretation, or at least my interpretation of the rules, was that you had to reverse out of the parking spot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And that's what our cars did, even if there's no obstacle in front.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: That's not what CMU's car did.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And it just kind of drove right through.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: So there's still a debate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And of course, you stop and then reverse out and go out the different way that cost you some time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: So there's still a debate whether it was my poor implementation that cost us extra time or whether it was CMU violating an important rule of the competition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And I have my own opinion here in terms of other bugs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And I have to apologize to Mike Montemariella for sharing this on air.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: But it is actually one of the more memorable ones.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And it's something that's kind of become a bit of a metaphor in the industry since then, I think, at least in some circles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: It's called the victory lap.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And our cars did that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: So in one of the missions in the Urban Challenge and one of the courses, there was this big oval right by the start and finish of the race.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: So the ARPA had a lot of the missions would finish in that same location.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And it was pretty cool because you could see the cars come by, kind of finish that part leg of the trip, that leg of the mission, and then go on and finish the rest of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And other vehicles would come, hit their waypoint and exit the oval and off they would go.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: Our car, on the other hand, which hit the checkpoint, and then it would do an extra lap around the oval and only then leave and go on its merry way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: So over the course of the full day, it accumulated some extra time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And the problem was that we had a bug where it wouldn't start reasoning about the next waypoint and plan a route to get to that next point until it hit a previous one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And in that particular case, by the time you hit that one, it was too late for us to consider the next one and kind of make a lane change.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: So every time we would do like an extra lap.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: So that's the Stanford Victory Lap.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: I feel like there's something philosophically profound in there somehow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: But I mean, ultimately, everybody is a winner in that kind of competition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And it led to sort of famously to the creation of Google Self-Driving Car Project and now Waymo.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: So can we give an overview of how is Waymo born?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: How is the Google Self-Driving Car Project born?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: What is the mission?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: What is the hope?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: What is it is the engineering kind of set of milestones that it seeks to accomplish?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: There's a lot of questions in there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: I don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: Kind of the DARPA Urban Challenge and the previous DARPA Grand Challenges kind of led, I think, to a very large degree to that next step.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And then Larry and Sergey, Larry Page and Sergey Bren, Google founders, I saw that competition and believed in the technology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: The Google Self-Driving Car Project was born.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: You know, at that time, and we started in 2009, it was a pretty small group of us, about a dozen people who came together to work on this project at Google.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: At that time, we saw an incredible early result in the DARPA Urban Challenge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: I think we're all incredibly excited about where we got to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And we believed in the future of the technology, but we still had a very rudimentary understanding of the problem space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: So the first goal of this project in 2009 was to really better understand what we're up against.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And with that goal in mind, when we started the project, we created a few milestones for ourselves that maximized learnings.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: Well, the two milestones were, one was to drive 100,000 miles in autonomous mode, which was at that time orders of magnitude that more than anybody has ever done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And the second milestone was to drive 10 routes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: Each one was 100 miles long.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: They were specifically chosen to become extra spicy, extra complicated, and sample the full complexity of that domain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And you had to drive each one from beginning to end with no intervention, no human intervention.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: So you would get to the beginning of the course, you would press the button that engaged in autonomy, and you had to go for 100 miles, beginning to end with no interventions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And it sampled, again, the full complexity of driving conditions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: Some were on freeways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: We had one route that went all through all the freeways and all the bridges in the Bay Area.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: We had some that went around Lake Tahoe and kind of mountainous roads.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: We had some that drove through dense urban environments like in downtown Palo Alto and through San Francisco.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: So it was incredibly interesting to work on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: It took us just under two years, about a year and a half or a bit more, to finish both of these milestones.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And in that process, it was an incredible amount of fun, probably the most fun I had in my professional career.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And you're just learning so much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: The goal here is to learn a prototype.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: You're not yet starting to build a production system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: So you're just working 24-7 and hacking things together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And you also don't know how hard this is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: I mean, that's the point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: So that's an ambitious, if I put myself in that mindset, even still, that's a really ambitious set of goals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: Like just those two, picking 10 different difficult, spicy challenges and then having zero interventions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: So like not saying gradually, we're going to like, you know, over a period of 10 years,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: we're going to have a bunch of roots and gradually reduce the number of interventions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: That literally says, as soon as possible, we want to have zero and on hard roads.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: So to me, if I was facing that, it's unclear whether that takes two years or whether that takes 20 years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: It took us under two.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: I guess that speaks to a really big difference between doing something once and having a prototype

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: where you are going after learning about the problem versus how you go about engineering a product

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: that where you look at, you properly do evaluation, you look at metrics, you drive down,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: and you're confident that you can do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And I guess that's why it took a dozen people 16 months or a little bit more than that back in 2009 and 2010

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: with the technology of more than a decade ago, that amount of time to achieve that milestone of 10 routes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: 100 miles each and no interventions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And it took us a little bit longer to get to a full driverless product that customers use.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: That's another really important moment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: Is there some memories of technical lessons or just one?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: What did you learn about the problem of driving from that experience?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: I mean, we can now talk about what you learned from modern day Waymo,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: but I feel like you may have learned some profound things in those early days, even more so,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: because it feels like what Waymo is now is to trying to know how to do scale,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: how to make sure you create a product, how to make sure it's safe, those things, which is all fascinating challenges.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: But like you were facing the more fundamental philosophical problem of driving in those early days.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: Like, what the hell is driving as an autonomous?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: Or maybe I'm again romanticizing it, but is there some valuable lessons you picked up over there at those two years?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: A ton. The most important one is probably that we believe that it's doable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And we've gotten far enough into the problem that we had, I think, only a glimpse of the true complexity of the domain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: It's a little bit like climbing a mountain where you kind of see the next peak and you think that's kind of the summit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: But then you get to that and you kind of see that this is just the start of the journey.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: But we've tried, we've sampled enough of the problem space and we've made enough rapid success,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: even with technology of 2009, 2010, that it gave us confidence to then pursue this as a real product.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: So, OK, so the next step, you mentioned the milestones that you had in those two years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: What are the next milestones that then led to the creation of Waymo and beyond?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: It was a really interesting journey.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: And Waymo came a little bit later than we completed those milestones in 2010.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitri Dolgov: Waymo and the Future of Self-Driving Cars | Lex Fridman Podcast #147

body.input: That was the pivot when we decided to focus on actually building a product using this technology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Of course, everything's more difficult than you ever thought it was going to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: But it looks, I would say more true rather than less true over that 10 year period.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: I think I have to take a step back every now and then and think, hang on a minute, where's this going?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: I'm happy it's going in a sensible direction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And I think then you have these other interesting dilemmas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: I mean, I'm often accused of being too focused on life on earth, too kind of narrow minded and inward looking, you might say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: I'm talking about carbon.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: I'm talking about cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And maybe you or plenty of people can say to me, ah, yeah, but life can be anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: I have no imagination.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Maybe they're right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: But unless we can say why life here is this way and if those reasons are fundamental reasons or if they're just trivial reasons, then we can't answer that question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So I think they're fundamental reasons and I think we need to worry about them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Yeah, there might be some deep truth to the puzzle here on earth that will resonate with other puzzles elsewhere that will solving this particular puzzle will give us that deeper truth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So what to this puzzle, you said vents, hydrogen, wet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So chemically, what is the potion here?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: How important is oxygen?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: You wrote a book about this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And I actually just came straight here from a conference where I was chairing a session on whether oxygen matters or not in the history of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Of course, it matters, but it matters most to the origin of life to be not there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: As I see it, we have this, I mean, life is made of carbon, basically, primarily organic molecules with carbon-carbon bonds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And the building block, the Lego brick that we take out of the air or take out of the oceans is carbon dioxide.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And to turn carbon dioxide into organic molecules, we need to strap on hydrogen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And so we need to, and this is basically what life is doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: It's hydrogenating carbon dioxide.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: It's taking the hydrogen that bubbles out of the earth in these hydrothermal vents and it sticks it on CO2.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And it's kind of really as simple as that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And actually thermodynamically, the thing that I find most troubling is that if you do these experiments in the lab,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: the molecules you get are exactly the molecules that we see at the heart of biochemistry in the heart of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Is there something to be said about the earliest origins of that little potion, that chemical process?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: What really is the spark there?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: There isn't a spark.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: There is a continuous chemical reaction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And there is kind of a spark, but it's a continuous electrical charge which helps drive that reaction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So literally spark.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Well, a charge at least, but yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: I mean, a spark in that sense is we tend to think of in terms of Frankenstein,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: we tend to think in terms of electricity and one moment you zap something and it comes alive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And what does that really mean?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: It's come alive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And now what's sustaining it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Well, we are sustained by oxygen, by this continuous chemical reaction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And if you put a plastic bag on your head, then you've got a minute or something before it's all over.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So some way of being able to leverage a source of energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Well, the source of energy at the origin of life is the reaction between carbon dioxide and hydrogen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And amazingly, most of these reactions are exogonic, which is to say they release energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: If you have hydrogen and CO2 and you put them together in a Falcon tube and you warm it up to say 50 degrees centigrade

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: and you put in a couple of catalysts and you shake it, nothing's going to happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: But thermodynamically, that is less stable, two gases, hydrogen and CO2 is less stable than cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: What should happen is you get cells coming out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So why doesn't that happen?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: It's because of the kinetic barriers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: That's where you need the spark.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Is it possible that life originated multiple times on Earth?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: The way you describe it, you make it sound so easy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: There's a long distance to go from the first bits of prebiotic chemistry to say molecular machines like ribosomes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Is that the first thing that you would say is life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Like if I introduce you to the two of you at a party, you would say that's a living thing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: I would say as soon as we introduce genes information into systems that are growing anyway,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: so I would talk about growing protocells, as soon as we introduce even random bits of information into there,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: I'm thinking about RNA molecules, for example, doesn't have to have any information in it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: It can be completely random sequence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: But if it's introduced into a system which is in any case growing and doubling itself and reproducing itself,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: then any changes in that sequence that allow it to do so better or worse are now selected by perfectly normal natural selection.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: But the system...

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So that's when it becomes alive to my mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: That's encompassed into like an object that keeps information and evolves that information over time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: changes that information over time in response to the...

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So it's always part of a cell system from the very beginning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So is your sense that it started only once because it's difficult or is it possibly started in multiple locations on Earth?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: It's possible it started multiple occasions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: There's two provisos to that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: One of them is oxygen makes it impossible really for life to start.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So as soon as we've got oxygen in the atmosphere, then life isn't going to keep starting over.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So I often get asked by people, why can't we have life starting?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: If it's so easy, why can't life start in these vents now?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And the answer is if you want hydrogen to react with CO2 and there's oxygen there, hydrogen reacts with oxygen instead.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: It's just, you know, you get an explosive reaction that way, it's rocket fuel.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So it's never going to happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: But the other...

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: For the origin of life earlier than that, all we know is that there's a single common ancestor for all of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: There could have been multiple origins and they all just disappeared.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: But there's a very interesting deep split in life between bacteria and what are called archaea, which look just the same as bacteria.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And they're not quite as diverse, but nearly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And they are very different in their biochemistry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And so any explanation for the origin of life has to account as well for why they're so different and yet so similar.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And that makes me think that life probably did arise only once.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Can you describe the difference that's interesting there?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: How they're similar, how they're different?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Well, they're different in their membranes primarily.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: They're different in things like DNA replication.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: They use completely different enzymes and the genes behind it for replicating DNA.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So they both have membranes, both have DNA replication.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: The process of that is different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: They both have DNA.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: The genetic code is identical in them both.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: The way in which it's transcribed into RNA, into the copy of a gene, and the way that that's then translated into a protein, that's all basically the same in both these groups.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So they clearly share a common ancestor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: It's just that they're different in fundamental ways as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And if you think about what kind of processes could drive that divergence very early on,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: I can think about it in terms of membranes, in terms of the electrical charges on membranes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And it's that that makes me think that there were probably many unsuccessful attempts and only one really successful attempt.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Can you explain why that divergence makes you think there's one common ancestor?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: OK, can you describe that intuition?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: I'm a little bit unclear about why the divert, like the leap from the divergence means there's one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Do you mean like the divergence indicates that there was a big invention at that time from one source?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: If you've got, as I imagine it, you have a common ancestor living in a hydrothermal vent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Let's say there are millions of vents and millions of potential common ancestors living in all of those vents.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: But only one of them makes it out first.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Then you could imagine that that cell is then going to kind of take over the world and wipe out everything else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And so what you would see would be a single common ancestor for all of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: But with lots of different vent systems all kind of vying to create the first life forms, you might say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So this thing is a cell, a single cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Well, we're always talking about populations of cells, but yes, these are celled organisms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: But the fundamental life form is a single cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Right. So like, or so they're always together, but they're alone together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: There's a machinery in each one individual component that if left by itself would still work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Yes, yes, yes. It's the unit of selection is a single cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: But selection operates over generations and changes over generations in populations of cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So it would be impossible to say that a cell is the unit of selection in the sense that unless you have a population, you can't evolve, you can't change.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Right. But there was one Chuck Norris, it's an American reference, cell that made it out of the vents.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Right. Or like the first one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So imagine then that there's one cell gets out and it takes over the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: It gets out in the water. It's like floating around.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: We're deep in the ocean somewhere, but actually two cells got out and they appear to have got out from the same vent because they both share the same code and everything else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So unless all the, you know, we've got a million different common ancestors in all these different vents.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So either they all have the same code and two cells spontaneously merged from different places or two different cells,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: fundamentally different cells came from the same place.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So either way, what are the constraints that say not just one came out or not half a million came out, but two came out?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: That's kind of a bit strange. So how did they come out?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Well, they come out because what you're doing inside event is you're relying on the electrical charges down there to power this reaction between hydrogen and CO2 to make yourself grow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And when you leave the vent, you've got to do that yourself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: You've got to power up your own membrane.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And so the question is, well, how do you power up your own membrane?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And the answer is, well, you need to pump. You need to pump ions to give an electrical charge on the membrane.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So what do the pumps look like? Well, the pumps look different in these two groups.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: It's as if they both emerge from a common ancestor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: As soon as you've got that ancestor, things move very quickly and divergently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Why does the DNA replication look different?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Well, it's joined to the membrane. The membranes are different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: The DNA replication is different because it's joined to a different kind of membrane.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So there's interesting, you know, this is detail, you may say, but it's also fundamental because it's about the two big divergent groups of life on Earth that seem to have diverged really early on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: It all started from one organism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And then that organism just start replicating the heck out of itself with some mutation of the DNA.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So like there's some there's a competition through the process of evolution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: They're not like trying to beat each other up. They're just they're just trying to live.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Just replicate us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Yeah. Well, you know, let's not minimize their. Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: They're just trying to chill. They're trying to relax up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And there's no but there's no sense of trying to survive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: They're replicating. I mean, there's no sense in which they're trying to do anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: They're just kind of an outgrowth of the earth, you might say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Of course, the aliens would describe us humans in that same way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: They might be right. This primitive life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: It's just it's just ants that are hairless, mostly hairless, overgrown ants, overgrown ants.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: OK. What do you think about the idea of panspermia, that the theory that life did not originate on Earth and was planted here from outer space or pseudo panspermia,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: which is like the basic ingredients, the magic that you mentioned was planted here from elsewhere in space?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: I don't find them helpful. That's not to say they're wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So pseudo transpermia, the idea that the chemicals, the amino acids, the nucleotides are being delivered from space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Well, we know that happens. It's unequivocal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: They're delivered on meteorites, comets and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So what do they do next? That's to me the question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Well, what do they do is they stock a soup that presumably they land in a pond or in an ocean or wherever they land.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And then you end up with a best possible case scenario as you end up with a soup of nucleotides and amino acids.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And then you have to say, so now what happens?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And the answer is, oh, well, they have to go become alive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So how did they do that? You may as well say then a miracle happened.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: I don't believe in soup.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: I think what we have in event is a continuous conversion, a continuous growth, a continuous reaction, a continuous converting a flow of molecules into more of yourself, you might say, even if it's a small bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So you've got you've got a kind of continuous self-organization and growth from the very beginning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: You never have that in a soup.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Isn't the entire universe and living organisms in the universe, isn't it just soup all the way down?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Isn't it all? No, no.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: I mean, soup almost by definition doesn't have a structure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: But soup is a collection of ingredients that are like randomly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Yeah, but they're not random.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: They're not. I mean, we have chemistry going on here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: We have membranes forming, which are, you know, effective oil water interactions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: OK, so it feels like there's a direction to a process.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: They could direct the process.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: There are directions to processes. Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And if you are if you're starting with CO2 and you've got two reactive fluids being brought together and they react, what are they going to make?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Well, they make carboxylic acids, which include the fatty acids that make up the cell membranes, and they form directly into bilayer membranes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: They form like soap bubbles. It's spontaneous organization caused by the nature of the molecules.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And those things are capable of growing and are capable in effect of being selected even before there are genes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: We have that. So we have a lot of order.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And that order is coming from thermodynamics and the thermodynamics is always about increasing the entropy of the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: But if you have if you have oil and water and they're separating, you're increasing the entropy of the universe, even though you've got some order, which is the soap and the water are not not missable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Now, to come back to your first question about pan-spermia properly, that just pushes the question somewhere else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: That just even if it's true, maybe life did start on Earth by pan-spermia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: But but so what are the principles that govern the emergence of life on any planet?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: We it's an assumption that life started here and it's an assumption that it you know, it started in a hydrothermal vent or it started in a terrestrial geothermal system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: The question is, can we work out a testable sequence of events that would lead from one to the other one and then test it and see if there's any truth in it or not with pan-spermia?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: You can't do any of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: But the fundamental question of pan-spermia is, do we have the machine here on Earth to build life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Is the vents enough?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Is oxygen and hydrogen and whatever the heck else we want and some source of energy and heat, is that enough to build life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Well, that's of course you would say that as a human.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: But there could be aliens right now, chuckling at that idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Maybe you need some special sauce, elsewhere sauce.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Your sense is we have everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: I mean, this is precisely the question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: I like to when I'm talking in schools, I like to start out with the idea of we can make a time machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: We go back four billion years and we go to these environments that people talk about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: We go to a deep sea hydrothermal vent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: We go to a kind of Yellowstone Park type place environment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And we find some slime that looks like we can test it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: It's made of organic molecules.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: It's got a structure which is not obviously cells, but is this a stepping stone on the way to life or not?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: How do we know?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Unless we've got an intellectual framework that says this is a stepping stone and that's not a step.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: We'd never know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: We wouldn't know which environment to go to, what to look for, how to say this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So all we can ever hope for, because we're never going to build that time machine,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: is to have an intellectual framework that can explain step by step, experiment by experiment,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: how we go from a sterile inorganic planet to living cells as we know them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And in that framework, every time you have a choice, it could be this way or it could be that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Or there's lots of possible forks down that road.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Did it have to be that way?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Could it have been the other way?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And would that have given you life with very different properties?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And so if you come up with a, you know, it's a long hypothesis, because as I say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: we're going from really simple prebiotic chemistry all the way through to genes and molecular machines.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: That's a long, long pathway.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And nobody in the field would agree on the order in which these things happened,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: which is not a bad thing because it means that you have to go out and do some experiments

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: and try and demonstrate that it's possible or not possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: It's so freaking amazing that it happened though.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: It feels like there's a direction to the thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Can you try to answer from a framework perspective of what is life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So you said there's some order and yet there's complexity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: So it's not perfectly ordered.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: It's not boring.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: There's still some fun in it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: And it also feels like the processes have a direction through the selection mechanism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: They seem to be building something always better, always improving.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: I mean, maybe it's, I mean, that's a perception.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: That's our romanticization of things are always better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: Things are getting better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: We'd like to believe that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: I mean, you think about the world from the point of view of bacteria and bacteria are the first things to emerge

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Lane: Origin of Life, Evolution, Aliens, Biology, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #318

body.input: from whatever environment they came from.
