body.input: But you don't think unintended consequences can arise even when you're far from optimality,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sergey Levine: Robotics and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #108

body.input: sort of like on the path to it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Sergey Levine: Robotics and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #108

body.input: Oh, no.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sergey Levine: Robotics and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #108

body.input: I think unintended consequences can absolutely arise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sergey Levine: Robotics and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #108

body.input: It's just I think right now the bottleneck for improving reliability, safety, and things

metadata.title: Podcast: Sergey Levine: Robotics and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #108

body.input: like that is more with systems that need to work better, that need to optimize their objective

metadata.title: Podcast: Sergey Levine: Robotics and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #108

body.input: better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sergey Levine: Robotics and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #108

body.input: Do you have thoughts, concerns about existential threats of human level intelligence that if

metadata.title: Podcast: Sergey Levine: Robotics and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #108

body.input: we put on our hat of looking in 10, 20, 100, 500 years from now, do you have concerns about

metadata.title: Podcast: Sergey Levine: Robotics and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #108

body.input: existential threats of AI systems?

metadata.title: Podcast: Sergey Levine: Robotics and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #108

body.input: I think there are absolutely existential threats for AI systems just like there are for any

metadata.title: Podcast: Sergey Levine: Robotics and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #108

body.input: powerful technology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sergey Levine: Robotics and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #108

body.input: But I think that these kinds of problems can take many forms and some of those forms will

metadata.title: Podcast: Sergey Levine: Robotics and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #108

body.input: come down to people with nefarious intent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sergey Levine: Robotics and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #108

body.input: Some of them will come down to AI systems that have some fatal flaws and some of them

metadata.title: Podcast: Sergey Levine: Robotics and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #108

body.input: will of course come down to AI systems that are too capable in some way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sergey Levine: Robotics and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #108

body.input: But among this set of potential concerns, I would actually be much more concerned about

metadata.title: Podcast: Sergey Levine: Robotics and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #108

body.input: the first two right now and principally the one with nefarious humans because just through

metadata.title: Podcast: Sergey Levine: Robotics and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #108

body.input: all of human history actually it's the nefarious humans that have been the problem, not the

metadata.title: Podcast: Sergey Levine: Robotics and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #108

body.input: nefarious machines, than I am about the others.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sergey Levine: Robotics and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #108

body.input: I think that right now the best that I can do to make sure things go well is to build

metadata.title: Podcast: Sergey Levine: Robotics and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #108

metadata.title: Podcast: Sergey Levine: Robotics and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #108

body.input: So in the space of advice, somebody who's interested in getting started in machine learning

metadata.title: Podcast: Sergey Levine: Robotics and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #108

body.input: So something that I think is important to do is to not be afraid to spend time imagining

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: and also, is there good ideas about regulators

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: of that information, about ways to prevent the distortion

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: and degradation of that information?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: Right, so we have silent information regulator genes

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: in our bodies, we have seven of them,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: SIRT1 through seven they're called,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: and we found in mice, one way to slow down

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: the loss of information is to just give more of these,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: to upregulate these genes.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: So we made a mouse that has more of this SIRT1 gene,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: turned it on, and that slowed down the aging of the brain

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: and preserved their information.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: Now, what information am I talking about, you might ask?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: Well, again, you can simplify biology.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: There are two types of information in the cell primarily.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: The one we all read about and know about

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: is the DNA, the genome, and that's base four information,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: A, T, C, G, the four chemicals that make up

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: the various sequences of the genome, billions of letters.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: And that also degrades over time,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: but what's been fascinating is that we find

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: that that information is pretty much intact

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: in old animals and people.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: You can clone a dog, one of my friends in LA

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: just cloned his dog three times.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: So this is doable, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: It means that the genome can be intact,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: but what's the other type of information?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: It's the epigenome, the regulators of

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: the genetic information.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: And physically, that's really just how the DNA is wrapped up

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: or looped out for the cell to access it and read it.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: So it's similar to, and excuse this analogy,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: but it's a good one, a compact disc or a DVD.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: Those pits in the foil are the digital information,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: that's the genome.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: And the epigenome is the reader of that information.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: And in a different cell, you'd read different music,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: different songs, different symphonies.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: And that's what gets laid down when we're in the womb

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: and that makes a skin cell forever a skin cell

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: and not a brain cell tomorrow.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: Thank God, otherwise our brains wouldn't work very well.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: But over time, what we see is that the brain cells

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: start to look more like skin cells

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: and the kidney cells start to look more like liver cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: And they, what we call X-differentiate,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: this is a term that we use in my lab,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: but isn't yet widely used,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: but we needed a term to explain this.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: And those, that process of X-differentiation,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: the loss of the reader of the CD or the DVD,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: we liken that to scratches on the DVD

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: so that the reader cannot fully access the information.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: Now we can slow down the scratches, as I mentioned,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: we can turn on these genes,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: we can even put in molecules into the cell

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: or even eat them and turn on those pathways,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: which my father and I have been trying to do

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: for about a decade to slow things down.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: But the question that I've had is,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: is there a repository of information still in the body?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: Because anyone who knows anything

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: about the loss of information

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: or even has tried to copy a cassette tape

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: or photocopy or Xerox anything,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: knows that over time you lose that information irreparably.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: So I've been looking for a backup copy,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: inspired largely by Claude Shannon's work at MIT as well

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: in the 1940s, his mathematical theory of communication

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: is just brilliant.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: And so I've been looking for what he called the observer,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: which is the backup copy.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: We today might call that the TCPIP protocol

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: of the internet that stores information

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: in case it doesn't make it to your computer,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: it will fill in the gaps.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: And we've been spending about the last five years

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: to try and find if there really is a backup copy

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: in the body to reset the epigenome

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: and polish those scratches away.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: That's incredible.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: So finding the backup,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: so whenever there are too many scratches pile up,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: you can just write a new version.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: Like write, not a new version,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: but go to the backup and restore it.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: Right, that's really all we're talking about.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: It's not that hard once you know the trick.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: And for people that actually remember

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: like DVDs and scratches on them,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: how frustrating it is,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: that's a brilliant metaphor for aging.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: And then the reader is the thing that skips

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: and then it could destroy your experience,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: the richness of the experience

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: that is listening to your favorite song.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: Right, but in biology, it's even worse

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: because you'll lose your memory,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: your kidneys will fail, you'll get diabetes,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: your heart will fail.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: And we call that aging and age-related diseases.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: So most people forget that diseases that we get

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: when we get old are 80 to 90% caused by aging.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: And we've been trying to fix things with band-aids

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: after they occur without even generally talking

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: about the root cause of the problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: Is there the scratches?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: Do those come from,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: are those programmed or are they failures?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: Meaning is it, so if it's by design,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: then there's like a encoded timeline schedule

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: that the body's just on purpose degrading the whole thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: And then there's the just the wear and tear

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: of like the scratches in a disc that happen through time.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: Which one is it that's the source of aging?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: It's more akin to wear and tear.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: There isn't a program.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: Getting back to evolution,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: there's no selection for aging.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: We're not designed to age,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: we just live as long as we need to.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: And then we're at the whim of entropy, basically.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: Second law of thermodynamics, stuff falls apart.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: We live a bit longer than age 40

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: only because there are robust resilient systems,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: but eventually they fail as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: Current limit to a human lifespan

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: where they completely fail is 122.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: But I don't like to think of it as wear and tear

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: because there's two aspects to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: There's a system that's built to keep us alive

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: when we're young, but actually comes back to bite us

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: as we get older.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: And we call this issue antagonistic pleiotropy.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: What's good for you when you're young

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: can cause problems when you're older.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: So we've been looking what is the cause

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: of the main causes of the noise?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: And we've found two of them definitively.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: The first one is broken chromosomes.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: When a chromosome breaks, the cell has to panic

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: because that's either gonna cause a cancer

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: or kill the cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: There's only two outcomes, it's pretty much a problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: And so what the cell does is it reorganizes

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: the epigenome in a massive way.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: What that leads to is think of it as a tennis match

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: or a ping pong game.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: The proteins are the balls

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: and they now leave where they should be,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: which is regulating the genes that make the cell type,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: whatever it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: And they have a dual function,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: they actually go to the break,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: the chromosome will break and fix that.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: And then they come back.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: You might ask, well, why is it set up that way?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: Well, it's a beautiful system.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: It coordinates gene expression,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: the control systems with the repair.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: You want them coordinated.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: Problem is as we get older, this ping pong game,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: some of the balls get lost.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: They don't come back to where they originally started.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: And that's what we think is the main noise for aging.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: And we've also, the other cause of aging that we found

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: is cell stress.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: We damage nerves and they age rapidly.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: So that's the other issue.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: There's probably others.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: Smoking chemicals, for example,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: we know accelerates biological age pretty dramatically.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: But the question is, can you slow that down

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: or can you reset them to get those ping pong balls

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: to go back to where they originally started in the game?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Sinclair: Extending the Human Lifespan Beyond 100 Years | Lex Fridman Podcast #189

body.input: And we think we found a way to do that.

body.input: Why do humans need sleep?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: Let's go with the big first question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: Okay, well, the answer I'll start with

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: is the one that I always default to

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: when there's a why question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: Which is I wasn't consulted at the design phase.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: So, I wriggle my way out of giving a absolute answer, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: But there's one mechanism that's very clear,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: that's super important,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: which is that the longer we are awake,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: the more adenosine accumulates in our brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: And adenosine binds to adenosine receptors,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: no surprise there,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: and it creates the feeling of sleepiness,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: independent of time of day or night.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: So, there are two mechanisms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: One is we get sleepy as adenosine accumulates.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: The longer we've been awake,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: the more adenosine has accumulated in our system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: But how sleepy we get for a given amount of adenosine

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: depends on where we are in this so-called circadian cycle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: And the circadian cycle is just this very,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: very well-conserved oscillation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: It's a temperature oscillation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: where you go from a low point,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: typically if you're awake during the day

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: and you're asleep at night,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: your lowest temperature point will be like 3 a.m., 4 a.m.,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: and then your temperature will start to creep up

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: as you wake up in the morning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: and then it'll peak in the late afternoon,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: and then it'll start to drop again toward the evening,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: and then you get sleepy again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: That oscillation in temperature takes 24 hours.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: Plus or minus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: Yeah, plus or minus an hour.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: And I don't, even though I wasn't consulted

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: at the design phase,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: I do not think it's a coincidence

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: that it's aligned to the 24-hour spin of the Earth

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: on its axis,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: and the fact that we tend to be bathed in sunlight

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: for a portion of that spin,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: and in darkness for the other portion of that spin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: So there are two mechanisms,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: the adenosine accumulation and the circadian time point

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: that we happen to be at.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: And those converge to create a sense of sleepiness,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: of wakefulness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: The simple way to reveal these two mechanisms,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: to uncouple them, is stay up for 24 hours,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: and you will find that even though you've been,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: let's say you stay up midnight, 2 a.m., 3 a.m.,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: provided you're on a regular schedule,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: like that I follow, not like the kind that you follow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: Yep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: I will get very sleepy around 3, 4 a.m.,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: but then around 5 or 6 or 7 a.m.,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: which is my normal wakeup time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: I'll start to feel more alert,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: even though adenosine has been accumulating further.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: So adenosine is higher for me the longer I stay up,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: and yet I feel more alert than I did a few hours ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: And that's because these are two interacting forces.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: So adenosine makes you sleepy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: and then just how sleepy or how awake you feel

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: also depends on where you are

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: in this temperature oscillation that takes 24 hours.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: Okay, so that's fascinating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: So there's a bunch of oscillations going on,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: and then they kind of, through the evolutionary process,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: have evolved to all be aligned somewhat,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: and they interplay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: So you said your body temperature goes up and down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: There's chemicals in your brain that oscillate,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: and then there's the actual oscillation

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: of the sun in the sky.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: So all of that together

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: has some impact on each other,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: and somehow that all results in us

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: Right, and we can get right into the meat of this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: is the effector of the circadian clock.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: that's dictated by genes like clock, per, B mal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: This is one of the great successes of biology.

body.input: They give a Nobel Prize to the Repard,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Sleep, Dreams, Creativity, Fasting, and Neuroplasticity | Lex Fridman Podcast #164

body.input: I don't know if Repard got it, forgive me,

body.input: but sorry if you got it, Steve, congratulations if you didn't,

body.input: Slaves produce a surplus which the master gets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Serfs produce a surplus which the lord gets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Employees produce a surplus which the employer gets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: It's very simple. These are exploitative class structures because

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: one class produces a surplus appropriated, distributed

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: by another group of people, not the ones who produced it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: which creates hostility, enmity, envy, anger, resentment, and all of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: problems you can lump under the heading class struggle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: The following is a conversation with Richard Wolff,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: one of the top Marxist economists and philosophers in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: This is a heavy topic in general and for me personally given my

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: family history in the Soviet Union, in Russia, and in Ukraine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Today the words Marxism, Socialism, and Communism

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: are used to attack and to divide much more than to understand and to learn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: With this podcast I seek the latter. I believe we need to study the ideas of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Karl Marx as well as their various implementations

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: throughout the 20th and the 21st centuries.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And in general we need to both steel man and to consider seriously

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the ideas we demonize and to challenge the ideas we dogmatically accept as true,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: even when doing so is unpleasant and at times dangerous.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: This is the Lex Friedman Podcast. To support it please check out our sponsors

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: in the description. And now dear friends, here's Richard Wolff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Let's start with a basic question but maybe not so basic after all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: What is Marxism? What are the defining characteristics of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Marxism as an economic and political theory and ideology?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Well the simplest way to begin a definition would be to say it's the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: tradition that takes its founding inspiration from the works of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Karl Marx. But because these ideas that he put forward

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: spread as fast as they did and as globally as they did,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: literally it's 140 years since Marx died, and in that time his ideas

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: have become major types of thinking in every country on the earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: If you know much about the great ideas of human history,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: that's an extraordinary spread in an extraordinarily short period of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: historical time. And what that has meant, that speed of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: spread and that geographic diversity, is that the Marxian ideas interacted

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: with very different cultural histories, religious

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: histories, and economic conditions. So the end result was that the ideas

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: were interpreted differently in different places at

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: different times. And therefore Marxism as a kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: first flush definition is the totality of all of these very

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: different ways of coming to terms with it. For the first roughly 40-50 years,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Marxism was a tradition of thinking critically about capitalism. Marx himself,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: that's all he really did, he never wrote a book about communism, he never wrote a

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: book really about socialism either. His

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: comments were occasional, fragmentary, dispersed. What he was

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: really interested in was a critical analysis of capitalism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And that's what Marxism was, more or less, in its first 40 or 50 years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: The only qualification of what I just said

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: was something that happened in Paris for a few weeks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: In 1871 there was a collapse of the French government,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: consequent upon losing a war to Bismarck's Germany,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and in the result was something called the Paris Commune.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: The working class of Paris rose up, basically took over the function of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: running the Parisian economy and the Parisian

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: society. And Marx's people, people influenced by

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Marx, were very active in that commune, in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: leadership of the commune. And Marx wasn't that far away, he was in

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: London, these things were happening in Paris,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: you know, that's an easy transport even then. And for a

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: short time, very short, Marxism had a different

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: quality. In addition to being a critique of capitalism,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: it became a theory of how to organize society differently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Before that had only been implicit, now it became

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: explicit. What is the leadership of the Paris Commune going to do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And why? And in what order? In other words, governing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: organizing a society. But since it only lasted a few weeks, the French army

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: regrouped, and under the leadership of people who

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: were very opposed to Marx, they marched back into Paris, took

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: over, killed a large number of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: communards, as they were called, and deported them to

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: islands in the Pacific that were part of the French Empire at the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: The really big change happens in Russia in 1917.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Now you have a group of Marxists, Lenin, Trotsky, all the rest, who

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: are in this bizarre position to seize a moment. Once again, a war,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: like in France, disorganizes the government,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: throws the government into a very bad reputation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: because it is the government that loses World War I,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: has to withdraw, as you know, Brest-Litovsk and all of that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and the government collapses, and the army revolts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And in that situation, a very small political party, Russian social

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: democratic workers party,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: splits under the pressures of all of this

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: into the Bolshevik and Menshevik divisions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Lenin, Trotsky, and the others are in the Bolshevik division.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And to make a long story short, he's in exile.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Lenin's position makes him, gets him deported, because he says

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Russian workers should not be killing German workers. I mean, this is a war of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: capitalists who are dividing the world up into colonies, and

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Russian working people should not kill and should not die

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: for such a thing. As you can expect, they arrest him and they throw him out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Interestingly, in the United States, the comparable leader

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: at that time of the Socialist Party here,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: as you know, there was no Communist Party at this point, that comes later,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the head of the Socialist Party, a very important American figure

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: named Eugene Victor Debs, makes exactly the same argument to the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Americans should not fight in the war. He's in the, he has nothing to do with

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Lenin, I don't even know if they knew of each other, but he does it on

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: his own. He gets arrested and put in jail here in the United States. By the way, he

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: runs for president from jail and does very well, really very

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: well, remarkable. And he's the inspiration for Bernie

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Sanders, if you see the link, although he had much more courage

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: politically than Bernie has. That's really interesting. I'd love to return to

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: that link maybe later. History rhymes. Yes, the complicated

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: story. Anyway, the importance in terms of Marxism is that now

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: this seizure of power by a group of Marxists, that is a group of people

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: inspired by Marx, developing what you might call a

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Russian, even though there were differences among the Russians too, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: a Russian interpretation. This now has to be transformed from a critique

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: of capitalism into a plan at least, what are you going to

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: do in the Soviet Union? And a lot of this was then trial and

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: error. Marx never laid any of this out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Probably wouldn't have been all that relevant if he had because it was 50

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: years earlier in another country, etc. So what begins to happen, and you can see

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: how this happens then more later in China and Cuba and Vietnam and Korea

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and so on, is that you have kind of a bifurcation. Much of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Marxism remains chiefly the critique of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: capitalism. But another part of it becomes

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: a set, and they differ from one to the other, a set

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: of notions of what an alternative post-capitalist society ought to look

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: like, how it ought to work. And there's lots of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: disagreement about it, lots of confusion. And I would say

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: that that's still where it is. That you have a tradition now

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: that has these two major wings, critique of capitalism, notion of the alternative,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and then a variety of each of those, and that would be the framework in

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: which I would answer, that's what Marxism is about. It's

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: basic idea, if you had to have one, is that human society can do better

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: than capitalism, and it ought to try. And then we can

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: start to talk about what we mean by capitalism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Fine. So we'll look at the critique of capitalism on one side,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: but maybe stepping back, what do you think Marx would say

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: if he just looked at the different implementations

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: of the ideas of Marxism throughout the 20th century,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: where his ideas that were implicit were made explicit?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Would he shake his head? Would he enjoy some of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: parts of the implementations? Like, how do you think he would analyze it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Well, he had a great sense of humor. I don't know if he had a chance to take a

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: look at his writing, but he had an extraordinary sense of humor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: My guess is he would deploy his humor in answering this question too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: He would say some of them are inspiring, some of the interpretations of his work,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and he's very pleased with those. Others are horrifying,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and he wishes somehow he could erase the connection between those things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and the lineage they claim from him, which he would.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: There's a German word—I don't know if you speak the other languages—

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: there's a wonderful German word called verzichte,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and it's stronger than the word refuse. It's if you want to refuse something,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: but with real strong emphasis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Vezichte darauf is a German way of saying,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: I don't want anything to do with that. And he would talk then,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: you know, in philosophical terms, because remember he was a student of philosophy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: He wrote his doctoral thesis on ancient Greek philosophy and all the rest.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: He would wax philosophical and say, you know, that the ideas you put out are a

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: little bit like having a child. You have a lot of influence, but the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: child is his own or her own person and will find his or her own way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And these ideas, once they're out there, go their own way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And as you said, there's a particular way that this idea spread,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the speed at which it spread throughout the world made it even less

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: able to be sort of stabilized and connected back to the origins of where the idea came from.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: The only people who ever really tried that were the Russians after the revolution,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: because they occupied a position for a while, not very long,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: but they occupied a position for a while in which, I mean, it was exalted, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: There had been all these people criticizing capitalism for a long time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: even the Marxists ever since mid-century. And these were the first guys who pulled it off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: They made it. And so there was a kind of presumption around the world,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: their interpretation must be kind of the right one, because look, they did it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And so for a while, they could enunciate their interpretation. And it came to be widely grasped

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: as something which, by the way, gets called in the literature, official Marxism, the very idea

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: that you would put that adjective in front of Marxism, or Soviet Marxism, or Russian Marxism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: There were these words where the adjective was meant to somehow say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: kind of, this is the canon. You can depart from it, but this is the canon.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Before the Russian Revolution, there was no such thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And by the 1960s, it was already, it was gone. But for a short time, 30, 40 years, it was a kind of,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and the irony is, particularly here in the United States, where the taboo against Marxism kicks in

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: right after World War II, is so total in this country that I, for example, through most of my

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: adult life, have had to spend a ridiculous amount of my time simply explaining to American audiences

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: that the Marxism they take as canonical is that old Soviet Marxism, which wasn't the canon before

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: 1917 and hasn't been since at least the 1960s, but they don't know. It's not that they're stupid,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and it's not that they're ignorant. It's that, well, the ignorance may be, but I mean,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: it's not a mental problem. It's the taboo, shut it down. And so all of the reopening

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: that in a way recaptures what went before and develops it in new direction, they just don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Nevertheless, it's a serious attempt at making the implicit ideas explicit. The Russians,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the Soviets at the beginning of the 20th century made a serious attempt at saying, okay,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: beyond the critique of capitalism, how do we actually build a system like this? And so in that

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: sense, not at a high level, but at a detailed level, it's interesting to look at those particular

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295
