body.input: schools. Maybe- Right, because for example, let me just take your point one step further.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: You really cannot understand the Cuban Revolution, the Chinese Revolution,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the Chinese Revolution, Vietnamese and the others, because each of them is a kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: response, let's call it, to the way the Soviets did it. Are you going to do it that way? Well,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: yes and no is the answer. This we will do that way, but that we're not going to do. And the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: differences are huge, but you could find a thread, I can do that for you if you want,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: in which all of them are in a way reacting. To the originals. Yes, very much so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Like maybe most of rock music is reacting to the Beatles and the Stones.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: There's something like that. Can you speak to the unique elements of the various schools

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: of that Soviet Marxism? So we've got Leninism, Trotskyism, Stalinism, maybe even let's expand

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: out to Maoism. So maybe I could speak to sort of Leninism and then please tell me if I'm saying

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: dumb things. I think for Lenin, there was an idea that there could be a small sort of Vanguard party,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: like a small controlling entity that's like wise and is able to do the central planning decisions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Then for Stalinism, one interesting, so Stalin's implementation of all of this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: one interesting characteristic is to move away from the international aspect of the ideal of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Marxism to make it all about nation, nationalism, the strength of nation. And then so Maoism is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: it's different in that it's focused on agriculture, on rural. And then Trotskyism,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: I don't know, except that it's anti-Stalin. I mean, I don't even know if there's unique

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: sort of philosophical elements there. Anyway, can you maybe from those or something else speak

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: to different unique elements that are interesting to think about implementation of Marxism in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: real world? Probably the best way to get into this is to describe something that happened

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: in Marxism that then shapes the answer to your question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: In the early days of Marx's writings, and you know, his life spans the 19th century. He's born in

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: 1818, dies in 1883. So literally, he lives the 19th century. And you might, I mean, to make things simple,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: you might look at the first half of the first two-thirds of his life as overwhelmingly

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: gathering together the precursors to his own work. Marx was unusually scholarly in the sense that

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: partly because he didn't work a regular job and partly because he was an exile in London,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: most of his adult life, he worked in the library. I mean, he had a lot of time. He got subsidized a

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: little bit by Engels, whose family were manufacturers. And you might say the first half to two-thirds of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: his life are about the critique of capitalism. And that was what, in a broad sense, the audience

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: for his work, Western Europe more or less, was interested in. That's what they wanted. And he

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: gave that to them. He wasn't the only one, but he was very, very effective at it. By the last

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: third of his life, he and the other producers of an anti-capitalist movement, people like the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Chartists in England, that's a whole other movement, the anarchists of various kinds,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: like Proudhon in France or Kropotkin or Bakunin in Russia, and so on. You pull all these together,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and there was a shift in what the audience—let's call it a mixture of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: militant working-class people on the one hand and critical or radical intelligentsia on the other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: They now wanted a different question. They were persuaded by the analysis. They were agreeable

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: that capitalism was a phase they would like to do better than. And the question became,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: how do we do this? Not anymore, should we, why should we, could we maybe fix capitalism? No,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: they had gotten to the point the system has to be fundamentally changed. But they didn't go—you

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: might imagine—they didn't go and say, well, what will that new system look like? They didn't go

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: that way. What they did was ask the question, how could we get beyond capitalism? It seems so powerful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: It seems to have captured people's minds, people's daily lives, and so on. And the focus of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: conversation became—this was already by the last third of the 19th century—the question of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: agency, the mechanism whereby we would get beyond. And again, make a long story short,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the conversation focused on seizing the government. See, before that, it wasn't that the government

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: was not of major interest. If you read Marx's Capital, the great work of his maturity, three

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: volumes, there's almost nothing in the state. He mentions it, but he's interested in the details

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: of how capitalism works, factory by factory, store by store, office. What's the structure?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: The government's secondary for him. But there's also humans within that capitalist system of,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: there's the working class. Right. It's about the class struggle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: That's what he's interested in. Think of it almost mechanically like the workplace.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: In the workplace, there are some people who do this and other people who do that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and they accept this division of authority, and they accept this division of what's going on here,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: particularly because he believed that the core economic objective of capitalism was to maximize

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: something called profit, which his analysis located right there in the workings of the enterprise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: The government was not the key factor here. And he was looking at ideas of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: value. How much value does the labor of the individual workers provide? And that means

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: how do we reward the workers in an ethical way? So those are the questions of-

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: We'll get to that. But the government was not part of that picture.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: So it's very significant that towards the end of the 19th century, Marx is still alive when this

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: begins, but it really gets going after he dies, is this debate among Marxists about the role of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: state. They all agree, nearly all of them agree that you have to get the state. The working class

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: has to get the state because they see the state as the ultimate guarantor of capitalism. When things

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: get really out of hand, the capitalist calls the police, or he calls the army, or both of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And so the government is, in a sense, this key institution captured in Marxist language

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: by the bourgeoisie, by the other side, the capitalists, and yet vulnerable because of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: suffrage. If suffrage is universal or nearly so, if everybody gets a vote, which in a way capitalism

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: brings to bear, part of its rejection of feudalism in the French American revolution is to create

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: a place where elected represented. So the government being subject to suffrage creates the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: notion, aha, here's how we're going to, we have to seize the state. And then that gets agreed upon,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: but there's a big split as to how to do it. One side says you go with the election, you mobilize

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the voter. That gets to be called reformism within Marxism. And the other side is revolution. Don't

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: do that. This system, if I may quote Bernie again, is rigged. You can't get there. They've long ago

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: learned how to manipulate parliaments. They buy the politicians and all that. And therefore,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: revolution is going to be the way to do it. Revolution gets a very big boost because the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Russians, they did it that way. They didn't do, I mean, they fought in the Duma, in the parliament,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: but they didn't. And this focus on the state, I would argue, goes way beyond what the debaters

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: at the time, and if you're interested in the great names, there was a great theorist of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: role of the state in a reformist strategy to get power in Germany named Edward Bernstein.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Very important. His opponents in Germany were Karl Kautsky and Rosa Luxemburg, two other

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: huge figures in Marxism at the time. And they wrote the articles that everybody reads, but it

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: was a much broader debate. By the way, that debate still goes on. Reformism versus revolution?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And in terms, not all that different. I mean, it's adjusted to history, but in terms,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: they're all different. Can you comment on where you lean in terms of the mechanism of progress,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: reformation versus- I'd rather show you the historical story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Sure. Over and over and over again, in most cases, the reformists have always won,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: because revolution is frightening, is scary, is dangerous. And so most of the time, when you get

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: to the point where it's even a relevant discussion, not an abstract thing for conferences, but a real

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: strategic issue, the reformists have won. I mean, and I'll give you an example from the United

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: States. In the Great Depression of the 1930s, you had an extraordinary shift to the left in

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the United States, the greatest shift to the left in the country's history, before or since.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Nothing like it. Suddenly, you created a vast left wing composed of the labor movement,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: which went crazy in the 1930s. We organized more people into unions in the 1930s than at any time

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: before or any time since. It is the explosion. And at the same time, the explosion of two socialist

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: parties and the communist party that became very powerful, and they all worked together, creating

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: a very powerful leftist presence in this country. They debated in a strategically real way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: reform or revolution. The reformers were the union people, by and large, and the communists

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: were the revolutionaries, by and large, because they were affiliated with the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Communist International, with Russia, and all of that. And in between, you might say, the two

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: socialist parties, one that was Trotskyist in inspiration, and the other one more moderate

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Western European kind of socialism. And they had this intense debate. And they ended up,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the reformists won that debate. There was no revolution in the 1930s here, but there was

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: a reform that achieved unspeakably great successes, which is why it was as strong and remains as

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: strong as it does, because it achieved in a few years in the 1930s, starting around 1932-3,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: social security in this country. We had never had that before. It's the same one we have now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Unemployment insurance never existed before, that you have till today. Minimum wage for the first

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: time, you still have that today, and a federal program of employment that hired 15 million people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: I mean, these were unspeakable gifts, if you like, to the working class.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: So that's the 30s and the 40s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: 30s, not much in the 40s anymore, but in the 30s. And here's the best part. It was paid for by taxes

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: on corporations and the rich. So when people today say, well, you can tax the corporate,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: tax the corporate, the joke is I have to teach American history to Americans,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: because it has been erased from consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: We'll return to that. But first, let's take a stroll back to the beginning of the 20th

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: century with the Russians.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Right, with the Russians. So their interpretation goes like this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Everybody was right. The state is crucial. We were right. We were the revolutionaries.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: We seized the state here in Russia. Now we have the state. And socialism

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: is when the working class captures the state, either by reform or revolution,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and then uses its power over the state to make the transition from capitalism

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: to the better thing we're going toward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And again, make a long story short, in the interest of time, what happens, which is not unusual in

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: human history, is that the means becomes the end. In other words, Lenin, who's crystal clear,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: before he died—you know, he doesn't live very long. He died in 23. So he's only in power from 17

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: to 22. By that time, he has his brain trouble.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Not 1923, by the way. Not at age 23.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Yeah, yeah, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: People who are listening.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: 1923. Yeah, he's only there for four or five years. He's very clear. He even says—I've done work

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: on that. I've published, so I know this stuff. He says in a famous speech, let's not fool ourselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: We have captured the state, but we don't have socialism. We have to create that. We have to

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: move towards that. With Stalin, you know, Lenin dies, and there's a fight between Stalin and

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Trotsky. Trotsky loses the fight. He's exiled. He goes to Mexico. Stalin is now alone in power,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: does all the things he's famous or infamous for. And by the end of the 20s, Stalin makes a decision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: I mean, not that he makes it alone, but things have evolved in Russia so that they do the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: following. They declare that they are socialism. In other words, socialism becomes when you capture

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the state, not when the state capture has enabled you to do x, y, z, other things. No, no. The state

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: itself, once you have it, is socialism. So when a socialist captures the state,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: that's socialism. Exactly. That's exactly right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And I feel like that's definitionally confusing. Well, it shouldn't be, because I'm going to give

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: you an example. If you go to many parts of the United States today and you ask people

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: what socialism, they'll look you right in the face and they'll say the post office.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: When I first heard this as a young man, you know what? The post office. It took me a while to

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: understand the post office, Amtrak, the Tennessee... All the examples in the United States where the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: government runs something. This is socialism. See, capitalism is if the government doesn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: run it. If a private individual who's not a government official runs it, well, then it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: capitalism. If the government takes it, then it's socialism. So what is wrong with that reasoning?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: So the idea, I think... There's nothing wrong with it's a way of looking at the world. It's just got

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: nothing to do with Marx. Well, there's Marx, there's Marxism. Let's try to pull this apart.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: So what role does central planning have in Marxism? So Marxism is concerned with this class struggle,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: with respecting the working class. What is the connection between that struggle and central

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: planning that is often... Central planning is often associated with Marxism. So a centralized power

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: doing... Russia did that. So that has to do with a very specific set of implementations initiated by

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the Soviet Union. It has nothing to do with Marx. How else can you do... I don't think you can find

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: anywhere in Marx's writing anything about central planning or any other kind of planning. Again,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: fundamentally then, Marx's work has to do with factories, with workers, with the bourgeoisie,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and the exploitation of the working class. You still have to take that leap. What is beyond

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: capitalism? Right. So maybe we should turn to that, focus on that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Okay. Yes. Okay, we've already looked historically at several attempts to go beyond capitalism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: How else can we go beyond capitalism? Right. Let me push a little further.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: They didn't succeed, in my judgment, as a Marxist. And I'm now going to tell you why they didn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: succeed, because they didn't understand as well as they could have or should have,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: what Marxist was trying to do. I think I would have been like them if I had lived at their time

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: under their circumcision. This is not a critique of them, but it's a different way of understanding

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: what's going on. All right. So, I'll give you an example. Most of my adult life, I have taught

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Marxian economics. I'm a professor of economics. I've been that all my life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: I'm a graduate of American universities. As it happens, I'm a graduate of what in this country

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: passes for its best universities. Another conversation you and I can have. So, I went

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: to Harvard, then I went to Stanford, and I finished at Yale. I'm like a poster boy

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: for elite education. They tried very hard. By the way, I spent 10 years of my life in the Ivy League,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: 20 semesters, one after the other, no break. In those 20 semesters, 19 of them never mentioned

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: a word about Marxism. That is, no critique of capitalism was offered to me, ever, with one

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: except one professor in Stanford in the one semester I studied with him. He gave me plenty

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: to read, but nobody else. So, that's really interesting. You've mentioned that in the past,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and that's very true, which makes you a very interesting figure to hold your ground

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: intellectually through this idea space where just people don't really even talk about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: No.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Perhaps we can discuss historically why that is, but nevertheless, that's the case. So,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Marxian economics, did Karl Marx come up in conversation as a kind of...

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Dismissalful. The best example, yeah, he came up only as an object of dismissal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: For example, the major textbook in economics that I was taught with, and that was for many years

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the canonical book, it isn't quite anymore, was a book authored by a professor of economics at MIT

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: named Paul Samuelson. A whole generation or two were trained on his textbook. If you open the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: cover of his textbook, he has a tree, and the tree is Adam Smith and David Ricardo at the root,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and then the different branches of it. He's trying to give you an idea as a student of how the thing

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: developed. And it's a tree, and everybody on it is a bourgeois. And then there's this one little

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: branch that goes off like this and sort of starts heading back down. That's Karl Marx. In other

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: words, he had to have it complete because he's not a complete faker. But beyond that, no, there was

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: no... Nothing in the book gives you two paragraphs of an approach. But that's Cold War. I mean,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: that's really neither here nor there. That's the craziness. Yeah, that's the Cold War in this

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: country. My professors were afraid. Anyway, let me get to the core of it, what I think will help.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Marx was interested in the relationship of people in the process of production. He's interested in

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the factory, the office, the store. What goes on? And by that he means, what are the relationships

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: among the people that come together in a workplace? And what he analyzes is that there is something

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: going on there that has not been adequately understood and that has not been adequately

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: addressed as an object needing transformation. What does he mean? The answer is exploitation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: which he defines mathematically in the following way. Whenever in a society, any society, you

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: organize people, adults, not the children, not the sick, but healthy adults, in the following way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: a big block of them, a clear majority, work. That is, they use their brains and their muscles

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: to transform nature. A tree into a chair, a sheep into a woolen sweater, whatever. In every human

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: community, Marx argues, there are the people who do that work, but they always produce more chairs,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: more sweaters, more hamburgers than they themselves consume, whatever their standard of living.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Doesn't have to be low, could be medium, could be high, but they always produce more than they

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: themselves consume. That more, by the way, Marx, when he writes this, uses the German term,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: mehr, which is the English equivalent of more. It's the more. That more got badly translated

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: into the word surplus. Shouldn't have been, but it was. By the way, by German and English people

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: doing the translations. What's the difference between more and surplus? Is there a nuance?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Yeah, because surplus has a notion of its discretionary, it's sort of extra, it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: not making a judgment that it's extra. It's a simple math equation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Yes, very simple. One minus the other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Yes. X minus Y. X is the total output. Y is the consumption by the producer. Therefore,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: X minus Y equals S, the surplus. Exactly. Now, Marx argues, the minute you understand this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: you will ask the following question. Who gets the surplus? Who gets this extra stuff that is made,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: but not consumed by those who made it? And Marx's answer is, therein lies one of the great shapers

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: of any society. How is that organized? For example, who gets it? What are they asked,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: if anything, to do with it in exchange for getting it? What's their social role? For example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: here we go now. If you get this and you get the core of it anyway, and I don't charge much,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the workers themselves could get it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Or less than lawyers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Right, that's right. The workers themselves could get it. That's the closest Marx comes

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: to a definition of communism. Communism would be if the workers who produce the surplus

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: together decide what to do with it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: So this has to do not just with who gets it, but more importantly, who gets to decide who gets it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Well, who gets it and who gets to decide what to do with it. Because you can't decide it if you

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: don't have disposition over it. So that's the logic of the word sequence. It's produced. Marx

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: uses the word appropriated. In other words, whose property, who gets to decide, if you like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: what happens, all that property ever meant is who gets to decide and who's excluded.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: That's a clean definition of communism for him.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Right. By the way, it's not just clean. The only thing that's clean is the definition of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: it. It's not just clean. It's the only one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: So what's, can we just linger on the definition of exploitation in that context?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Easy. It becomes very easy. Exploitation exists if and when the surplus that's produced

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: is taken and distributed by people other than those who produced it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Slaves produce a surplus which the master gets. Serfs produce a surplus which the lord gets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Employees produce a surplus which the employer gets. It's very simple.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: These are exploitative class structures because one class produces a surplus appropriated,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: distributed by another group of people, not the ones who produced it, which creates hostility,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: enmity, envy, anger, resentment, and all of the problems you can lump under the heading

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: class struggle. I use a metaphor, simple metaphorical story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: You have two children, let's assume, and you take them to Central Park a few blocks from here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: It's a nice day and the children are playing and in comes one of those men with an ice cream truck

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: comes by. Ding-a-ling-a-ling-a-ling, your children see the ice cream, daddy, get me an ice cream.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: So you walk over, you take some money, and you get two ice cream cones and you give them to one of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the children. The other one begins to scream and yell and how? Obviously. What's the issue?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And you realize you've just made a terrible mistake. So you order the one you gave the two

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: ice cream cones to, give one of those to your sister or your brother or whatever it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And that's how you solve the problem until a psychologist comes along and says,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: you know, you didn't fix it by what you just did. You should never have done that in the first place.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: My response, so you understand, all of the efforts to deal with inequality in economic,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: political, cultural, these are all giving the ice cream cone back to the kid. You should never do

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: this in the first place. The reallocation of resources creates bitterness in the populace.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Look at our... This country is tearing itself apart now in a way that I have never seen in my

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: life and I've lived here all my life and I've worked here all my life. It's tearing itself

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: apart and it's tearing itself apart basically over the re-division, the redistribution of wealth,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: having so badly distributed in the first... But that's all in marks. And notice as I explained to

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: you what is going on in this tension-filled production scene in the office of factory to

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: store, I don't have to say a word about the government. I'm not interested in the government.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: The government's really a very secondary matter to this core question. And here comes the big point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: If you make a revolution and all you do is remove the private exploiter and substitute a government

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: official without changing the relationship, you can call yourself a Marxist all day long,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: but you're not getting the point of the Marxism. The point was not who the exploiter is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: but the exploitation per se. You've got to change the organization of the workplace so there isn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: a group that makes all the decisions and gets the surplus vis-a-vis another one that produces it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: If you do that, you will destroy the whole project. Not only will you not achieve what you set out to

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: get, but you'll so misunderstand it that the Germans again have a phrase, it's geht schief,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: it goes crooked. It doesn't go right. The project gets off the rails because it can't understand

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: either what its objective should have been and therefore it doesn't understand how and why it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: missing its objective. It just knows that this is not what it had hoped for.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: I mean, there's a lot of fascinating questions here. So one is, to what degree, so this human

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: nature, to what degree does communism, a lack of exploitation of the working class naturally emerge

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: if you leave two people together in a room and come back a year later, if you leave five people

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: together in a room, if you leave a hundred people and a thousand people, it seems that humans form

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: hierarchies naturally. So the clever, the charismatic, the sexy, the muscular, the powerful,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: however you define that, start becoming a leader and start to do maybe exploitation in a non-negative

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: sense, a more generic sense, starts to become an employer, not in a capitalist sense, but just as a

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: human. Here, you go do this and in exchange I will give you this. Just becomes the leadership role.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: So the question is, yes, okay, it would be nice, the idea sort of of communism would be nice to

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: not steal from the world. It's nice in theory, but it doesn't work in practice

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: because of human nature. Because of human nature. Thank you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: So what can we say about leveraging human nature to achieve some of these ends?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: There are so many ways of responding, in no particular order. Here are some of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: The history of the human race, as best I can tell, is a history in which a succession of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: social forms, forms of society, arise. And as they do, they rule out some kinds of human behavior

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: on the grounds that they are socially disruptive and unacceptable. The argument isn't really then,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: is there a need or an instinct? Is there some human nature that makes people want to do this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Well, whatever that is, this has to be repressed or else we don't have a society.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And Freud helps us to understand that that repression is going on all the time and it

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: has consequences. It's not a finished project. You repress it. It's gone. It doesn't work like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: So for example, when you get a bunch of people together at some point, they may develop

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: animosities towards one another that lead them to want the other person or persons to disappear,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: to be dead, to be gone. But we don't permit you to do that. We just don't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Every economic system that has ever existed has included people who defend it on the grounds that

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: it is the only system consistent with human nature and that every effort to go beyond it

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: has to fail because it contradicts human nature. I can show you endless documents of every tribal

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: society I've ever studied, every anthropological community that has ever been studied, slavery,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: wherever it's existed. I can show you endless documents in which the defenders of those systems,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: not all of them, of course, but many defenders used that argument to naturalize a system is a

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: way to hold on to it, to prevent it from going, to counter the argument that every system is born,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: every system evolves, and then every system dies. And therefore, capitalism, since it was born,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: since it's been developing, we all know what the next stage of capitalism is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: What can infer? If what you're saying-

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: The burden is on the people who think it isn't going to die.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: So it doesn't mean they're wrong, but what you're saying is if we look at history,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: you're deeply suspicious of the argument this is going against human nature because we keep using

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: that for basically everything including toxic relationship, toxic systems, destructive systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: That said, let me just ask a million different questions. So one, what about the argument

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: that the employer, the capitalist takes on risk versus the employee who's just there doing the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: labor? The capitalist is actually putting up a lot of risk. Are they not in aggregating this

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: organization and taking this giant effort, hiring a lot of people? Aren't they taking on risk that

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: this is going to be a giant failure? So first of all, there's risk. Almost in everything

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: you undertake, any project that begins now and ends in the future takes a risk that between now

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and that future, something's going to happen that makes it not work out. I mean, I got into a cab

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: before I came here today in order to do this with you. I took a risk. The cab could have been in an

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: accident. The lightning could have hit us. A bear could have eaten my left foot. Who the hell knows?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Shouldn't I reward you for the risk you took? No, hold it a second. Let's do this step by step.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: So everybody's taking a risk. I always found it wonderful. You talk about risk and then you imagine

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: it's only some of us who take a risk. Let's go with the worker and with the capitalist. That worker,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: he moved his family from Michigan to Pennsylvania to take that job. He made a decision to have

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: children. They are teenagers. They're now in school at a time when their friendships are crucial to

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: their development. You're going to yank them out of the school because his job is gone. He took an

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: enormous risk to do that job every day, to forestall all the other things he could have done. He was

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: taking a risk that this job would be here tomorrow, next month, next year. He bought a house, which

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Americans only do with mortgages, which means he's now stuck. He has to make a monthly payment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: If you make a mistake, you capitalist, he's the one who's going to... You're a capitalist. You've

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: got a lot of money. Otherwise, you wouldn't be in that position. You've got a cushion. He doesn't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: If you investigate, you'll see that in every business I've ever been in. I've been involved

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: in a lot of them. So you think it's possible to actually measure risk or is your basic argument

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: is there's risk involved in a lot of both the working class and the bourgeoisie, the capitalist,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and it's very difficult. That's right. The worker would never come and say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: because he's been taught right, I want this payment, a wage, for the work I do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: I want this page, this payment, for the risk I take. Well, there's some level of communication

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: like that. You have acknowledgement of dangerous jobs, but that's probably built into the salary,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: all those kinds of things. But you're not incorporating the full spectrum of risk.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: You don't believe that. This country is now being literally transformed from below by an army of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: workers who work at Amazon, fast food joints. You know what their complaint is? It's killing us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: We get paid shit and it's killing us. There is no relationship except in the minds of the defenders

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: of capitalism between the ugliness, the difficulty, the danger of labor on the one hand and the wage.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Let me give you just a couple of examples because this is my job. This is my life, what I do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: The median income of a childcare worker in the United States right now as we speak

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: is $11.22 an hour, median. So 50% make less, 50% make more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: The median income for a car park attendant is several dollars per hour higher than that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: What does the car park attendant do? He stares at your car for many hours to make sure that nobody

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: comes and grabs it. Maybe he parks it and he moves it around to get it in and out. By any measure that

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: I know of that makes any rational sense, being in charge of toddlers, two, three, four-year-olds

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: who are at the key moment of mental formation the first five years, to give that a lower salary

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: than you give the guy who watches your car. Come on, I know how to explain it. Gender explained,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: all kinds of issues. The car park people are males and the day the childcare people are females.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And that in our culture is a very big marker of what, but the one who said only the economics

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: professor, nobody else, says this stuff. Because in economics, I don't know if you were familiar

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: with our profession, but we have something which we call marginal product. This is a fantasy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: I was a mathematician before I became an economist. I loved mathematics. I specialized in

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: mathematics. So I know mathematics pretty well. What economists do is silly, is childish, but they

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: think it's mathematics. But think for a minute what it means to suggest that you can identify

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the marginal product of a factor of production, like a worker. In the textbook when it's taught,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: I've taught this stuff. I hold my nose, but I teach it. Then I explain to students what I've

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: just taught you is horse shit, but first I teach it. What is the marginal product, if it might be

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: useful to say? The notion is, if you take away one worker right now from the pile, what will be the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: diminution of the output? That's the marginal product of that worker. Measured by? The amount

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: of the output that diminishes. Output of the raw product, of the product. Usually in real terms,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: so physical, not the value. You could do a value, but it's really more the physical you're in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: I mean, there is a transformation thing. I'd love to talk to you about value. It's so interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Yeah, I'd be glad to talk to you about value and price and all of that. But I just want to get to

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: that. Hegel, who is Marx's teacher, has a famous line, you can't step in the same river twice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: The argument is, you and the river have changed between the first and the second time. So it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: a different you and it's a different river. You can choose not to pay attention to that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Just you can't claim you're not doing that. You can't claim that you can actually do that

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: because you can't. There is no way to do that. So the meaning that you can't just remove a worker

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and have a clean mathematical calculation of the effect that it has on the output.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: That's right. Because too many other things are going on. Too many things are changing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And you cannot assume, much as you want to, that the outcome on the output side is uniquely

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: determined by the change you made on the input side. Can't do that. Even in the average, it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: not going to work out. Look, mathematics is full of abstractions. You can say, as we do in economics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Keteris Paribus, everything else held constant, but you have to know what you just did. You held

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: everything constant. You know why you do that? Because you can't do that in the real world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: That's not possible. You better account for that. Otherwise, you're mistaking the abstraction from

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the messy reality you abstracted from to get the abstraction. As a quick tangent, if we somehow

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: went through a thought experiment or an actual experiment of removing every single economist

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: from the world, would we be better off or worse off? Much better off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Okay. Economics is… And I'm one. I'm talking about myself. See, economics…

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: We're going to ship all the economies to Mars and see how it works off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: But the serious part of this is that economics… It's really about capitalism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Economics as a discipline is born with capital. There was no such thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: I teach courses at the university, for example, called History of Economic Thought.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Right? And I begin the students with Aristotle and Plato. And I say, you know, they talked about

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: really interesting things, but they never called it economics. It made no sense to people to abstract

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: something as central to daily life as economics broadly defined. It made no sense. That's a

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: creation much, much later. That's capitalism that did that, created the field of… So when I give

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Plato and Aristotle, I have to give them particular passages. By the way, footnote,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: because your audience will like it. Plato and Aristotle talked about markets because they

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: lived at a time in ancient Greece when market relations were beginning to intrude upon these

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: societies. So they were both interested in this phenomena that we're not just producing goods and

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: then distributing among us. We're doing it in a quid pro quo. I'll give you three oranges,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: you give me two shirts, a market exchange. And both Aristotle and Plato hated markets,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: denounced them. And for the same reason, they destroy social cohesion. They destroy community.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: They make some people rich and other people poor. And they set us against each other. And it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: terrible. And here's what they agreed on that. Here's what they disagreed on. One of them said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: okay, there can be no markets. That was Plato. Aristotle comes back and says, no, no, no, no,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: no, no, too late for that. The disruption caused in society by getting rid of this institution that

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: has crawled in amongst us would be too devastating. So we can't do that. But what we can do is

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: control it, regulate it, get from the market what it does reasonably well, and prevent it from doing

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the destructive things it does so badly. So fundamentally, the destructive thing of a market

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: is just the engine of capitalism. And so it creates exploitation of the worker.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: I wouldn't create that. Facilitates it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Facilitates it. And it is an institution that Plato and Aristotle feel is a terrible danger

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: to community. Which, by the way, is a way of thinking about it that exists right now all

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: over the world. Look, the medieval Catholic Church had a doctrine, the prohibition of usury.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And this was that God said, if there's a person who needs to borrow from you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: then that's a person in need. And the good Christian thing to do is to help him.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: To demand an interest payment rather than to help your fellow man is God hates you for that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: That's a sin. Jesus is crying all the way to wherever it is he goes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: But would Jesus be crying when you try to scale that system? So that has to do with the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: intimate human interaction. The idea of markets is you're able to create a system that involves

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: thousands, millions of humans. And there'd be some level of safe, self-regulating fairness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: There might be, but it's hard to imagine that charging interest would be the way to do that.
