metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: I wonder what, so I guess- Suppose you were interested in that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Suppose you took us your problem. We have a set of funds that can be loaned out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: People don't want to consume it. They're ready to lend it. Okay. To whom should they lend it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Well, we could say in our society, we're going to run this the way professors

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: in institutions like MIT work this. They write up a project. They send the project in to some

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: government office where it is looked at against other projects. And this office in the government

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: decides we're going to fund this one and that one because they're more needed in our society.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: We are in greater need of solving this problem than that problem. And so we're going to lend money to

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: people working on this problem more readily or more money than we lend over here because we're

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: going to- But instead, what we do is who can pay the highest interest rate? Whoa, what do you do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: What ethics would justify you? Do it. It's like a market in general. Something is in shortage.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: All markets are about how to handle shortage. That's one basic way to understand it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And so if the demand is greater than the supply, which is all the word shortage means, has no other

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: meaning. If the demand is greater than the supply, okay, now you've got a problem. You can't satisfy

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: all the demanders because you don't have enough supply. You have a shortage. Okay. Now, how are

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: you going to do it? In a market, you allow people who have a lot of money to bid up the price of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: whatever is short. That solves your problem because as the price goes up, the poor people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: they drop out. They can't buy the thing at the exalted price. So you've got a way of distributing

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the shortage. It goes to the people with the most money. At this point, most human beings

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: confronted with this explanation of a market would turn against it because it contradicts their

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Christian, Judaic, Islamic, all of them would say, what? You know what that means? It means that a

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: rich person can get the scarce milk and give it to their cat while the poor person has no milk

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: for their five children. There it is. You want a market? Why?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: There was a fundamental thing that seems unfair. There's the resulting inequality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Now...

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Or death.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Or death. Well, that's the ultimate inequality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Yes, it is. What about... And we're going to jump around from the philosophical, from the economics

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: to the debate type of thing. What about the lifting ties raise all boats? Meaning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: if we look at the 20th century, a lot of people, maybe you disagree with this, but they attribute

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: a lot of the innovation and the average improvement in the quality of life to capitalism,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: to inventions and innovation, to engineering and science developments that resulted from

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: competition and all those kinds of forces. So not looking at the individual unfairness of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: exploitation as it's specifically defined, but just observing historically. Looking at the 20th

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: century, we came up with a lot of cool stuff that seemed to have made life easier and better on

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: average. What do you say to that? I have several responses to that, but I do disagree

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: pretty fundamentally with what's going on there. But let me give you the arguments so that you

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: can hear them and then you can evaluate them, as can anybody who's listening or watching.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Marx was a student of Hegel. And one of Hegel's central arguments was that everything that exists

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: exists, quote, in contradiction. In simple English, there's a good and bad side, if you like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: to everything. And you won't understand it unless you accept that proposition and start looking

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: for the good things that are the other side of the bad ones and the bad things that are the other

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: side of the good ones, etc. The dialectic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Yes, exactly. And Marx, very attentive to that, explicitly agrees with this on many occasions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and applies it, of course, to the central object of his research, capitalism. So this is not a

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: simple-minded fellow who's telling you all the bad things about capitalism as if there were nothing

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: that this system achieved or accomplished. And one of the things he celebrates a lot is

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the technological dynamism of the system, which Marx takes to be profound, because he lived at

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the time when major breakthroughs in textile technology and mining and chemistry and so on

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: were achieved. But as to the notion that capitalism is therefore responsible for the improvement in

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the quality or the standard of living of the mass of people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Marx now comes back and says, oh, wait a minute here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Number one, capitalism as a system has been mostly represented by capitalists, which makes a certain

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: sense. And those capitalists, with very few exceptions, some, but very few, have fought

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: against every effort to improve the lives of the mass of people. The goal of a capitalist is to

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: minimize labor costs. What that means is replace a worker with a machine, move the production from

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: expensive US to cheap China, bring in desperate immigrants from other parts of the world, because

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: they will work for less money than the folks that you have here at home. Every measure to help the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: standard of living of American workers had to be fought for for decades over the opposition of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: capitalists from the beginning to right now. The reason we have a minimum wage, which was past

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the middle of the 1930s, when it was proposed, it was blocked by capitalists. They got together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: They don't want, and today, just a factoid for you. The last time the minimum wage was raised

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: in the United States, federal minimum wage, was in 2009, when it was set at the lofty sum of $7

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and 25 cents an hour, which you cannot live on. Over the last 12 years or so, whatever it is now,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: 11, 12, 13 years since then, we have had an increase in the price level in this country

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: every year, and in the last year, 8.5%. During that time that the prices went up,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the minimum wage was never raised. What? This is a time of stock market boom, of growing inequality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: This is the nerve of the defender of capitalists who wants now to get credit for the improvement

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: in the standard of life of the workers that was fought by every generation. You know it takes your

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: breath away. It's an argument. Whoa. But I take my hat off if I had one, because that is one of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: only ways to justify this system. Long ago, let me get the heart of it, long ago, capitalism could have

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: overcome hunger, could have overcome disease, could have, I mean, way beyond what we have now,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: but it didn't. And that's the worst moral condemnation imaginable. How do you justify

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: that when you could, you didn't? Look, let me get at it another way, because this may

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: interest you anyway. The issue is not that capitalism isn't technologically dynamic. It is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And along the way, it has developed things that have helped people's lives get better. No question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: But the notion that the mass enjoyment of a rising standard of living is somehow built into

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: capitalism is factually nuts and is such an outrageous, and I can give you, because you do

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: math, you'll understand it. Think of it this way. Imagine a production process in which you have

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: $100 that the capitalist has to lay out for tools, equipment, and raw materials,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and $100 that he has to lay out for workers, hire the workers, and he puts them all together,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and he has an output. And let's say the output is 100 units of something, one of the prices,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and that's his revenue. And when he takes his product and sells it and gets the revenue,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: let's say the revenue is, it doesn't really matter, it's 120, for lack of a better word,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: 220, sorry, and he takes 100 of it and replaces the tools, equipment, and raw materials he used up,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: another 100 to hire the workers for the next shift, and the other 20 is his profit, and he puts that

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: aside. Now along comes a technological breakthrough, a machine, a new machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And the new machine is so effective, you can get the same number of units of output with half the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: workers. So you don't need to spend 100 on workers, you only need to spend 50. You can do it with half

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the workers. And so the capitalist goes to the workers—by the way, this happens every day—and

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: he says to half of them, you're fired. Don't come back Monday morning, I don't need you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: It's nothing personal. I got a machine. Why does he do that? Because the 50 he now no longer has

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: to spend on labor, because he doesn't need half of them, he keeps. Everything else is the same,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the machine, everything else is the same, just to make the math easy. So he keeps as his own profit

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the 50 that before he paid for those workers. Because when he sells it for 220, that 50 he

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: doesn't have to give to the next job because he has a new machine. So that's what he does.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: The technology leads. He's happy. He's become more profitable. He's got an extra 50,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: which is why he buys the machine. The workers are screwed. Half of them just lost their job,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: have to go home to their husband and wife, tell them I don't have a job anymore. I didn't do

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: anything wrong. The guy was nice enough to say it was nothing wrong with me, but he doesn't need it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: So I'm completely screwed here. I don't know what I'm going to do about the debts we have,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the house on mortgage, my children's education, or whatever else he's got going for himself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: All right, now the point. There was, of course, an alternative path. The alternative path would

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: have been to keep all the workers, pay them exactly the same that you did before for half a day's work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: You would have got the same output, same revenue, same profit as before.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: But the gain of the technology would have been a half a day of freedom every day of the lives

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: of these workers. The majority of workers would have been really helped by this technology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: But instead, they were screwed so that one guy, the employer, could make a big bundle of more money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: You want to support a system like this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Well, to go back to Hegel, the good and the bad. You just listed the bad, and you also first listed the good, the technological innovation of this kind of system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: The question is the alternative, whatever, as we try to sneak up to ideas of what the alternative might look like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: what are the good and the bad of the alternative? You just, as an opposite, by contrast, showed that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: well, a nice alternative is you work less, get paid the same, you have more leisure time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: opportunity to pursue other interests, the creative interests, family,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: flourish as a human being, basically strengthen and embolden the basic humanity that's under all of us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Yes, but then what cost does that have on the deadline-fueled, competition-fueled machine

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: of technological innovation that is the positive side of capitalism?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Slows it down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: It slows it down. And the question is, which is more important for the flourishing of humanity?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: I agree with that. And I'd love there to be a democratic mechanism. So let's discuss it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: let's debate it, and then let's decide what mixture, because it's not either or. The math

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: problem I gave you is either or. We could mix it. You could have a third less of a working day

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: instead of a half less, and then the other part would be extra profit for our employer, etc. So

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: let's have a democratic discussion of what is the mix between the positive and we have no such thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: All of this is decided by one side in this debate, which not only we know what they do,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: they always choose the one that maximizes their profit, because that's what they were told to do

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: in business school where I've taught. So not only is it an undemocratic decision, but it's lopsided

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: taboot. So we don't have the opportunity, but I would love for us to be good Hegelian Marxists and

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: say, let's take a look at the plus and the minus and make the best decision that we can. We'll make

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: mistakes, but we'll all make them together. It won't be one of us making a dictatorial decision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: You know, Marx developed the notion of the dictatorship of the proletariat,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: not as a notion of how government works, but as a notion of what the practical reality is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: The dictatorship of these key decisions is not made by some sitting council, it's made by each

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: little capitalist in his or her relationships with the workers in the workplace, which is why Marx

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: focused his analysis on that point. And by the way, I can sketch for you right now so it doesn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: lurk in the background what the alternative is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Yeah, let's go there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Okay. It goes right back to what I said earlier. The workers themselves, the collection of employees

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: together, appropriate their own surplus and decide democratically what to do with it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: which includes the decision of whether or not to buy a machine and whether or not

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: to use the machine and the savings it might allow to be handled by more leisure for themselves,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: or as a fund for new developments in technology or new products or whatever they want.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And you know, this is an old idea in human—Marx loved that. Toward the end of his life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: he started reading extensively in anthropology. And one of the reasons he did that toward the end

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: of his life was because he kept discovering that in this society and that, including here in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: United States, that there were examples of people who organized their production in precisely this

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: way, as a collective democratic community in which everybody had an idea of what to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Everybody had an equal voice. So we all together decide democratically what to produce, how to

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: produce, where to produce, and what to do with the output we all helped to produce. So let's do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: In this country where democracy is a value nearly everybody subscribes to,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: think about it this way, the stunning contradiction that there is a place in our society where

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: democracy has never been allowed to enter. The workplace. In the workplace, a tiny group of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: people, unaccountable to the rest of them, the employer, whether that's an individual, a family,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: a partnership, or a corporate board of directors, tiny group of people controls economically a vast

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: mass of employees. Those employees don't elect those people. There is no accountability.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: It is the most undemocratic arrangement imaginable. And this society insists on calling itself

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: democratic when it has organized the minor matter of producing everything in a way that is

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the direct, it's autocratic. So to push back on a few things. So one is the idea of this society

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: calling itself democratic is that the government is elected democratically and the government is

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: able to pressure the workplace through the process of regulation. You pass laws of the boundaries of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: how, you know, minimum wage, all those kinds of things. That's the one idea. The other is there is

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: a natural force within the capitalist when there's no monopolies of competition being the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: accountability. So if you're a shitty boss, the employee in the capitalist system has the freedom

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: to move to another company, work for a better boss. So that creates pressure on the employers

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and the bosses. That's at least the idea that there's two boundaries of you not misbehaving.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: One is the law, so regulations passed by the government, democratic. And the second is because

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: there's always alternatives in theory, then that puts pressure on everyone to behave well because

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: you can always leave. So I mean, that's kinds of accountability. But what you're saying is that

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: does not result in a significant enough accountability where the employer that avoids

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: exploitation of the worker. Absolutely. I mean, whatever accountability you get in those mechanisms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And let me respond to that and then on the counter argument. First, competition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Here again, we have to be Hegelians just a little. Competition destroys itself. It doesn't need any

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: out. The whole point of competition is to beat the other guy. If I can produce the same product

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: as the other guy, either a better quality or a lower price or maybe both, then I win because

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the customers will come to me because my price is lower or my quality is better and they'll leave

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the other guy. He'll go out of business. Now let's follow. When he goes out of business,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: because I won the competition, he fires his workers. I hire them because I'm now going to

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: be able to serve a market he can't serve anymore. So I'm going to buy the used equipment. And then

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: thereby many become fuel. Monopoly is the product of competition. It's not the antithesis. It's the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: product. Well, let's see. That's where it comes from. There's another element to the system where

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: there's always a new guy that comes in. There isn't. Well, that's the dream. The entrepreneurial

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: spirit of the United States, for example, of a capitalist system is you can be broke and one day

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: have a strong idea and build up a business that takes on Google and Facebook and Twitter and all

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the different car, Ford, GM, which is what you look at Tesla, for example. That's the American

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: dream. One of the many ideals of the American dream is you can move from dirt poor to being the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: richest person in the world. It can happen. It can happen. But you're against-

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: You know what that's like? That's like you can win the lottery.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: No, that's not quite. No, the lottery is complete luck. Here you can work your ass off if you have a

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: good idea. The odds are better in the lottery. That's not true. There's a lot of new businesses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: How many Teslas do you know? Tesla's a really bad example because the car company,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the automotive sector is so difficult to operate at such a thin margin of profit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: They're probably a good example of capitalism just completely coming to a halt in terms of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: lack of innovation. That's a very complicated industry because of the supply chain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Come on. They have their uniquenesses, you're quite right, but so does every other industry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: The one thing that's common is that many become few. What you can also have is when you have a few,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: they jack up the price, they make an enormous profit. And in the irony of capitalism,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Marx would love this, they begin to incentivize people to break into this industry because the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: few remaining are making a wild amount of profit because they are a few and can jigger the market

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: to make it work like that for them. The reason every small capitalist is trying to build market

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: share, that's a polite way of saying they want to become a monopolist or to be more exact,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: an oligopolist, one of a handful of firms that dominates. That's what they're there for.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: But yeah, to push back a little bit also, because that could be, this is a question also,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: do you think we're in danger of oversimplifying capitalism that completely removes the basic

body.input: decency of human beings? So if you give me a choice to press a button to get rid of the

body.input: You think?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: So maybe I'll just say my bias is the people I know, especially at the top of companies,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: are in the tech sector where innovation is such a big part of it. So I think a lot of the things

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: around whatever the newest technology is. And then you have a period where you can get excited

body.input: about that and the very rich people who come to the top can talk endlessly, as they always do,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: For me, how do I put this in a way that I don't mean to offend.

body.input: Please, please.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: No, no, no. I don't want to. But the problem with capitalism is, and maybe you'll like this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the problem with capitalism is not that it is the one thing that's consistent with human nature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: why? Because their humanity is contradicted by what it is they're being asked to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: I mean, the corporate sector this year, just to give you an idea,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: pays now 300 times what the average worker pays, but they're jacking it up even more. Why?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And it ends the system. By the way, there's one more thing on the rationality, and this goes to

body.input: individual car. That's fucking nuts. What are you doing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: That's one of the things they're doing, but automation is also another one. But on the Elon

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: side, there's also a hilariously named boring company, which is working on tunnels, which is

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: actually expanding the flexibility you might have to start playing with ideas of public transit,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: I think. Listen, I'm now partially living in Austin, Texas that I don't know if they know

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: what a public transit system is, period. There's F-150 pickup trucks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Well, this is an interesting…

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: The older… By the way, footnote, the older this city, the more likely it has public transportation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Boston is the best example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Have you been…

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Yeah, yeah, of course. Yeah, I have a place in Boston.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Boston, with the street railway, Boston is your case study of how to do this because they've been

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: doing it all along. New York's pretty good, too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: There's a trade-off. Yeah, New York, I would say, is better than Boston because

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: their technology also helps you out to do the public transit better. It's almost like

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Boston is a little too old, but yes, I get your point. But there is… The Ford F-150 pickup truck

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: symbolizes something about America. And there is a practical nature to the fact

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: that in order to do public transit, in order to do some of these things that you're talking about

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: with the working class, there has to be a central planning component or there has to be a centralized

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: component. And America is very much based on the idea of, at least in recent times, I would say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: from the founding of individualism, of respecting individual freedom. Are you worried that in order

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: to bring some of these ideas of Marxism to life, you would trample on individual freedoms?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: No.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Can you respect both? Sure. For me, Marxism is a way to enhance

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the individual freedom of the mass of people who have had that freedom eroded under the capitalism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: That's a motive for my Marxism. It was for Marx too. He loved the French Revolution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: He loved the liberté, égalité, fraternité, the great three, and then democracy, the American

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: contribution, if you like. He believed in all of that. His critique of capitalism was it promised

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: it and then never delivered it. And the reason you have to go beyond it is because it didn't deliver

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: what it had promised. So for me, it is the fulfillment of a general. But again, I'm a

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Hegelian Marxist, so if you want. Individualism, for me, is not the way it's set up in this society,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: some sort of antithesis to the government. I think an immense con has been pulled on the American

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: people. And the con works like this. You know what's bad and what's dangerous and threatens you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: It's the government. The government is going to come in and tell you what to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: The government is going to run your life. The government is the problem. There really is no

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: other way to explain the following in American politics. Large numbers of people lose their homes

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: in a downturn, like the so-called Great Recession of 2008. Who do they blame? The government. Large

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: numbers of people go unemployed. And what are the media all about? The government.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: If I were a capitalist, I'd love this. I kick the workers by throwing them out of their home,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and they don't get angry with me. They get angry with the government. I fire large numbers of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: people. I have no responsibility for what happens to them as a result of having no job and no income.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And they get angry at the senator. I'm laughing all the way to the bank. This is a genius stroke.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: In theory. But if you look at government, because you said accountability and the capitalist system

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: has no accountability, there's some pushback I give on the accountability. I think there is some

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: accountability we can discuss in a Hegelian way. There's more accountability.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: I would say that in theory, government is perfectly accountable. That's the whole point of a democratic

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: system, is you vote people in. In practice, there's a giant growing bureaucracy that is

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: accountable only on the surface. There's two parties that seem to be-

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Are the same.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Are the same. Media is somehow integrated into making the same two parties that are just wearing

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: different colored shirts to seem like they're very opposed and are arguing and bitterly arguing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: calling each other's spouses nasty names and all those kinds of things. Okay. But that's government.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: So who exactly is worse here, government or companies?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Well, why are we asking that question? These are twins. Look, what you were able to say about

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Republicans and Democrats just now, with which I agree, I would say the same thing about

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: corporations and the government. This is the same people, literally the same.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: But let's go to Churchill. Which one is worse? Let's go to Churchill. Democracy is the worst

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: form of government, except all the other ones or whatever. So this same idea, which one exactly

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: is worse? Because to me, it seems like-

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Which one between what and what?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Government and industry and companies. It's because government is plagued by,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: I will call it corruption because the corruption of bureaucratic paperwork.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: There doesn't seem to be a serious accountability.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Again, we're not living on the same planet. The greatest practitioners of central planning are

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: corporations. Elon has an operation like General Motors, Ford, IBM, or any of the other

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: mega corps. They have to plan. They buy up companies because they don't want to deal in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: market. They don't want the insecurity, the uncertainty of having to buy their inputs or

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: sell their outputs to somebody they don't control. They want the professor to teach the genius of a

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: market. They hate the market. And when they grow to be big, they keep buying whoever they were

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: dealing with before so they could better control them, which requires them then to plan the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: production and distribution of goods inside rather than buying them in the market.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: The model of the government is the private corporation. I have spent my life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: give you an example, in American universities, big ones, famous ones, not just as a student,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: but as a professor. I've been half a dozen schools. I teach there. It's a new school here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: It's another one, right? They all model themselves after businesses. They model their-

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: You can attack the bureaucracy of universities. Good reason. It's a mess. But they're proudly

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: modeling themselves on organizing their bureaucracy in a business-like manner.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: So you're looking at a difference which isn't there. The government and the private sector

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: are partners, and both of them wouldn't have it any other way. The corporations want that from

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: the government, and the government now knows that to please the corporations is the number one

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: objective they have because that's how they keep their jobs and keep their system going.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: And so for all practical purposes, this is the same people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: But there's important differences that I don't know if they're fundamental or just

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: consequences of history, but if you have government, they're accountable in a different way than

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: companies. Companies are accountable by, especially if you have a consumer, they're accountable by

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: sort of the consumer spending or not spending their money on whatever the heck the company is

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: selling. The government is accountable by votes, and it seems like government, unlike companies

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: for most of companies' history, is always too big to fail, meaning it can always just print money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: It can always save itself, and that creates a bureaucracy. You rarely pay the cost of having

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: made bad decisions if you're in government. You distribute the blame, and it's very unclear who's

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: responsible for bad decisions, so bad decisions in government accumulate. So you become more and more

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and more inefficient and more and more poor in your decision-making in terms of, you said public

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: transit. Should we build a public transit system in this city or not? That's a difficult decision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: That's an interesting decision. I would say it's very often a very good decision, but whoever makes

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: that decision should be accountable for a good or bad decision, and it seems like companies are more

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: accountable. They feel the pain of having made a bad decision more because they can go bankrupt.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: There's much more day-to-day pressure to make good engineering decisions. Government doesn't seem

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: to be under the same level of pressure. Do you disagree with that? I disagree with that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Everything in my history pushes me. I may be living a different...

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Who knows? A planet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Who knows? Or taking a different sort of drug. I won't mention the name, but I personally had a

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: lot to do with a very large company here in the United States, here in the New York area. It

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: involved two brothers and a family who built it up into a huge corporation. One of the brothers was

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: kind of the dynamo of the family, and he was more responsible than anybody else building it up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: But he took care of his brothers. He had a nice feeling about his brothers. So the one brother who

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: could not, without help, tie his shoes, became a vice president, got an enormous salary,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: got a beautiful office in a skyscraper, not that many blocks from where I'm sitting,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and that was the way that family handled that company. And all of his relatives were somewhere

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: in this company doing a variety of whatever. And my experience with this, and because I went to the

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: schools I told you, all my experiences with that group of people, corporate executives,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: full of those stories, you know, they made mistake after mistake, which they would tell you about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Didn't undermine their… They were always able to blame somebody else, something else

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: that scraped them through. And had they not been able to, they would have been replaced by another

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: person who did the same thing for as long as they could. And they knew it. They would talk about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: At family events, that's how I know. I understand that you want the outside world to look at it this

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: way, but it's not my experience. Interesting. But again, that kind of thing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: at the risk of saying human nature again, I wonder what kind of system allows for that more versus

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: versus less. This is the question of, I would call that, let's put that under the umbrella term of

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: corruption. Which system allows for more corruption? But remember that the way I defined a different

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: system is not more or less government. It's more or less allowing a democratic workplace,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: reconfiguring it. What happens when everybody has a vote, when you have to explain what the strategies

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: are, what the alternatives are to a larger number of people than a board of directors or major

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: shareholders or whoever it is that most companies are responsible to. And now you've got a whole

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: different universe. It's not a small group of people. It can't be hidden the way it's normally

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: hidden, most of it, and on and on and on. This is… Worker co-ops is what this is called in many parts

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: of the world. So it's not that I'm advocating something that's never been seen before.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Not at all. The Marxism I understand is to pick from historical precedents the things that we think

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: will work better. And I think if all the people in an enterprise, just to drive the point home,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: democratically decided, they would never give two or three individuals $100 million while everybody

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: else can't send their kid to college. I mean, they can do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: So just to return, just to address this point about the particular implementation of Marxism,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: that was the early days in the Soviet Union. Why did Stalinism, for example, lead to so much

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: bloodshed, do you think, and human suffering? Is there any elements within the ideas of Marxism

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: that catalyzed the kind of government, the kind of system that led to that bloodshed?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: I don't think so. I think there were many things that led to the bloodshed and to all that Stalin's

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: regimes did. And I spent 10 years of my life with another economist writing a book,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: about that, to try to explain from a Marxist position the rise and fall of the Soviet Union.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: You might want to take a look at it sometime. But there, I'm going to say a few things now,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: but all of those things are spelled out in great detail with loads of empirical evidence, etc.,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: in that work. Let me start with playing a little bit with Hegel. The biggest impact

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: that Marxism had on the Soviet Union was really not so much what the Soviet Union did,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: but what the rest of the world did. I mean, you had a really interesting

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: move, and I'll give you a parallel from today. The move was that the old Russian regime collapsed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: World War I, just it fell apart. The Tsar and all of that, it couldn't survive. It had already been

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: in trouble. There was a revolution in 1905, and the Soviet Union was in a state of crisis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: It couldn't survive. It had already been in trouble. There was a revolution in 1905.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: There was the loss of the war to Japan. I mean, if you know Russian history, which I assume you do,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: you'll know that there was a lot leading up to the collapse in 1917. And in some ways, it was

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: fortuitous that the political group, very small, that could seize the opportunity of that collapse

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: happened to be Marxists. Earlier on, with Kerensky, the first government that tried,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: it wasn't people all that impressed by Marxism. It was people more skeptical and would not have

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: been called Marxists probably by history. They tried. They couldn't. Lenin and his associates

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: were able to take over from them later in that same year. The rest of the world, though, was

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: horrified. The rest of the world saw Marxism having taken this immense leap from being a

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: political party, a movement, critical of capitalism, yes, but still not challenging the power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: Now it had the power, and in a big country. And they freaked out. If you know American history,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295

body.input: and the disruption goes real deep for any refugee.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Wolff: Marxism and Communism | Lex Fridman Podcast #295
