metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: also an architect and she adored him and decided to share her life with him. And I basically grew

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: up in a big cave full of books. I'm almost feral. And I was bored out there. It was very, very

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: beautiful, very quiet and quite lonely. So I started to read. And by the time I came to school,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: I've read everything until fourth grade and then some, and there was not a real way for me to relate

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: to the outside world. And I couldn't quite put my finger on why. And today I know it was because I

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: was a nerd, obviously, and it was the only nerd around. So there were no other kids like me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And there was nobody interested in physics or computing or mathematics and so on. And this

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: village school that I went to, it was basically a nice school. Kids were nice to me. I was not

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: beaten up, but I also didn't make many friends or build deep relationships. That only happened

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: starting from ninth grade when I went into a school for mathematics and physics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Do you remember any key books from this moment?

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: I basically read everything. So I went to the library and I worked my way through the

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: children's and young adult sections. And then I read a lot of science fiction. For instance,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Stanislav Lem, basically the great author of cybernetics, has influenced me. Back then,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: I didn't see him as a big influence because everything that he wrote seemed to be so natural

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: to me. And it's only later that I contrasted it with what other people wrote. Another thing

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: that was very influential on me were the classical philosophers and also the teacher of romanticism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So German poetry and art, Dr. Hilshoff and Heine, and up to Heise and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Heise, I love Heise. So at which point do the classical philosophers end? At this point,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: we're in the 21st century. What's the latest classical philosopher? Does this stretch through

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: even as far as Nietzsche or is this, are we talking about Plato and Aristotle?

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: I think that Nietzsche is the classical equivalent of a shit poster.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So he's a classical troll.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: He's very smart and easy to read. But he's not so much trolling others, he's trolling himself

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: because he was at odds with the world. Largely his romantic relationships didn't work out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: He got angry and he basically became a nihilist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Isn't that a beautiful way to be as an intellectual, is to constantly be trolling yourself,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: to be in that conflict, in that tension?

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: I think it's a lack of self-awareness. At some point, you have to understand the comedy of

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: your own situation. If you take yourself seriously and you are not functional,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: it ends in tragedy as it did for Nietzsche.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: You think he took himself too seriously in that tension.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And as you find the same thing in Heise and so on, the Steppenwolf syndrome is classic

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: adolescence where you basically feel misunderstood by the world and you don't understand that all the

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: misunderstandings are the result of your own lack of self-awareness. Because you think that you are

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: a prototypical human and the others around you should behave the same way as you expect them

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: based on your innate instincts and it doesn't work out. And you become a transcendentalist

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: to deal with that. So it's very, very understandable and have great sympathies for this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: to the degree that I can have sympathy for my own intellectual history. But you have to grow out of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So as an intellectual, a life well lived, a journey well traveled is one where you

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: don't take yourself seriously from that perspective?

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: I think that you are neither serious or not serious yourself because you need to become

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: unimportant as a subject. That is, if you are a philosopher, belief is not a verb.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: You don't do this for the audience, you don't do it for yourself. You have to submit to the things

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: that are possibly true and you have to follow wherever your inquiry leads, but it's not about

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: you. It has nothing to do with you. So do you think then people like Ayn Rand

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: believed sort of in the idea of there's objective truth. So what's your sense in the philosophical,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: if you remove yourself as objective from the picture, you think it's possible to actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: discover ideas that are true or are we just in a mesh of relative concepts that are either true

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: nor false? It's just a giant mess. You cannot define objective truth without

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: understanding the nature of truth in the first place. So what does the brain mean by saying that

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: it's cover something as truth? So for instance, a model can be predictive or not predictive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Then there can be a sense in which a mathematical statement can be true because it's defined as

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: true under certain conditions. So it's basically a particular state that a variable can have in a

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: simple game. And then you can have a correspondence between systems and talk about truth, which is

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: again a type of model correspondence. And there also seems to be a particular kind of ground truth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So for instance, you're confronted with the enormity of something existing at all, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: That's stunning when you realize something exists rather than nothing. And this seems to be true,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: right? There's an absolute truth in the fact that something seems to be happening.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Yeah, that to me is a showstopper. I could just think about that idea and be amazed by that idea

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: for the rest of my life and not going any farther because I don't even know the answer to that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Why does anything exist at all? Well, the easiest answer is existence

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: is the default, right? So this is the lowest number of bits that you would need to encode this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Whose answer? Who provides it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: The simplest answer to this is that existence is the default.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: What about non-existence? I mean, that seems...

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Non-existence might not be a meaningful notion in this sense. So in some sense,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: if everything that can exist exists, for something to exist, it probably needs to be implementable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: The only thing that can be implemented is finite automata. So maybe the whole of existence is the

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: superposition of all finite automata and we are in some region of the fractal that has the properties

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: that it can contain us. What does it mean to be a superposition of finite automata? So any

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: superposition of all possible rules? Imagine that every automaton is basically an operator

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: that acts on some substrate and as a result, you get emergent patterns.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: What's the substrate? I have no idea to know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: But some substrate. It's something that can store information.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Something that can store information, there's a automaton.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Something that can hold state.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Still, doesn't make sense to me the why that exists at all. I could just sit there with a

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: beer or a vodka and just enjoy the fact, pondering the why.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: May not have a why. This might be the wrong direction to ask into this. So there could be no

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: relation in the why direction without asking for a purpose or for a cause. It doesn't mean that

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: everything has to have a purpose or cause. So we mentioned some philosophers in that

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: earlier, just taking a brief step back into that. Okay, so we asked ourselves when did

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: classical philosophy end. I think for Germany, it largely ended with the first revolution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Which one was that? This was when we ended the monarchy

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: and started a democracy. And at this point, we basically came up with a new form of government

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: that didn't have a good sense of this new organism that society wanted to be. And in a way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: it decapitated the universities. So the universities went on through modernism like a headless chicken.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: At the same time, democracy failed in Germany and we got fascism as a result.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And it burned down things in a similar way as Stalinism burned down intellectual traditions in

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Russia. And Germany, both Germanies have not recovered from this. Eastern Germany had this

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: vulgar dialectic materialism and Western Germany didn't get much more edgy than Habermas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So in some sense, both countries lost their intellectual traditions and killing off and

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: driving out the Jews didn't help. Yeah, so that was the end of really

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: rigorous, what you would say is classical philosophy. There's also this thing that

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: in some sense, the low-hanging fruits in philosophy were mostly wrapped. And the last big things

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: that we discovered was the constructivist turn in mathematics. So to understand that the parts of

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: mathematics that work are computation, that was a very significant discovery in the first half of

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: the 20th century. And it hasn't fully permeated philosophy and even physics yet. So physicists

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: checked out the code libraries from mathematics before constructivism became universal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: What's constructivism? What are you referring to, Gödel's incompleteness theorem, those kinds of

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: ideas? So basically, Gödel himself, I think, didn't get it yet. Hilbert could get it. Hilbert

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: saw that, for instance, a country's set theoretic experiments in mathematics led into contradictions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And he noticed that with the current semantics, we cannot build a computer in mathematics that

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: runs mathematics without crashing. And Gödel could prove this. And so what Gödel could show is using

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: classical mathematical semantics, you run into contradictions. And because Gödel strongly believed

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: in these semantics and more than in what he could observe and so on, he was shocked. It basically

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: shook his world to the core because in some sense, he felt that the world has to be implemented in

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: classical mathematics. And for Turing, it wasn't quite so bad. I think that Turing could see that

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: the solution is to understand that mathematics was computation all along, which means, for instance,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: pi in classical mathematics is a value. It's also a function, but it's the same thing. And in

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: computation, a function is only a value when you can compute it. And if you cannot compute the last

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: digit of pi, you only have a function. You can plug this function into your local sun, let it run

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: until the sun burns out. This is it. This is the last digit of pi you will know. But it also means

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: there can be no process in the physical universe or in any physically realized computer that depends

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: on having known the last digit of pi. Which means there are parts of physics that are defined in

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: such a way that cannot strictly be true because assuming that this could be true leads into

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: contradictions. So I think putting computation at the center of the world view is actually the

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: right way to think about it. Yes. And Wittgenstein could see it. And Wittgenstein basically preempted

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: the logitist program of AI that Minsky started later, like 30 years later. Turing was actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: a pupil of Wittgenstein. Really? So I didn't know there's any connection between Turing and Wittgenstein.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Wittgenstein even canceled some classes when Turing was not present because he thought it was not

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: worth spending the time with the others. Interesting. If you read the Tractatus,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: it's a very beautiful book. It's basically one thought on 75 pages. It's very non-typical for

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: philosophy because it doesn't have arguments in it and it doesn't have references in it. It's just

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: one thought that is not intending to convince anybody. It's mostly for people that have the

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: same insight as me. Just spell it out. And this insight is there is a way in which mathematics

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: and philosophy ought to meet. Mathematics tries to understand the domain of all languages by

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: starting with those that are so formalizable that you can prove all the properties of the statements

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: that you make. But the price that you pay is that your language is very, very simple. So it's very

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: hard to say something meaningful in mathematics. And it looks complicated to people, but it's far

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: less complicated than what our brain is casually doing all the time. And it makes sense of reality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: That's right. And philosophy is coming from the top. So it's mostly starting from natural languages

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: with vaguely defined concepts. And the hope is that mathematics and philosophy can meet at some

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: point. And Wittgenstein was trying to make them meet. And he already understood that, for instance,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: you could express everything with the NAND calculus, that you could reduce the entire logic

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: to NAND gates as we do in our modern computers. So in some sense, he already understood Turing

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: universality before Turing spelled it out. I think when he wrote the Tractatus, he didn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: understand yet that the idea was so important and significant. And I suspect then when Turing wrote

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: it out, nobody cared that much. Turing was not that famous when he lived. It was mostly his work

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: in decrypting the German codes that made him famous and gave him some notoriety. But this

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: saint status that he has to computer science right now, and the AI is something that I think he

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: could acquire later. That's kind of interesting. And do you think of computation and computer

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: science, and you kind of represent that to me, is maybe that's the modern day. You in a sense are

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: the new philosopher by sort of the computer scientist who dares to ask the bigger questions

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: that philosophy originally started. Is the new philosopher? Certainly not me, I think. I'm mostly

body.input: into the sentence. Do you think that's like a little step towards that eventually will take us

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: to the attentional mechanisms from which consciousness can emerge?

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Not quite. I think it models only one aspect of attention. In the early days of automated

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: language translation, there was an example that I found particularly funny, where somebody tried

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: to translate a text from English into German, and it was a bat broke the window. And the

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: translation in German was, eine Fledermaus zerbrach das Fenster mit einem Baseballschläger.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So to translate back into English, a bat, this flying mammal broke the window with a baseball bat.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And it seemed to be the most similar to this program because it somehow maximized the

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: possibility of translating the concept bat into German in the same sentence. And this is some

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: mistake that the transformer model is not doing because it's tracking identity. And the attentional

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: mechanism in the transformer model is basically putting its finger on individual concepts and

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: make sure that these concepts pop up later in the text and tracks basically the individuals

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: through the text. And it's why the system can learn things that other systems couldn't before

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: it, which makes it, for instance, possible to write a text where it talks about the scientist,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: then the scientist has a name and has a pronoun, and it gets a consistent story about that thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: What it does not do, it doesn't fully integrate this. So this meaning falls apart at some point,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: it loses track of this context. It does not yet understand that everything that it says has to

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: refer to the same universe. And this is where this thing falls apart. But the attention in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: transformer model does not go beyond tracking identity. And tracking identity is an important

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: part of attention, but it's a different, very specific attentional mechanism. And it's not the

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: one that gives rise to the type of consciousness that we have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Okay. Just to linger on, what do you mean by identity in the context of language?

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So when you talk about language, you have different words that can refer to the same concept.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Got it. So space of concepts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And it can also be in a nominal sense or in an exical sense that you say this word does not only

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: refer to this class of objects, but it refers to a definite object, to some kind of agent

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: that waves their way through the story. And it's only referred by different ways in the language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So the language is basically a projection from a conceptual representation, from a scene that is

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: evolving into a discrete string of symbols. And what the transformer is able to do, it learns

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: aspects of this projection mechanism that other models couldn't learn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So have you ever seen an artificial intelligence or any kind of construction idea that allows for,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: unlike neural networks or perhaps within neural networks, that's able to form

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: something where the space of concepts continues to be integrated? So what you're describing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: building a knowledge base, building this consistent larger and larger sets of ideas

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: that would then allow for deeper understanding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Wittgenstein thought that we can build everything from language, from basically a logical

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: grammatical construct. And I think to some degree, this was also what Minsky believed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So that's why he focused so much on common sense, reasoning, and so on. And a project that was

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: inspired by him was Psyche. That was basically-

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: That's still going on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Yes. Of course, ideas don't die. Only people die. And-

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: That's true, but-

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And Psyche is a productive project. It's just probably not one that is going to

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: converge to general intelligence. The thing that Wittgenstein couldn't solve,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: and he looked at this in his book at the end of his life, Philosophical Investigations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: was the notion of images. So images play an important role in tractatus. The tractatus

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: is an attempt to basically turn philosophy into logical programming language, to design

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: a logical language in which you can do actual philosophy that's rich enough for doing this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And the difficulty was to deal with perceptual content. And eventually, I think he decided

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: that he was not able to solve it. And I think this preempted the failure of the logitist program

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: in AI. And the solution, as we see it today, is we need more general function approximation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: There are functions, geometric functions, that we learn to approximate that cannot be

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: efficiently expressed and computed in a grammatical language. We can, of course, build automata that

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: go via number theory and so on to learn in algebra and then compute an approximation of this geometry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: But to equate language and geometry is not an efficient way to think about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So functional, well, you kind of just said that neural networks are sort of,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: the approach that neural networks takes is actually more general than what can be expressed through

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Yes. So what can be efficiently expressed through language at the data rates at which

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: we process grammatical language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Okay. So you don't think languages, so you disagree with Wittgenstein that language is

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: not fundamental to...

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: I agree with Wittgenstein. I just agree with the late Wittgenstein. And I also agree with

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: the beauty of the early Wittgenstein. I think that the tractatus itself is probably the most

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: beautiful philosophical text that was written in the 20th century.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: But language is not fundamental to cognition and intelligence and consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So I think that language is a particular way or the natural language that we're using is

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: a particular level of abstraction that we use to communicate with each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: But the languages in which we express geometry are not grammatical languages in the same sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So they work slightly different. They're more general expressions of functions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And I think the general nature of a model is you have a bunch of parameters.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: These have a range. These are the variances of the world. And you have relationships between

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: them which are constraints, which say if certain parameters have these values, then other

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: parameters have to have the following values. And this is a very early insight in computer

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: science. And I think some of the earliest formulations is the Boltzmann machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And the problem with the Boltzmann machine is that it has a measure of whether it's good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: This is basically the end result of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: system, the amount of tension that you have left in the constraints where the constraints don't quite match.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: It's very difficult to, despite having this global measure, to train it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Because as soon as you add more than trivially few elements, parameters into the system,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: it's very difficult to get it settled in the right architecture.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And so the solution that Hinton and Zanowski found was to use a restricted Boltzmann machine,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: which uses the hidden links, the internal links in the Boltzmann machine, and only

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: has basically input and output layer. But this limits the expressivity of the Boltzmann machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So now he builds a network of small of these primitive Boltzmann machines.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And in some sense, you can see almost continuous development from this to the deep learning models

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: that we're using today, even though we don't use Boltzmann machines at this point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: But the idea of the Boltzmann machine is you take this model, you clamp some of the values to perception.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And this forces the entire machine to go into a state that is compatible with the states that you currently perceive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And this state is your model of the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Right. So I think it's a very general way of thinking about models, but we have to use a different approach to make it work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And this is we have to find different networks that train the Boltzmann machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So the mechanism that trains the Boltzmann machine and the mechanism that makes the Boltzmann machine settle into its state

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: are distinct from the constrained architecture of the Boltzmann machine itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: The kind of mechanism that we want to develop, you're saying?

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Yes. So there's the direction in which I think our research is going to go.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: For instance, what you notice in perception is our perceptual models of the world are not probabilistic,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: but possibleistic, which means you should be able to perceive things that are improbable, but possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Perceptual state is valid, not if it's probable, but if it's possible, if it's coherent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So if you see a tiger coming after you should be able to see this even if it's unlikely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And the probability is necessary for convergence of the model.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So given the state of possibilities that is very, very large and a set of perceptual features,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: how should you change the states of the model to get it to converge with your perception?

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: But the space of ideas that are coherent with the context that you're sensing is perhaps not as large.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: I mean, that's perhaps pretty small.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: The degree of coherence that you need to achieve depends, of course, how deep your models go.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: For instance, politics is very simple when you know very little about game theory and human nature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So the younger you are, the more obvious is how politics should work, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Because you get a coherent aesthetics from relatively few inputs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And the more layers you model, the more layers you model reality,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: the harder it gets to satisfy all the constraints.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So the current neural networks are a fundamentally supervised learning system

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: with a feed-forward neural network. You use backpropagation to learn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: What's your intuition about what kind of mechanisms might we move towards to improve the learning procedure?

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: I think one big aspect is going to be meta-learning and architecture search starts in this direction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: In some sense, the first wave of classical AI work by identifying a problem and a possible solution

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: and implementing the solution, right? Program that plays chess.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And right now we are in the second wave of AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So instead of writing the algorithm that implements the solution,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: we write an algorithm that automatically searches for an algorithm that implements the solution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So the learning system in some sense is an algorithm

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: that itself discovers the algorithm that solves the problem, like Go.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Go is too hard to implement the solution by hand,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: but we can implement an algorithm that finds the solution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Let's move to the third stage, right? The third stage would be meta-learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Find an algorithm that discovers a learning algorithm for the given domain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Our brain is probably not a learning system, but a meta-learning system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: This is one way of looking at what we are doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: There is another way if you look at the way our brain is, for instance, implemented.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: There is no central control that tells all the neurons how to wire up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Instead, every neuron is an individual reinforcement learning agent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Every neuron is a single-celled organism that is quite complicated

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: and in some sense quite motivated to get fed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And it gets fed if it fires on average at the right time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And the right time depends on the context that the neuron exists in,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: which is the electrical and chemical environment that it has.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So it basically has to learn a function over its environment

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: that tells us when to fire to get fed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Or if you see it as a reinforcement learning agent,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: every neuron is in some sense making a hypothesis when it sends a signal

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: and tries to pipe a signal through the universe and tries to get positive feedback for it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And the entire thing is set up in such a way that it's robustly self-organizing into a brain,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: which means you start out with different neuron types

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: that have different priors on which hypothesis to test on how to get its reward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And you put them into different concentrations in a certain spatial alignment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And then you entrain it in a particular order.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And as a result, you get a well-organized brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Yeah. So, okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So the brain is a meta-learning system with a bunch of...

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Reinforcing learning agents.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And what... I think you said, but just to clarify,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: where do the... There's no centralized government that tells you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: But it's basically an extraordinary attention that we have for faces.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And for me, a very interesting discovery in the last year was the word spirit

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: because I realized that what spirit actually means is an operating system for an autonomous robot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And when the word was invented, people needed this word.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: But they didn't have robots that they built themselves yet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: The only autonomous robots that were known were people, animals, plants, ecosystems, cities,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And they all had spirits.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: If you pinch the plant in one area, then it's going to have repercussions throughout the plant.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Everything in the plant is in some sense connected into some global aesthetics like in other organisms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: An organism is not a collection of cells. It's a function that tells cells how to behave.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And this function is not implemented as some kind of supernatural thing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: like some morphogenetic field.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: It is an emergent result of the interactions of each cell with each other cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: I wouldn't give advice because I am certainly not an expert, but I can give my thoughts on this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Our brain has solved this problem to some degree. Our brain has lots of individual agents that

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: manage to play together in a way, and they have also many contexts in which other organisms

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: have found ways to solve the problems of cooperation that we don't solve on Twitter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Maybe the solution is to go for an evolutionary approach. Imagine that you have something like

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Reddit or something like Facebook and something like Twitter, and you think about what they have

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: in common. What they have in common? They're companies that in some sense own a protocol.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: This protocol is imposed on a community, and the protocol has different components for

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: monetization, for user management, for user display, for rating, for anonymity, for import

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: of other content, and so on. Now imagine that you take these components of the protocol apart,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: and you do it in some sense like communities within this social network. These communities

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: are allowed to mix and match their protocols and design new ones. For instance, the UI and the UX

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: can be defined by the community. The rules for sharing content across communities can be defined.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: The monetization can be redefined. The way you reward individual users for what can be redefined.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: The way users can represent themselves and to each other can be redefined.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Who could be the redefiner? Can individual human beings build enough intuition to redefine those

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: things? Itself can become part of the protocol. For instance, it could be in some communities,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: it will be a single person that comes up with these things, and others it's a group of friends.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Some might implement a voting scheme that has some interesting weighted voting. Who knows?

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Who knows what will be the best self-organizing principle for this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: But the process can't be automated. I mean, it seems like the brain...

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: It can be automated so people can write a software for this. Eventually, the idea is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: let's not make an assumption about this thing if you don't know what the right solution is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: In those areas, we have no idea whether the right solution will be people designing this ad hoc

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: or machines doing this. Whether you want to enforce compliance by social norms like Wikipedia,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: or with software solutions, or with AI that goes through the posts of people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: or with a legal principle and so on. This is something maybe you need to find out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And so the idea would be if you let the communities evolve and you just control it in such a way that

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: adopt themselves to effectively get the incentives have to die. And the thing about social media is

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101
