metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: dying. One of the things that people really get protests aggressively is when they're censored.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Especially in America, I don't know much about the rest of the world, but the idea of freedom of

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: speech, the idea of censorship is really painful in America. And so what do you think about that

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: having grown up in East Germany? Do you think censorship is an important tool in our brain,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: in the intelligence and in the social networks? So basically, if you're not a good member

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: of the entirety of the system, then you should be blocked away, well, locked away, blocked.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: An important thing is who decides that you are a good member.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Who? Is it distributed or?

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And what is the outcome of the process that decides it, both for the individual and for society at

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: large? For instance, if you have a high trust society, you don't need a lot of surveillance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And the surveillance is even in some sense undermining trust. Because it's basically

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: punishing people that look suspicious when surveyed, but do the right thing anyway.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And the opposite, if you have a low trust society, then surveillance can be a better trade off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And the US is currently making a transition from a relatively high trust or mixed trust society to a

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: low trust society. So surveillance will increase. Another thing is that beliefs are not just inert

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: representations. There are implementations that run code on your brain and change your reality and

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: change the way you interact with each other at some level. And some of the beliefs are just

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: public opinions that we use to display our alignment. So for instance, people might say

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: all cultures are the same and equally good, but still they prefer to live in some cultures over

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: others, very, very strongly so. And it turns out that the cultures are defined by certain rules of

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: interaction. And these rules of interaction lead to different results when you implement them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So if you adhere to certain rules, you get different outcomes in different societies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And this all leads to very tricky situations when people do not have a commitment to shared purpose.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And our societies probably need to rediscover what it means to have a shared purpose

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: and how to make this compatible with a non-totalitarian view.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So in some sense, the US is caught in a conundrum between totalitarianism and diversity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And it doesn't need to how to resolve this. And the solutions that the US has found so far are very

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: crude because it's a very young society that is also under a lot of tension. It seems to me that

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: the US will have to reinvent itself. What do you think, just philosophizing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: It all seems to work pretty crapily. Some things worse than others. Some people argue that

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: communism is the best. Others say, yeah, look at the Soviet Union. Some people argue that

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: anarchy is the best and then completely discarding the positive effects of government.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: There's a lot of arguments. US seems to be doing pretty damn well in the same way

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: in the span of history. There's a respect for human rights, which seems to be a nice feature,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: not a bug. And economically, a lot of growth, a lot of technological development.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: People seem to be relatively kind on the grand scheme of things. What lessons do you draw from

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: that? What kind of government system do you think is good? Ideally, government should not be

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: the more friction you experience, the less effective and efficient the government probably is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: A government, game theoretically, is an agent that imposes an offset on your payout metrics

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: to make your national equilibrium compatible with the common good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Yeah. And these local incentives, everybody does the thing that's locally the best for them,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: but the global outcome is not good. And this is even the case when people care about the global

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: outcome, because regulation mechanisms exist that creates a causal relationship between what I want

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: is then imposing a regulation that for instance makes flying more expensive and it gives incentives

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: for inventing other forms of transportation that are less putting the strain on the environment,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: for instance. So there's so much optimism and so many things you describe, and yet there's the

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: pessimism of you think our civilization is going to come to an end. So that's not a hundred percent

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: probability. Nothing in this world is. So what's the trajectory out of self-destruction? Do you think?

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: I suspect that in some sense we are both too smart and not smart enough, which means we are very good

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: at solving near-term problems. And at the same time, we are unwilling to submit to the

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: imperatives that we would have to follow in if you want to stick around. So that makes it difficult.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: principle compute all these things game theoretically and adapt to it. But if you cannot do this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: because you are like me and you have children, you don't want them to die. You will use any kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: as Aristotle envisions, which basically organisms with cybernetic control. And then he says that

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: there are additional rational principles that humans can discover and everybody can discover

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: them so they are universal. If you are sane, you should understand, you should submit to them

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: because you can rationalize use them. And these principles are roughly, you should be willing to

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: self-regulate correctly. You should be willing to do correct social regulation, it's intra-organismic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: You should be willing to act on your models so you have skin in the game. And you should have

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: goal rationality. You should be choosing the right goals to work on. So basically these three rational

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: principles, goal rationality, he calls prudence or wisdom. Social regulation is justice, the correct

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: social one, and the internal regulation is temperance. And this thing, the willingness

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: to act on your models is courage. And then he says that there are additionally to these four

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: cardinal virtues, three divine virtues. And these three divine virtues cannot be rationalized used,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: but they reveal themselves by the harmony, which means if you assume them and you extrapolate what's

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: going to happen, you will see that they make sense. And it's often been misunderstood as

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: God has to tell you that these are the things, so basically there's something nefarious going on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: The Christian conspiracy forces you to believe some guy with a long beard that they discovered

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: this. So these principles are relatively simple. Again, it's for high-level organization, for the

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: resulting civilization that you form, commitment to unity. So basically you serve this higher,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: larger thing, this structural principle on the next level, and he calls that faith.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Then there needs to be commitment to shared purpose, this is basically this global reward

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: that you try to figure out what that should be and how you can facilitate this. And this is love,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: the commitment to shared purpose is the core of love. You see this sacred thing that is more

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: important than your own organismic interests in the other, and you serve this together. And this

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: is how you see the sacred in the other. And the last one is hope, which means you need to be willing

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: to act on that principle without getting rewards in the here and now, because it doesn't exist yet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Then you start out building the civilization. So you need to be able to do this in the absence

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: of its actual existence yet. So it can come into being. So the way it comes into being is by you

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: accepting those notions, and then you see these three divine concepts and you see them realized.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Now the problem is divine is a loaded concept in our world, because we are outside of this cult

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: and we are still scarred from breaking free of it. But the idea is basically we need to have a

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: civilization that acts as an intentional agent, like an insect state. And we are not actually a

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: tribal species, we are a state building species. And what enabled state building is basically

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: the formation of religious states and other forms of rule-based administration in which the individual

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: doesn't matter as much as the rule or the higher goal. We got there by the question, what's the

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: optimal form of governance? So I don't think that Catholicism is the optimal form of governance,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: because it's obviously on the way out. So it is for the present type of society that we are in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Religious institutions don't seem to be optimal to organize that. So what we discovered right now

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: that we live in in the West is democracy. And democracy is the rule of oligarchs that are the

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: people that currently own the means of production that is administered not by the oligarchs

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: themselves, because there's too much disruption, right? We have so much innovation that we have

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: in every generation new means of production that we invent. And corporations die usually after 30

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: years or so and something other takes a leading role in our societies. So it's administered by

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: institutions. And these institutions themselves are not elected, but they provide continuity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And they are led by electable politicians. And this makes it possible that you can adapt to

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: change without having to kill people, right? So you can, for instance, have a change in

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: governments. If people think that the current government is too corrupt or is not up to date,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: you can just elect new people. Or if a journalist finds out something inconvenient about

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: the institution and the institution has no plan B, like in Russia, the journalist has to die.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: This is what when you run society by the deep state. So ideally, you have an administration layer

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: that you can change if something bad happens, right? So you will have a continuity in the whole

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: thing. And this is the system that we came up in in the West. And the way it's set up in the US

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: is largely result of low level models. So it's mostly just second, third order consequences that

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: people are modeling in the design of these institutions. It's a relatively young society

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: that doesn't really take care of the downstream effects of many of the decisions that are being

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: made. And I suspect that AI can help us this in a way if you can fix the incentives. The society

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: of the US is a society of cheaters. It's basically cheating is so indistinguishable from innovation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: and we want to encourage innovation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Can you elaborate on what you mean by cheating?

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: It's basically people do things that they know are wrong. It's acceptable to do things that you

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: know are wrong in the society to a certain degree. You can, for instance, suggest some

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: non-sustainable business models and implement them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Right, but you're always pushing the boundaries. I mean, you're-

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Yes. And yes, this is seen as a good thing, largely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And this is different from other societies. So for instance, social mobility is an aspect of this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Social mobility is the result of individual innovation that would not be sustainable at

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: scale for everybody else. Normally, you should not go up, you should go deep, right? We need

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: bakers, and indeed we are very good bakers, but in a society that innovates, maybe you can replace

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: all the bakers with a really good machine. That's not a bad thing, and it's a thing that made the US

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: so successful, right? But it also means that the US is not optimizing for sustainability, but for

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: innovation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And so it's not obvious as the evolutionary process is unrolling, it's not obvious that

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: that long-term would be better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: It has side effects. So basically, if you cheat, you will have a certain layer of toxic sludge

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: that covers everything that is a result of cheating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And we have to unroll this evolutionary process to figure out if these side effects are so damaging

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: that the system is horrible, or if the benefits actually outweigh the negative effects.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: How do we get to the which system of government is best? That was from- I'm trying to trace back

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: the last five minutes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: I suspect that we can find a way back to AI by thinking about the way in which our brain

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: has to organize itself. In some sense, our brain is a society of neurons, and our mind is a society

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: of behaviors. And they need to be organizing themselves into a structure that implements

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: regulation, and government is social regulation. We often see government as the manifestation of

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: power or local interests, but it's actually a platform for negotiating the conditions of

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: human survival. And this platform emerges over the current needs and possibilities and the

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: trajectory that we have. So given the present state, there are only so many options on how we

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: can move into the next state without completely disrupting everything. And we mostly agree that

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: it's a bad idea to disrupt everything because it will endanger our food supply for a while and the

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: entire infrastructure and fabric of society. So we do try to find natural transitions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And there are not that many natural transitions available at any given point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: What do you mean by natural transitions?

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So we try not to have revolutions if we can help it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Right. So speaking of revolutions and the connection between government systems and the

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: mind, you've also said that in some sense, becoming an adult means you take charge of

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: your emotions. Maybe you never said that. Maybe I just made that up. But in the context of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: mind, what's the role of emotion? And what is it? First of all, what is emotion? What's its role?

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: It's several things. So psychologists often distinguish between emotion and feeling. And

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: in common day parlance, we don't. I think that an emotion is a configuration of the cognitive system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And that's especially true for the lowest level for the affective state. So when you have an affect,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: it's the configuration of certain modulation parameters like arousal, valence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: your attentional focus, whether it's wide or narrow, inter-reception or extra-reception,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: and so on. And all these parameters together put you in a certain way to relate to the environment

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: and to yourself. And this is in some sense an emotional configuration. In the more narrow sense,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: an emotion is an affective state that has an object. And the relevance of that object is

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: given by motivation. And motivation is a bunch of needs that are associated with rewards, things

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: that give you pleasure and pain. And you don't actually act on your needs, you act on models of

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: your needs. Because when the pleasure and pain manifest, it's too late, you've done everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So you act on expectations what will give you pleasure and pain. And these are your purposes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: The needs don't form a hierarchy, they just coexist and compete. And your organism has to,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: your brain has to find a dynamic homeostasis between them. But the purposes need to be

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: consistent. So you basically can create a story for your life and make plans. And so we organize

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: them all into hierarchies. And there is not a unique solution for this. Some people eat to make

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: art and other people make art to eat. They might end up doing the same things, but they cooperate

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: in very different ways. Because their ultimate goals are different and we cooperate based on

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: shared purpose. Everything else that is not cooperation on shared purpose is transactional.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: I don't think I understood that last piece of achieving the homeostasis. Are you distinguishing

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: between the experience of emotion and the expression of emotion?

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Of course. So the experience of emotion is a feeling. And in this sense, what you feel is

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: an appraisal that your perceptual system has made of the situation at hand. And it makes this based

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: on your motivation and on your estimates, not your, but of the subconscious geometric parts of your

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: mind that assess the situation in the world with something like a neural network. And this neural

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: network is making itself known to the symbolic parts of your mind, to your conscious attention

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: by mapping them as features into a space. So what you will feel about your emotion is a projection

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: usually into your body map. So you might feel anxiety in your solar plexus and you might feel

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: it as a contraction, which is all geometry. Your body map is the space that is always instantiated

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: and always available. So it's a very obvious cheat if your non-symbolic parts of your brain

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: try to talk to your symbolic parts of your brain to map the feelings into the body map.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And then you perceive them as pleasant and unpleasant depending on whether the appraisal

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: has a negative or positive valence. And then you have different features of them that give you

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: more knowledge about the nature of what you're feeling. So for instance, when you feel connected

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: to other people, you typically feel this in your chest region around your heart. And you feel this

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: is an expansive feeling in which you are reaching out. And it's very intuitive to encode it like this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: That's why it's encoded like this for most people. It's a code in which the non-symbolic parts of

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: your mind talk to the symbolic ones. And then the expression of emotion is then the final step

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: that could be sort of gestural or visual and so on that's part of the communication.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Probably evolved as part of an adversarial communication. So as soon as you started to

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: observe the facial expression and posture of others to understand what emotional state they are in,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: others started to use this as signaling and also to subvert your model of their emotional state.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So we now look at the inflections, at the difference between the standard face that

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: they're going to make in this situation. When you are at a funeral, everybody expects you to

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: make a solemn face, but the solemn face doesn't express whether you're sad or not. It just

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: expresses that you understand what face you have to make at a funeral. Nobody should know that you

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: are triumphant. So when you try to read the emotion of another person, you try to look at

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: the delta between a truly sad expression and the things that are animating this face behind the

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: curtain. So the interesting thing is, so having done this podcast and the video component,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: one of the things I've learned is that now I'm Russian and I just don't know how to

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: express emotion on my face. One, I see that as weakness, but whatever. The people look to me,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: JG Now, I don't think that God has anything to do with creation. I think it's a mistranslation

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: of the Talmud into the Catholic mythology. I think that Genesis is actually the childhood

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: memories of a God. So the-

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: CB Oh, sorry. Genesis is the-

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: JG The childhood memories of a God. It's basically a mind that is remembering how it came into being.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And we typically interpret Genesis as the creation of a physical universe by a supernatural being.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: CB Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: JG And I think when you read it, there is light and darkness that is being created,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: and then you discover sky and ground, create them. You construct the plants and the animals,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: and you give everything their names and so on. That's basically cognitive development. It's a

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: sequence of steps that every mind has to go through when it makes sense of the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And when you have children, you can see how initially they distinguish light and darkness,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: and then they make out directions in it, and they discover sky and ground, and they discover

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: the plants and the animals, and they give everything their name. And it's a creative

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: process that happens in every mind, because it's not given, right? Your mind has to

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: invent these structures to make sense of the patterns on your retina.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Also, if there was some big nerd who set up a server and runs this world on it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: this would not create a special relationship between us and the nerd. This nerd would not

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: have the magical power to give meaning to our existence, right? So this equation of a creator

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: god with the god of meaning is a slate of hand. You shouldn't do it. The other one that is done

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: in Catholicism is the equation of the first mover, the prime mover of Aristotle, which is basically

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: the automaton that runs the universe. Aristotle says, if things are moving and things seem to be

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: moving here, something must move them, right? If something moves them, something must move the

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: thing that is moving it, so there must be a prime mover. This idea to say that this prime

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: mover is a supernatural being is complete nonsense, right? It's an automaton in the simplest case.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: So we have to explain the enormity that this automaton exists at all. But again,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: we don't have any possibility to infer anything about its properties except that it's able to

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: produce change in information, right? So there needs to be some kind of computational principle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: This is all there is. But to say this automaton is identical again with the creator of first

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: cause or with the thing that gives meaning to our life is confusion. No, I think that what we

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: perceive is the higher being that we are part of. And the higher being that we are part of is the

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: civilization. It's the thing in which we have a similar relationship as the cell has to our body.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: And we have this prior because we have evolved to organize in these structures. So basically,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: the Christian God in its natural form without the mythology, if you undress it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: is basically the platonic form of the civilization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: Is the ideal- Yes, it's this ideal that you try to approximate when you interact with others,

metadata.title: Podcast: Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #101

body.input: not based on your incentives, but on what you think is right.

body.input: And now here's my conversation with Nick Bostrom.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: At the risk of asking the Beatles to play yesterday or the Rolling Stones to play Satisfaction,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: let me ask you the basics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: What is the simulation hypothesis?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: That we are living in a computer simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: What is a computer simulation?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: How are we supposed to even think about that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, so the hypothesis is meant to be understood in a literal sense, not that we can kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: metaphorically view the universe as an information processing physical system, but that there

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: is some advanced civilization who built a lot of computers and that what we experience

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: is an effect of what's going on inside one of those computers so that the world around

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: us, our own brains, everything we see and perceive and think and feel would exist because

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: this computer is running certain programs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So do you think of this computer as something similar to the computers of today, these deterministic

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: sort of touring machine type things?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Is that what we're supposed to imagine or we're supposed to think of something more

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: like a quantum mechanical system, something much bigger, something much more complicated,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: something much more mysterious from our current perspective?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: The ones we have today would do fine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, bigger, certainly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You'd need more memory and more processing power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I don't think anything else would be required.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Now, it might well be that they do have additional, maybe they have quantum computers and other

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: things that would give them even more oomph.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It seems kind of plausible, but I don't think it's a necessary assumption in order to get

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: to the conclusion that a technologically mature civilization would be able to create these

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: kinds of computer simulations with conscious beings inside them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So do you think the simulation hypothesis is an idea that's most useful in philosophy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: computer science, physics?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Or do you see it having valuable kind of starting point in terms of the thought experiment of

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Is it useful?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I guess it's more informative and interesting and maybe important, but it's not designed

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: to be useful for something else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Okay, interesting, sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But is it philosophically interesting or is there some kind of implications of computer

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: science and physics?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I think not so much for computer science or physics per se.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Certainly it would be of interest in philosophy, I think also to say cosmology or physics in

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: as much as you're interested in the fundamental building blocks of the world and the rules

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: that govern it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: If we are in a simulation, there is then the possibility that say physics at the level

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: where the computer running the simulation could be different from the physics governing

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: phenomena in the simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So I think it might be interesting from point of view of religion or just for kind of trying

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: to figure out what the heck is going on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So we mentioned the simulation hypothesis so far.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: There is also the simulation argument, which I tend to make a distinction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So simulation hypothesis, we are living in a computer simulation argument.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: This argument that tries to show that one of three propositions is true, one of which

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: is the simulation hypothesis, but there are two alternatives in the original simulation

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: argument which we can get to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, let's go there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: By the way, confusing terms because people will I think probably naturally think simulation

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: argument equals simulation hypothesis just terminology wise, but let's go there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So simulation hypothesis means that we are living in a simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: The hypothesis that we're living in a simulation argument has these three complete possibilities

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: that cover all possibilities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So what are they?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, so it's like a disjunction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It says at least one of these three is true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Although it doesn't on its own tell us which one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So the first one is that almost all civilizations at our current stage of technological development

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: go extinct before they reach technological maturity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So there is some great filter that makes it so that basically none of the civilizations

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: throughout maybe vast cosmos will ever get to realize the full potential of technological

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: development.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So theoretically speaking, this could be because most civilizations kill themselves too eagerly

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: or destroy themselves too eagerly, or it might be super difficult to build a simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So the span of time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Theoretically it could be both.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Now, I think it looks like we would technologically be able to get there in a time span that is

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: short compared to say the lifetime of planets and other sort of astronomical processes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So your intuition is to build a simulation is not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, so this is interesting concept of technological maturity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It's kind of an interesting concept to have other purposes as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: We can see even based on our current limited understanding what some lower bound would

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: be on the capabilities that you could realize by just developing technologies that we already

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: see are possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So for example, one of my research fellows here, Eric Drexler back in the eighties studied

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: molecular manufacturing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: That is you could analyze using theoretical tools and computer modeling the performance

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: of various molecularly precise structures that we didn't then and still don't today have

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: the ability to actually fabricate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But you could say that, well, if we could put these atoms together in this way, then

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: the system would be stable and it would rotate at this speed and have these computational

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: characteristics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And he also outlined some pathways that would enable us to get to this kind of molecularly

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: manufacturing in the fullness of time and you could do other studies we've done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You can look at the speed at which say it would be possible to colonize the galaxy if

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: you had mature technology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: We have an upper limit, which is the speed of light.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: We have sort of a lower current limit, which is how fast current rockets go.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: We know we can go faster than that by just making them bigger and have more fuel and

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So we could then start to describe the technological affordances that would exist once a civilization

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: has had enough time to develop, at least those technologies we already know are possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Then maybe they would discover other new physical phenomena as well that we haven't realized

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: that would enable them to do even more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But at least there is this kind of basic set of capabilities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Can you just linger on that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: How do we jump from molecular manufacturing to deep space exploration to mature technology?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: What's the connection there?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, so these would be two examples of technological capability sets that we can have a high degree

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: of confidence are physically possible in our universe and that a civilization that was

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: allowed to continue to develop its science and technology would eventually attain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You can intuit, we can kind of see the set of breakthroughs that are likely to happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You can see, what did you call it, the technological set?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: With computers, maybe it's easiest.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: One is we could just imagine bigger computers using exactly the same parts that we have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So you can kind of scale things that way, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But you could also make processors a bit faster.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: If you had this molecular nanotechnology that Eric Brextor described, he characterized a

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: kind of crude computer built with these parts that would perform at a million times the

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: human brain while being significantly smaller, the size of a sugar cube.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And he made no claim that that's the optimum computing structure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Like for all to know, we could build a faster computers that will be more efficient, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: at least you could do that if you had the ability to do things that were atomically

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: precise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So you can then combine these two.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You could have this kind of nanomolecular ability to build things atom by atom and then

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: say, at this spatial scale that would be attainable through space colonizing technology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You could then start, for example, to characterize a lower bound on the amount of computing power

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: that a technologically mature civilization would have if it could grab resources, planets

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: and so forth, and then use this molecular nanotechnology to optimize them for computing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You'd get a very, very high lower bound on the amount of compute.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So sorry, just to define some terms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So technologically mature civilization is one that took that piece of technology to

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: its lower bound.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: What is a technologically mature civilization?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So that means it's a stronger concept than we really need for the simulation hypothesis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I just think it's interesting in its own right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So it would be the idea that there is some stage of technological development where you

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: basically maxed out, that you developed all those general purpose, widely useful technologies

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: that could be developed, or at least kind of come very close to the 99.9% there or something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So that's an independent question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You can think either that there is such a ceiling or you might think the technology

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: tree just goes on forever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Where does your sense fall?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I would guess that there is a maximum that you would start to asymptote towards.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So new things won't keep springing up, new ceilings.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: In terms of basic technological capabilities, I think there is like a finite set of those

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: that can exist in this universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Moreover, I wouldn't be that surprised if we actually reached close to that level fairly

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: shortly after we have say machine superintelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So I don't think it would take millions of years for a human originating civilization

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: to begin to do this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It's more likely to happen on historical timescales.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But that's an independent speculation from the simulation argument.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, for the purpose of the simulation argument, it doesn't really matter whether

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: it goes indefinitely far up or whether there is a ceiling, as long as we know we can at

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: least get to a certain level.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And it also doesn't matter whether that's going to happen in 100 years or 5,000 years

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: or 50 million years.
