metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Like the timescales really don't make any difference for this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Can you link on that a little bit?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Like there's a big difference between 100 years and 10 million years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So it doesn't really not matter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Because you just said, it doesn't matter if we jump scales to beyond historical scales.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So we described that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So for the simulation argument, doesn't it matter that if it takes 10 million years,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: it gives us a lot more opportunity to destroy civilization in the meantime?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, well, so it would shift around the probabilities between these three alternatives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: That is, if we are very, very far away from being able to create these simulations, if

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: it's like say billions of years into the future, then it's more likely that we will fail ever

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: to get there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: There's more time for us to kind of go extinct along the way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And so similarly for other civilizations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So it is important to think about how hard it is to build a simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: In terms of figuring out which of the disjuncts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But for the simulation argument itself, which is agnostic as to which of these three alternatives

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: is true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, yeah, okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So like the simulation argument would be true whether or not we thought this could be done

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: in 500 years or it would take 500 million years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: No, for sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: The simulation argument stands.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, I'm sure there might be some people who oppose it, but it doesn't matter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It's very nice those three cases cover it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But the fun part is at least not saying what the probabilities are, but kind of thinking

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: about kind of intuiting reasoning about like what's more likely, what are the kind of things

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: that would make some of the arguments less and more so like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But let's actually, I don't think we went through them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So number one is we destroy ourselves before we ever create simulated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So that's kind of sad, but we have to think not just what might destroy us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, so there could be some whatever disasters or meteorite slamming the earth a few years

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: from now that could destroy us, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So you'd have to postulate in order for this first disjunct to be true that almost all

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: civilizations throughout the cosmos also failed to reach technological maturity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And the underlying assumption there is that there is likely a very large number of other

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: intelligent civilizations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, if there are, yeah, then they would virtually all have to succumb in the same

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, then that leads off another, I guess there are a lot of little digressions that

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: are interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Definitely, let's go there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Let's go there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Keep dragging us back.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, there are these, there is a set of basic questions that always come up in conversations

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: with interesting people, like the Fermi paradox.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You could almost define whether a person is interesting, whether at some point the question

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: of the Fermi paradox comes up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, so for what it's worth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It looks to me that the universe is very big.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, in fact, according to the most popular current cosmological theories, infinitely big.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And so then it would follow pretty trivially that it would contain a lot of other civilizations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: In fact, infinitely many.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: If you have some local stochasticity and infinitely many, it's like infinitely many lumps of matter

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: one next to another, there's kind of random stuff in each one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You're going to get all possible outcomes with probability one infinitely repeated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So then certainly there would be a lot of extraterrestrials out there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Even short of that, if the universe is very big, there might be a finite but large number.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: If we were literally the only one, yeah, then of course, if we went extinct, then all of

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: civilizations at our current stage would have gone extinct before becoming technological

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: material.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So then it kind of becomes trivially true that a very high fraction of those went extinct.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But if we think there are many, I mean, it's interesting because there are certain things

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: that plausibly could kill us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: If you look at existential risks, and it might be a different...

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: The best answer to what would be most likely to kill us might be a different answer than

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: the best answer to the question, if there is something that kills almost everyone, what

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: would that be?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Because that would have to be some risk factor that was kind of uniform overall possible

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: civilization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, so for the sake of this argument, you have to think about not just us, but every

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: civilization dies out before they create the simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Or something very close to everybody.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Okay, so what's number two in the...

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, so number two is the convergence hypothesis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Maybe some of these civilizations do make it through to technological maturity, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: out of those who do get there, they all lose interest in creating these simulations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So they have the capability of doing it, but they choose not to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Not just a few of them decide not to, but out of a million, maybe not even a single

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: one of them would do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I think when you say lose interest, that sounds unlikely because it's like they get bored

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: or whatever, but it could be so many possibilities within that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Losing interest could be anything from it being exceptionally difficult to do to fundamentally

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: changing the fabric of reality if you do it, ethical concerns, all those kinds of things

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: could be exceptionally strong pressures.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, certainly, I mean, yeah, ethical concerns.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, not really too difficult to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, in a sense, that's the first assumption that you get to technological maturity where

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: you would have the ability using only a tiny fraction of your resources to create many,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: many simulations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So it wouldn't be the case that they would need to spend half of their GDP forever in

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: order to create one simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And I had this difficult debate about whether they should invest half of their GDP for this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It would more be like, well, if any little fraction of the civilization feels like doing

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: this at any point during maybe their millions of years of existence, then there would be

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: millions of simulations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But certainly, there could be many conceivable reasons for why there would be this convert,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: many possible reasons for not running ancestor simulations or other computer simulations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: even if you could do so cheaply.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: By the way, what's an ancestor simulation?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, that would be the type of computer simulation that would contain people like those we think

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: have lived on our planet in the past and like ourselves in terms of the types of experiences

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: they have and where those simulated people are conscious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So not just simulated in the same sense that a non-player character would be simulated

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: in the current computer game where it kind of has an avatar body and then a very simple

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: mechanism that moves it forward or backwards.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But something where the simulated being has a brain, let's say, that's simulated at a

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: sufficient level of granularity that it would have the same subjective experiences as we

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So where does consciousness fit into this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Do you think simulation, like, is there different ways to think about how this can be simulated

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: just like you're talking about now?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Do we have to simulate each brain within the larger simulation?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Is it enough to simulate just the brain, just the minds and not the big universe itself?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Is there different ways to think about this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I guess there is a kind of premise in the simulation argument rolled in from philosophy

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: of mind that is that it would be possible to create a conscious mind in a computer and

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: that what determines whether some system is conscious or not is not like whether it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: built from organic biological neurons, but maybe something like what the structure of

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: the computation is that it implements.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So we can discuss that if we want, but I think it would be, if it were this way, it might

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: be that it would be sufficient, say, if you had a computation that was identical to the

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: computation in the human brain down to the level of neurons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So if you had a simulation with a hundred billion neurons connected in the same way

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: as the human brain and you then roll that forward with the same kind of synaptic weights

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: and so forth, so you actually had the same behavior coming out of this as a human with

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: that brain would have done, then I think that would be conscious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Now it's possible you could also generate consciousness without having that detailed

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: assimilation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: There, I'm getting more uncertain exactly how much you could simplify or abstract away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Can you look around that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: What do you mean?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I missed where you're placing consciousness in this second.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, so if you are a computationalist, do you think that what creates consciousness

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: is the implementation of a computation?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Some property, emerging property of the computation itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: That's the idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, you could say that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But then the question is what's the class of computations such that when they are run,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: consciousness emerges?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So if you just have something that adds one plus one plus one plus one, like a simple

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: thing, you think maybe that's not going to have any consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: If on the other hand, the computation is one like our human brains are performing where

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: as part of the computation, there is a global workspace, a sophisticated attention mechanism,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: there is self-representations of other cognitive processes and a whole lot of other things

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: that possibly would be conscious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And in fact, if it's exactly like ours, I think definitely it would.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But exactly how much less than the full computation that the human brain is performing would be

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: required is a little bit, I think, of an open question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And he asked another interesting question as well, which is, would it be sufficient

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: to just have say the brain or would you need the environment?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: That's a nice one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: The same kind of experiences that we have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And there is a bunch of stuff we don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, if you look at say current virtual reality environments, one thing that's clear

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: is that we don't have to simulate all details of them all the time in order for say the

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: human player to have the perception that there is a full reality in there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You can have say procedurally generated, which might only render a scene when it's actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: within the view of the player character.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And so similarly, if this environment that we perceive is simulated, it might be that

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: all of the parts that come into our view are rendered at any given time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And a lot of aspects that never come into view, say the details of this microphone,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I'm talking into exactly what each atom is doing at any given point in time might not

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: be part of the simulation, only a more coarse grained representation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So that to me is actually from an engineering perspective, why the simulation hypothesis

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: is really interesting to think about is how difficult is it to fake sort of in a virtual

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: reality context, I don't know if fake is the right word, but to construct a reality that

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: is sufficiently real to us to be immersive in the way that the physical world is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I think that's actually probably an answerable question of psychology, of computer science,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: of where's the line where it becomes so immersive that you don't want to leave that world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, or that you don't realize while you're in it that it is a virtual world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, those are two actually questions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yours is the more sort of the good question about the realism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But mine, from my perspective, what's interesting is it doesn't have to be real, but how can

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: we construct a world that we wouldn't want to leave?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, I mean, I think that might be too low a bar.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, if you think, say when people first had Pong or something like that, I'm sure

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: there were people who wanted to keep playing it for a long time because it was fun and

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: they wanted to be in this little world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I'm not sure we would say it's immersive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, I guess in some sense it is, but like an absorbing activity doesn't even have to

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But they left that world though.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I think that bar is deceivingly high.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You can play Pong or StarCraft or whatever more sophisticated games for hours, for months.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Wow, the world of Warcraft could be in a big addiction, but eventually they escaped that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So you mean when it's absorbing enough that you would choose to spend your entire life

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: in there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And then thereby changing the concept of what reality is because your reality becomes the

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: game, not because you're fooled, but because you've made that choice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, and it made different people might have different preferences regarding that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: People might, even if you had any perfect virtual reality, might still prefer not to

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: spend the rest of their lives there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, in philosophy, there's this experience machine, thought experiment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Have you come across this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So Robert Nozick had this thought experiment where you imagine some crazy super duper neuroscientist

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: of the future have created a machine that could give you any experience you want if

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: you step in there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And for the rest of your life, you can kind of pre-programmed it in different ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So your fondest dreams could come true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You could, whatever you dream, you want to be a great artist, a great lover, have a wonderful

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: life, all of these things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: If you step into the experience machine, will be your experiences, constantly happy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But you would kind of disconnect from the rest of reality and you would float there

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: in a tank.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And so Nozick thought that most people would choose not to enter the experience machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, many might want to go there for a holiday, but they wouldn't want to sort of

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: check out of existence permanently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And so he thought that was an argument against certain views of value according to what we

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: value is a function of what we experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Because in the experience machine, you could have any experience you want and yet many

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: people would think that would not be much value.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So therefore, what we value depends on other things than what we experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So okay, can you take that argument further?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: What about the fact that maybe what we value is the up and down of life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So you could have up and downs in the experience machine, but what can't you have in the experience

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: machine?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, that then becomes an interesting question to explore.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But for example, real connection with other people, if the experience machine is a solo

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: machine where it's only you, that's something you wouldn't have there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You would have this subjective experience that would be like fake people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But if you gave somebody flowers, that wouldn't be anybody there who actually got happy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It would just be a little simulation of somebody smiling.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But the simulation would not be the kind of simulation I'm talking about in the simulation

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: argument where the simulated creature is conscious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It would just be a kind of smiley face that would look perfectly real to you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So we're now drawing a distinction between appear to be perfectly real and actually being

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: real.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So that could be one thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, like a big impact on history, maybe it's also something you won't have if you

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: check into this experience machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So some people might actually feel the life I want to have for me is one where I have

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: a big positive impact on how history unfolds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So you could kind of explore these different possible explanations for why it is you wouldn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: want to go into the experience machine if that's what you feel.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And one interesting observation regarding this Nozick thought experiment and the conclusions

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: he wanted to draw from it is how much is a kind of a status quo effect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So a lot of people might not want to get this on current reality to plug into this dream

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But if they instead were told, well, what you've experienced up to this point was a

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: dream.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Now do you want to disconnect from this and enter the real world when you have no idea

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: maybe what the real world is?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Or maybe you could say, well, you're actually a farmer in Peru growing peanuts and you could

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: live for the rest of your life in this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Or would you want to continue your dream life as Alex Friedman going around the world, making

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: podcasts and doing research?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So if the status quo was that they were actually in the experience machine, I think a lot of

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: people might prefer to live the life that they are familiar with rather than sort of

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: bail out into.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So essentially the change itself, the leap.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So it might not be so much the reality itself that we're after, but it's more that we are

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: maybe involved in certain projects and relationships and we have a self identity and these things

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: that our values are kind of connected with carrying that forward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And then whether it's inside a tank or outside a tank in Peru or whether inside a computer

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: or outside a computer, that's kind of less important to what we ultimately care about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But still, so just to linger on it, it is interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I find maybe people are different, but I find myself quite willing to take the leap to the

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: farmer in Peru, especially as the virtual reality system become more realistic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I find that possibility and I think more people would take that leap.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But in this thought experiment, just to make sure we are understanding, so in this case,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: the farmer in Peru would not be a virtual reality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: That would be the real, your life before this whole experience machine started.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, I kind of assumed from that description, you're being very specific, but that kind

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: of idea just like washes away the concept of what's real.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, I'm still a little hesitant about your kind of distinction between real and

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: illusion, because when you can have an illusion that's feels, I mean, that looks real, I mean,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: what I don't know how you can definitively say something is real or not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Like what's a good way to prove that something is real in that context?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, so I guess in this case, it's more a stipulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: In one case, you're floating in a tank with these wires by the super duper neuroscientists

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: plugging into your head, giving you Lex Friedman experiences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: In the other, you're actually tilling the soil in Peru, growing peanuts, and then those

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: peanuts are being eaten by other people all around the world who buy the exports.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So these are two different possible situations in the one and the same real world that you

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: could choose to occupy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But just to be clear, when you're in a vat with wires and the neuroscientists, you can

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: still go farming in Peru, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: No, well, if you wanted, you could have the experience of farming in Peru, but there wouldn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: actually be any peanuts grown.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But what makes a peanut...

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So a peanut could be grown and you could feed things with that peanut.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And why can't all of that be done in a simulation?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I hope first of all that they actually have peanut farms in Peru.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I guess we'll get a lot of comments otherwise from Angri.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I was way up to the point when you started talking about Peru peanuts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You should know you can't grow peanuts in that climate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: No, I mean, in the simulation, I think there is a sense, the important sense in which it

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: would all be real.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Nevertheless, there is a distinction between inside a simulation and outside a simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Or in the case of no six thought experiment, whether you're in the vat or outside the vat,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: and some of those differences may or may not be important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, that comes down to your values and preferences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So if the experience machine only gives you the experience of growing peanuts, but you're

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: the only one in the experience machines.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: No, but there's other...

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Within the experience machine, others can plug in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, there are versions of the experience machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So in fact, you might want to have distinguished different thought experiments, different versions

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So like in the original thought experiment, maybe it's only you, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Just you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And you think, I wouldn't want to go in there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, that tells you something interesting about what you value and what you care about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Then you could say, well, what if you add the fact that there would be other people

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: in there and you would interact with them?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, it starts to make it more attractive, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Then you could add in, well, what if you could also have important long-term effects on human

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: history and the world, and you could actually do something useful even though you were in

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: there?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: That makes it maybe even more attractive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You could actually have a life that had a purpose and consequences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So as you sort of add more into it, it becomes more similar to the baseline reality that

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: you were comparing it to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, but I just think inside the experience machine and without taking those steps you

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: just mentioned, you still have an impact on long-term history of the creatures that live

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: inside that, of the quote unquote fake creatures that live inside that experience machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And at a certain point, if there's a person waiting for you inside that experience machine,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: maybe your newly found wife, and she dies, she has fear, she has hopes, and she exists

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: in that machine when you unplug yourself and plug back in, she's still there going on about

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: her life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Oh, well, in that case, yeah, she starts to have more of an independent existence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But it depends, I think, on how she's implemented in the experience machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Take one limit case where all she is is a static picture on the wall of photograph.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So you think, well, I can look at her, but that's it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Then you think, well, it doesn't really matter much what happens to that, any more than a

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: normal photograph if you tear it up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It means you can't see it anymore, but you haven't harmed the person whose picture you

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: tore it up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But if she's actually implemented, say, at a neural level of detail so that she's a fully

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: realized digital mind with the same behavioral repertoire as you have, then very plausibly

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: she would be a conscious person like you are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And then what you do in this experience machine would have real consequences for how this

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: other mind felt.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So you have to specify which of these experience machines you're talking about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I think it's not entirely obvious that it would be possible to have an experience machine

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: that gave you a normal set of human experiences, which include experiences of interacting with

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: other people without that also generating consciousnesses corresponding to those other

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So if you create another entity that you perceive and interact with that to you looks entirely

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: realistic, not just when you say hello, they say hello back, but you have a rich interaction,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: many days, deep conversations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It might be that the only plausible way of implementing that would be one that also as

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: a side effect instantiated this other person in enough detail that you would have a second

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: consciousness there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I think that's to some extent an open question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So you don't think it's possible to fake consciousness and fake intelligence?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, it might be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, I think you can certainly fake.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: If you have a very limited interaction with somebody, you could certainly fake that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: If all you have to go on is somebody said hello to you, that's not enough for you to

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: tell whether that was a real person there or a prerecorded message or a very superficial

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: simulation that has no consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Because that's something easy to fake.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: We could already fake it now, you can record a voice recording.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But if you have a richer set of interactions where you're allowed to ask open-ended questions

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: and probe from different angles that you couldn't give canned answer to all of the possible

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: ways that you could probe it, then it starts to become more plausible that the only way

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: to realize this thing in such a way that you would get the right answer from any of which

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: angle you probed it would be a way of instantiating it where you also instantiated a conscious

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, I'm with you on the intelligence part, but there's something about me that says consciousness

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: is easier to fake.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I've recently gotten my hands on a lot of rubas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Don't ask me why or how.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And I've made them, there's just a nice robotic mobile platform for experiments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And I made them scream and or moan in pain and so on just to see when they're responding

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And it's just a sort of psychological experiment on myself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And I think they appear conscious to me pretty quickly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: To me, at least my brain can be tricked quite easily.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So if I introspect, it's harder for me to be tricked that something is intelligent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So I just have this feeling that inside this experience machine, just saying that you're

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: conscious and having certain qualities of the interaction, like being able to suffer,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: like being able to hurt, like being able to wander about the essence of your own existence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: not actually creating the illusion that you're wandering about it is enough to create the

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: feeling of consciousness and the illusion of consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And because of that, create a really immersive experience to where you feel like that is

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: the real world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Do you think there's a big gap between appearing conscious and being conscious?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Or is it that you think it's very easy to be conscious?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I'm not actually sure what it means to be conscious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: All I'm saying is the illusion of consciousness is enough to create a social interaction that's

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: as good as if the thing was conscious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Meaning, I'm making it about myself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, I guess there are a few different things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: One is how good the interaction is, which might, I mean, if you don't really care about

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: probing hard for whether the thing is conscious, maybe it would be a satisfactory interaction,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: whether or not you really thought it was conscious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Now, if you really care about it being conscious inside this experience machine, how easy would

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: it be to fake it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And you say, it sounds fairly easy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But then the question is, would that also mean it's very easy to instantiate consciousness?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It's much more widely spread in the world than we have thought.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It doesn't require a big human brain with a hundred billion neurons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: All you need is some system that exhibits basic intentionality and can respond and you

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: already have consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: In that case, I guess you still have a close coupling.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I guess that case would be where they can come apart, where you could create the appearance

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: of there being a conscious mind without actually not being another conscious mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, I'm somewhat agnostic exactly where these lines go.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I think one observation that makes it plausible that you could have very realistic appearances

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: relatively simply, which also is relevant for the simulation argument and in terms of

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: thinking about how realistic would a virtual reality model have to be in order for the

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: simulated creature not to notice that anything was awry?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, just think of our own humble brains during the wee hours of the night when we

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: are dreaming.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Many times, well, dreams are very immersive, but often you also don't realize that you're

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: in a dream.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And that's produced by simple, primitive, three-pound lumps of neural matter effortlessly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So if a simple brain like this can create a virtual reality that seems pretty real to

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: us, then how much easier would it be for a super-intelligent civilization with planetary-sized

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: computers optimized over the eons to create a realistic environment for you to interact

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: with?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: By the way, behind that intuition is that our brain is not that impressive relative to the

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: possibilities of what technology could bring.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It's also possible that the brain is the epitome, is the ceiling.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: The ceiling?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: How is that possible?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Meaning this is the smartest possible thing that the universe could create.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So that seems unlikely to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: For some of these reasons we alluded to earlier, in terms of designs we already have for computers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: that would be faster by many orders of magnitude than the human brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, but it could be that the cognitive constraints in themselves is what enables the intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So the more powerful you make the computer, the less likely it is to become super-intelligent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: This is where I say dumb things to push back on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, I'm not sure I follow you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So there are different dimensions of intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: A simple one is just speed, like if you can solve the same challenge faster in some sense,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: you're smarter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So there I think we have very strong evidence for thinking that you could have a computer

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: in this universe that would be much faster than the human brain and therefore have speed

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: super-intelligence, like be completely superior, maybe a million times faster.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Then maybe there are other ways in which you could be smarter as well, maybe more qualitative

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: The concepts are a little bit less clear cut, so it's harder to make a very crisp, neat,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: firmly logical argument for why that could be qualitative super-intelligence as opposed

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: to just things that were faster.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Although I still think it's very plausible for various reasons that are less than watertight

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: arguments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: For example, if you look at animals and even within humans, there seems to be like Einstein

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: versus random person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It's not just that Einstein was a little bit faster, but how long would it take a normal

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: person to invent general relativity?
