metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It's not 20% longer than it took Einstein or something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I don't know whether they would do it at all or it would take millions of years or some

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: totally bizarre.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But your intuition is that the compute size will get you go.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Taking the size of the computer and the speed of the computer might create some much more

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: powerful levels of intelligence that would enable some of the things we've been talking

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: about with the simulation, being able to simulate an ultra-realistic environment, ultra-realistic

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: perception of reality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Strictly speaking, it would not be necessary to have super-intelligence in order to have

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: say the technology to make these ancestors simulations or other kinds of simulations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: As a matter of fact, I think if we are in a simulation, it would most likely be one

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: built by a civilization that had super-intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It certainly would help.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, you could build more efficient, larger scale structures if you had super-intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I also think that if you had the technology to build these simulations, that's like a

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: very advanced technology, it seems kind of easier to get the technology to super-intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So I'd expect by the time they could make these fully realistic simulations of human

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: history with human brains in there, before that, they got to that stage, they would have

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: figured out how to create machine super-intelligence or maybe biological enhancements of their

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: own brains if they were biological creatures to start with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So we talked about the three parts of the simulation argument.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: One, we destroy ourselves before we ever create the simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Two, we somehow, everybody somehow loses interest in creating the simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Three, we're living in a simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So you've kind of, I don't know if your thinking has evolved on this point, but you kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: said that we know so little that these three cases might as well be equally probable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So probabilistically speaking, where do you stand on this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, I mean, I don't think equal necessarily would be the most supported probability assignment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So how would you, without assigning actual numbers, what's more or less likely in your

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: view?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, I mean, I've historically tended to punt on the question of like as between these

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: three.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So maybe you asked me another way is which kind of things would make it each of these

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: more or less likely?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: What kind of intuition?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, certainly in general terms, if you think anything that say increases or reduces

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: the probability of one of these, we tend to slush probability around on the other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So if one becomes less probable like the other would have to, because it's got to add up

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: to one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So if we consider the first hypothesis, the first alternative that there's this filter

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: that makes it so that virtually no civilization reaches technical maturity, in particular

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: our own civilization, if that's true, then it's like very unlikely that we would reach

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: technical maturity, just because if almost no civilization at our stage does it, then

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: it's unlikely that we do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So I had-

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Oh, sorry, can you linger on that for a second?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, so if it's the case that almost all civilizations at our current stage of technical

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: maturity fail to reach maturity, that would give us very strong reason for thinking we

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: will fail to reach technical maturity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Oh, and also sort of the flip side of that is the fact that we've reached it means that

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: many other civilizations have reached this point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, so that means if we get closer and closer to actually reaching technical maturity, there's

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: less and less distance left where we could go extinct before we are there, and therefore

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: the probability that we will reach increases as we get closer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And that would make it less likely to be true that almost all civilizations at our current

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: stage failed to get there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: The one case we'd started ourselves would be very close to getting there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: That would be strong evidence that it's not so hard to get to technical maturity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So to the extent that we feel we are moving nearer to technical maturity, that would tend

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: to reduce the probability of the first alternative and increase the probability of the other

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It doesn't need to be a monotonic change.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: If every once in a while some new threat comes into view, some bad new thing you could do

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: with some novel technology, for example, that could change our probabilities in the other

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: direction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: That technology has to be able to equally, in an even way, affect every civilization

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: out there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, pretty much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Strictly speaking, that could be two different existential risks in every civilization, one

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: or the other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But none of them kills more than 50%.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Gotcha.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Incidentally, some of my other work on machine superintelligence, I pointed to some existential

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: risks related to superintelligent AI and how we must make sure to handle that wisely and

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: carefully.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It's not the right kind of existential catastrophe to make the first alternative true though.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It might be bad for us if the future lost a lot of value as a result of it being shaped

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: by some process that optimized for some completely non-human value.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But even if we got killed by machine superintelligence, that machine superintelligence might still

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: attain technological maturity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Oh, I see.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You're not human exclusive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: This could be any intelligent species that achieves... It's all about the technological

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: maturity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But the humans have to attain it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So superintelligence could replace us and that's just as well for the simulation argument.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It could interact with a second alternative.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: If the thing that replaced us was either more likely or less likely, then we would be to

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: have an interest in creating ancestor simulations that could affect probabilities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But yeah, to a first order, if we all just die, then yeah, we won't produce any simulations

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: because we are dead.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But if we all die and get replaced by some other intelligent thing that then gets to

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: technological maturity, the question remains, of course, if not that thing that used some

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: of its resources to do this stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So can you reason about this stuff?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Because given how little we know about the universe, is it reasonable to reason about

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: these probabilities?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: How little... Well, maybe you can disagree, but to me, it's not trivial to figure out

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: how difficult it is to build a simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: We talked about it a little bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: We also don't know, as we try to start building it, start creating virtual worlds and so on,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: how that changes the fabric of society.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: There's all these things along the way that can fundamentally change just so many aspects

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: of our society, about our existence, that we don't know anything about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: The kind of things we might discover when we understand to a greater degree the fundamental,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: the physics, the theory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: If we have a breakthrough, have a theory and everything, how that changes stuff, how that

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: changes deep space exploration and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Is it still possible to reason about probabilities given how little we know?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I think there will be a large residual of uncertainty that we'll just have to acknowledge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I think that's true for most of these big picture questions that we might wonder about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: We are small, short-lived, small-brained, cognitively very limited humans with little

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: evidence and it's amazing we can figure out as much as we can really about the cosmos.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: There's this cognitive trick that seems to happen when I look at the simulation argument,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: which for me, it seems like case one and two feel unlikely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I want to say feel unlikely as opposed to it's not like I have too much scientific evidence

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: to say that either one or two are not true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It just seems unlikely that every single civilization destroys itself and it feels unlikely that

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: the civilizations lose interest.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Naturally, without necessarily explicitly doing it, but the simulation argument basically

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: says it's very likely we're living in a simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: To me, my mind naturally goes there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I think the mind goes there for a lot of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Is that the incorrect place for it to go?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, not necessarily.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I think the second alternative, which has to do with the motivations and interests of

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: technological and mature civilizations, I think there is much we don't understand about

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Can you talk about that a little bit?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: What do you think?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, this is a question that pops up when you build an AGI system or build a general

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: intelligence or how does that change our motivations?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Do you think it will fundamentally transform our motivations?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, it doesn't seem that implausible that once you take this leap to technological maturity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, I think it involves creating machine superintelligence possibly that would be sort

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: of on the path for basically all civilizations maybe before they are able to create large

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: numbers of ancestor simulations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: That possibly could be one of these things that quite radically changes the orientation

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: of what a civilization is in fact optimizing for.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: There are other things as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: At the moment, we have not perfect control over our own being, our own mental states,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: our own experiences are not under our direct control.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: For example, if you want to experience pleasure and happiness, you might have to do a whole

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: host of things in the external world to try to get into the mental state where you experience

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: pleasure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Like some people get some pleasure from eating great food.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, they can't just turn that on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: They have to kind of actually go to a nice restaurant and then they have to make money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So there's like all this kind of activity that maybe arises from the fact that we are

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: trying to ultimately produce mental states.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But the only way to do that is by a whole host of complicated activities in the external

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Now, at some level of technological development, I think we'll become out of potent in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: sense of gaining direct ability to choose our own internal configuration and enough

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: knowledge and insight to be able to actually do that in a meaningful way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So then it could turn out that there are a lot of instrumental goals that would drop

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: out of the picture and be replaced by other instrumental goals because we could now serve

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: some of these final goals in more direct ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And who knows how all of that shakes out after civilizations reflect on that and converge

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: on different attractors and so on and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And that could be new instrumental considerations that come into view as well that we are just

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: oblivious to that would maybe have a strong shaping effect on actions, like very strong

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: reasons to do something or not to do something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: We just don't realize they are there because we are so dumb, bumbling through the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But if almost inevitably on route to attaining the ability to create many answers to simulations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: you do have this cognitive enhancement or advice from super intelligences or you yourself,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: then maybe there's like this additional set of considerations coming into view and you

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: just realize, ah, it's obvious that the thing that makes sense is to do X.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Whereas right now it seems, oh, you could X, Y or Z and different people will do different

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: things and we are kind of random in that sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Because at this time with our limited technology, the impact of our decisions is minor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, that's starting to change in some ways, but...

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, I'm not sure it follows that the impact of our decisions is minor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, it's starting to change.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, I suppose a hundred years ago was minor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It's starting to...

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, it depends on how you view it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: What people did a hundred years ago still have effects on the world today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Oh, I see.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: As a civilization in the togetherness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So it might be that the greatest impact of individuals is not at technological maturity

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: or very far down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It might be earlier on when there are different tracks, civilization could go down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Maybe the population is smaller.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Things still haven't settled out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: If you count the indirect effects, those could be bigger than the direct effects that people

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: have later on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So part three of the argument says that...

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So that leads us to a place where eventually somebody creates a simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I think you had a conversation with Joe Rogan.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I think there's some aspect here where you got stuck a little bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: How does that lead to likely living in a simulation?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So this kind of probability argument, if somebody eventually creates a simulation, why does that

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: mean that we're now in a simulation?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: What you get to if you accept alternative three first is there would be more simulated

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: people with our kinds of experiences than non-simulated ones.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: If you look at the world as a whole, by the end of time as it were, you just count it

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: up, there would be more simulated ones than non-simulated ones.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Then there is an extra step to get from that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: If you assume that, suppose for the sake of the argument that that's true, how do you

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: get from that to the statement, we are probably in a simulation?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So here you're introducing an indexical statement like it's that this person right now is in

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: a simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: There are all these other people that are in simulations and some that are not in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But what probability should you have that you yourself is one of the simulated ones

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: in this setup?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So yeah, I call it the bland principle of indifference, which is that in cases like this, when you

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: have two sets of observers, one of which is much larger than the other, and you can't

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: from any internal evidence you have tell which set you belong to, you should assign a probability

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: that's proportional to the size of these sets so that if there are 10 times more simulated

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: people with your kinds of experiences, you would be 10 times more likely to be one of

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: those.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Is that as intuitive as it sounds?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: If you don't have enough information, you should rationally just assign the same probability

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: as the size of the set.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It seems pretty plausible to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: What are the holes in this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Is it at the very beginning, the assumption that everything stretches sort of infinite

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: time essentially?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You don't need infinite time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You just need how long does the time take?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: However long it takes, I guess, for a universe to produce an intelligent civilization that

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: then attains the technology to run some ancestry simulations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Gotcha.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It's like when the first simulation is created, that stretch of time just a little longer

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: than they'll all start creating simulations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Kind of like quarter of a minute.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, if you think of there being a lot of different planets and some subset of them

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: have life and then some subset of those get to intelligent life and some of those maybe

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: eventually start creating simulations, they might get started at quite different times.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Maybe on some planet it takes a billion years longer before you get like monkeys or before

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: you get even bacteria than on another planet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: This might happen kind of at different cosmological epochs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Is there a connection here to the doomsday argument and that sampling there?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, there is a connection in that they both involve an application of anthropic reasoning

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: that is reasoning about these kind of indexical propositions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But the assumption you need in the case of the simulation argument is much weaker than

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: the assumption you need to make the doomsday argument go through.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: What is the doomsday argument?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Maybe you can speak to the anthropic reasoning in more general.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, that's a big and interesting topic in its own right, anthropics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But the doomsday argument is this really first discovered by Brandon Carter who was a theoretical

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: physicist and then developed by philosopher John Leslie.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I think it might have been discovered initially in the 70s or 80s and Leslie wrote this book

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I think in 96.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And there are some other versions as well by Richard Gartz who's a physicist, but let's

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: focus on the Carter-Leslie version where it's an argument that we have systematically underestimated

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: the probability that humanity will go extinct soon.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Now I should say most people probably think at the end of the day there is something wrong

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: with this doomsday argument that it doesn't really hold.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It's like there's something wrong with it, but it's proved hard to say exactly what is

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: wrong with it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And different people have different accounts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: My own view is it seems inconclusive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And I can say what the argument is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, that would be good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So maybe it's easiest to explain via an analogy to sampling from urns.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So imagine you have two urns in front of you and they have balls in them that have numbers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: The two urns look the same, but inside one there are 10 balls, ball number one, two,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: three, up to ball number 10.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And then in the other urn you have a million balls numbered one to a million.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And somebody puts one of these urns in front of you and asks you to guess what's the chance

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: it's the 10 ball urn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And you say 50-50, I can't tell which urn it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But then you're allowed to reach in and pick a ball at random from the urn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And that's suppose you find that it's ball number seven.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So that's strong evidence for the 10 ball hypothesis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It's a lot more likely that you would get such a low numbered ball if there are only

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: 10 balls in the urn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It's in fact 10% then, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Then if there are a million balls, it would be very unlikely you would get number seven.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So you perform a Bayesian update and if your prior was 50-50 that it was the 10 ball urn,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: you become virtually certain after finding the random sample was seven that it only has

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: 10 balls in it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So in the case of the urns, this is uncontroversial, just elementary probability theory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: The Doomsday argument says that you should reason in a similar way with respect to different

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: hypotheses about how many balls there will be in the urn of humanity as it were, how

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: many humans there will have been by the time we go extinct.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So to simplify, let's suppose we only consider two hypotheses, either maybe 200 billion humans

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: in total or 200 trillion humans in total.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You could fill in more hypotheses, but it doesn't change the principle here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So it's easiest to see if we just consider these two.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So you start with some prior based on ordinary empirical ideas about threats to civilization

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And maybe you say it's a 5% chance that we will go extinct by the time there will have

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: been 200 billion only.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Kind of optimistic, let's say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You think probably we'll make it through colonized the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But then according to this Doomsday argument, you should think of your own birth rank as

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: a random sample.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So your birth rank is your sequence in the position of all humans that have ever existed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It turns out you're about a human number of 100 billion, give or take.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: That's roughly how many people have been born before you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: That's fascinating because we each have a number.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: We would each have a number in this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Obviously the exact number would depend on where you started counting, like which ancestor

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: was human enough to count as human.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But those are not really important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: They're relatively few of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So yeah, so you're roughly 100 billion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Now if they're only going to be 200 billion in total, that's a perfectly unremarkable

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: number.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You're somewhere in the middle, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It's run of the mill human, completely unsurprising.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Now if they're going to be 200 trillion, you would be remarkably early.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: What are the chances out of these 200 trillion human that you should be human number 100

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: billion?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: That seems it would have a much lower conditional probability.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And so analogously to how in the urn case you thought after finding this low numbered

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: random sample, you updated in favor of the urn having few balls.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Similarly, in this case you should update in favor of the human species having a lower

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: total number of members.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: That is doom soon.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You said doom soon?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, that would be the hypothesis in this case that it will end at 100 billion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I just like that term for that hypothesis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So what it kind of crucially relies on, the doomsday argument, is the idea that you should

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: reason as if you were a random sample from the set of all humans that will ever have

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: existed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: If you have that assumption, then I think the rest kind of follows.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: The question then is why should you make that assumption?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: In fact, you know you're 100 billion, so where do you get this prior?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And then there is like a literature on that with different ways of supporting that assumption.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: That's just one example of anthropic reasoning, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: That seems to be kind of convenient when you think about humanity, when you think about

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: sort of even like existential threats and so on, is it seems that quite naturally that

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: you should assume that you're just an average case.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, that you're kind of a typical randomly sample.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Now in the case of the doomsday argument, it seems to lead to what intuitively we think

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: is the wrong conclusion, or at least many people have this reaction, that there's got

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: to be something fishy about this argument because from very, very weak premises, it

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: gets this very striking implication that we have almost no chance of reaching size 200

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: trillion humans in the future, and how could we possibly get there just by reflecting on

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: when we were born?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It seems you would need sophisticated arguments about the impossibility of space colonization,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: blah, blah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So one might be tempted to reject this key assumption.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I call it the self-sampling assumption, the idea that you should reason as if you were

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: a random sample from all observers or in your some reference class.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: However, it turns out that in other domains, it looks like we need something like this

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: self-sampling assumption to make sense of bona fide scientific inferences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: In contemporary cosmology, for example, you have these multiverse theories, and according

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: to a lot of those, all possible human observations are made.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, if you have a sufficiently large universe, you will have a lot of people observing all

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: kinds of different things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So if you have two competing theories, say about the value of some constant, it could

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: be true according to both of these theories that there will be some observers observing

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: the value that corresponds to the other theory, because there will be some observers that

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: have hallucinations, so there's a local fluctuation or a statistically anomalous measurement.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: These things will happen, and if enough observers make enough different observations, there

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: will be some that by chance make these different ones.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: What we would want to say is, well, many more observers, a larger proportion of the observers

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: will observe as if it were the true value, and a few will observe the wrong value.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: If we think of ourselves as a random sample, we should expect with our own probability

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: to observe the true value, and that will then allow us to conclude that the evidence we

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: actually have is evidence for the theories we think are supported.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It kind of is a way of making sense of these inferences that clearly seem correct, that

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: we can make various observations and infer what the temperature of the cosmic background

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: is and the fine structure constant and all of this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But it seems that without rolling in some assumption similar to the self-sampling assumption,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: this inference just doesn't go through.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And there are other examples.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: There are these scientific contexts where it looks like this kind of anthropic reasoning

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: is needed and makes perfect sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And yet, in the case of the Doobster argument, it has this weird consequence, and people

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: might think there's something wrong with it there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So there's then this project that would consist in trying to figure out what are the legitimate

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: ways of reasoning about these indexical facts when observer selection effects are in play.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: In other words, developing a theory of anthropics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And there are different views of looking at that, and it's a difficult methodological

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: area.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But to tie it back to the simulation argument, the key assumption there, this bland principle

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: of indifference, is much weaker than the self-sampling assumption.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So if you think about in the case of the Doobster argument, it says you should reason as if

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: you are a random sample from all humans that will have ever lived, even though in fact

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: you know that you are about number 100 billionth human and you're alive in the year 2020.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Whereas in the case of the simulation argument, it says that, well, if you actually have no

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: way of telling which one you are, then you should assign this kind of uniform probability.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Your role as the observer in the simulation argument is different, it seems like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Who is the observer?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I keep assigning the individual consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, I mean, when you say you, but a lot of observers in the context of the simulation

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: argument, the relevant observers would be A, the people in original histories, and B,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: the people in simulations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So this would be the class of observers that we need.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, they're also maybe the simulators, but we can set those aside for this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So the question is, given that class of observers, a small set of original history observers

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: and the large class of simulated observers, which one should you think is you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Where are you amongst this set of observers?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Maybe having a little bit of trouble wrapping my head around the intricacies of what it

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: means to be an observer in the different instantiations of the anthropic reasoning cases that we mentioned.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, does it have to be-

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, maybe an easier way of putting it is just like, are you simulated or are you

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: not simulated, given this assumption that these two groups of people exist?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, in the simulation case, it seems pretty straightforward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, so the key point is the methodological assumption you need to make to get the simulation

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: argument to where it wants to go is much weaker and less problematic than the methodological

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: assumption you need to make to get the Doomsday argument to its conclusion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Maybe the Doomsday argument is sound or unsound, but you need to make a much stronger and more

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: controversial assumption to make it go through.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: In the case of the simulation argument, I guess one maybe way intuition popped to support

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: this bland principle of indifference is to consider a sequence of different cases where

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: the fraction of people who are simulated to non-simulated approaches one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: In the limiting case where everybody is simulated, obviously you can deduce with certainty that

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: you are simulated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: If everybody with your experiences is simulated, then you know you've got to be one of those.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You don't need a probability at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You just kind of logically conclude it, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So then as we move from a case where say 90% of everybody is simulated, 99.9%, it should

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: seem possible that the probability you assign should approach one certainty as the fraction

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: approaches the case where everybody is in a simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You wouldn't expect that to be a discrete, well, if there's one non-simulated person,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: then it's 50-50, but if we move that, then it's 100%.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: There are other arguments as well one can use to support this bland principle of indifference,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: but that might be enough too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But in general, when you start from time equals zero and go into the future, the fraction

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: of simulated, if it's possible to create simulated worlds, the fraction of simulated worlds will

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: go to one.

body.input: Well, it won't.

body.input: Is that an obvious kind of thing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It won't go all the way to one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: In reality, that would be some ratio.

body.input: It probably wouldn't be able to run infinitely many.

body.input: If we take say the observed, the physics in the observed universe, if we assume that that's

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: processing that any one civilization could perform in its future trajectory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Right.

body.input: Well, first of all, there's limited amount of matter you can get your hands off because

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: There's a finite sphere of stuff, even if you travel with the speed of light that you

body.input: And then if you think there is a lower limit to the amount of loss you get when you perform
