metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: In those simulations that only include a subset, it might be more likely that they would include

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: subsets of people with unusually interesting or consequential lives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So if you're Elon Musk, it's more likely that you're an inspiration.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Like if you're Donald Trump or if you're Bill Gates or you're some particularly distinctive

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: character, you might think that that add...

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: If you just think of yourself into the shoes, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It's got to be like an extra reason to think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: That's kind of...

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So on a scale of farmer in Peru to Elon Musk, the more you get towards the Elon Musk, the

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: higher the probability...

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You'd imagine that would be some extra boost from that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: There's an extra boost.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So he also asked the question of what he would ask an AGI saying, the question being what's

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: outside the simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Do you think about the answer to this question?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: If we are living in a simulation, what is outside the simulation?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So the programmer of the simulation?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, I think it connects to the question of what's inside the simulation in that if

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: you had views about the creators of the simulation, it might help you make predictions about what

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: kind of simulation it is, what might happen, what happens after the simulation if there

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: is some after, but also like the kind of setup.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So these two questions would be quite closely intertwined.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But do you think it would be very surprising to...

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Is the stuff inside the simulation, is it possible for it to be fundamentally different

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: than the stuff outside?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Another way to put it, can the creatures inside the simulation be smart enough to even understand

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: or have the cognitive capabilities or any kind of information processing capabilities

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: enough to understand the mechanism that created them?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: They might understand some aspects of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, it's a level of...

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It's kind of a level of explanation, like degrees to which you can understand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So does your dog understand what it is to be human?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, it's got some idea, like humans are these physical objects that move around and

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: do things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And a normal human would have a deeper understanding of what it is to be a human.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And maybe some very experienced psychologists or great novelists might understand a little

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: bit more about what it is to be human.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And maybe superintelligence could see right through your soul.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So similarly, I do think that we are quite limited in our ability to understand all of

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: the relevant aspects of the larger context that we exist in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But there might be hope for some.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I think we understand some aspects of it, but how much good is that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: If there's one key aspect that changes the significance of all the other aspects.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So we understand maybe seven out of 10 key insights that you need.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But the answer actually varies completely depending on what number eight, nine, and

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: 10 insight is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Just like whether you want to suppose that the big task were to guess whether a certain

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: number was odd or even, like a 10-digit number.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And if it's even, the best thing for you to do in life is to go north.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And if it's odd, the best thing for you is to go south.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Now we are in a situation where maybe through our science and philosophy, we figured out

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: what the first seven digits are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So we have a lot of information, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Most of it we figured out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But we are clueless about what the last three digits are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So we are still completely clueless about whether the number is odd or even, and therefore

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: whether we should go north or go south.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I feel that's an analogy, but I feel we're somewhat in that predicament.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: We know a lot about the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: We've come maybe more than half of the way there to fully understanding it, but the parts

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: we're missing are plausibly ones that could completely change the overall upshot of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: thing and including change our overall view about what the scheme of priorities should

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: be or which strategic direction would make sense to pursue.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I think your analogy of us being the dog trying to understand human beings is an entertaining

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: one and probably correct.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: The closer the understanding tends from the dog's viewpoint to a human psychologist's

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: viewpoint, the steps along the way there will have completely transformative ideas of what

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: it means to be human.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So the dog has a very shallow understanding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It's interesting to think that, to analogize that a dog's understanding of a human being

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: is the same as our current understanding of the fundamental laws of physics in the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Oh man.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: We spent an hour and 40 minutes talking about the simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I like it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Let's talk about super intelligence, at least for a little bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And let's start with the basics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: What to you is intelligence?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I tend not to get too stuck with the definitional question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, the common sense to understand, like the ability to solve complex problems, to

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: learn from experience, to plan, to reason, some combination of things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Is consciousness mixed up into that or no?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Is consciousness mixed up into that or is it-

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, I think it could be fairly intelligent, at least without being conscious probably.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So then what is super intelligence?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So-

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: That would be like something that was much more-

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Had much more general cognitive capacity than we humans have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So if we talk about general super intelligence, it would be much faster learner be able to

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: reason much better, make plans that are more effective at achieving its goals, say in a

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: wide range of complex challenging environments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: In terms of, as we turn our eye to the idea of sort of existential threats from super

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: intelligence, do you think super intelligence has to exist in the physical world or can

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: it be digital only?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: We think of our general intelligence as us humans, as an intelligence that's associated

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: with the body, that's able to interact with the world, that's able to affect the world

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: directly with physically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, digital only is perfectly fine, I think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It's physical in the sense that obviously the computers and the memories are physical.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But its capability to affect the world sort of-

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Could be very strong, even if it has a limited set of actuators.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: If it can types text on the screen or something like that, that would be, I think, ample.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So in terms of the concerns of existential threat of AI, how can an AI system that's

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: in the digital world have existential risk?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: What are the attack vectors for digital system?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, I guess maybe to take one step back, I should emphasize that I also think there's

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: this huge positive potential from machine intelligence, including super intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I want to stress that because some of my writing has focused on what can go wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: When I wrote the book Super Intelligence, at that point, I felt there was a kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: neglect of what would happen if AI succeeds, and in particular, a need to get a more granular

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: understanding of where the pitfalls are so we can avoid them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I think that since the book came out in 2014, there has been a much wider recognition of

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And a number of research groups are now actually working on developing, say, AI alignment techniques

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: and so on and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So I think now it's important to make sure we bring back onto the table the upside as

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And there's a little bit of a neglect now on the upside.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: If you look at, I was talking to a friend, if you look at the amount of information that

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: is available, or people talking, or people being excited about the positive possibilities

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: of general intelligence, it's far outnumbered by the negative possibilities in terms of

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: our public discourse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Possibly, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It's hard to measure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So what are, can you linger on that for a little bit, what are some, to you, possible

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: big positive impacts of general intelligence, super intelligence?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, I mean, super intelligence, because I tend to also want to distinguish these two

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: different contexts of thinking about AI and AI impacts, the kind of near-term and long-term,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: if you want, both of which I think are legitimate things to think about, and people should discuss

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: both of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But they are different, and they often get mixed up, and then you get confusion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I think you get simultaneously maybe an overhyping of the near-term and then underhyping of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: long-term.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And so I think as long as we keep them apart, we can have two good conversations, or we

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: can mix them together and have one bad conversation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Can you clarify just the two things we're talking about, the near-term and the long-term?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: What are the distinctions?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, it's a blur distinction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But say the things I wrote about in this book, Super Intelligence, long-term, things people

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: are worrying about today with, I don't know, algorithmic discrimination or even things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: self-driving cars and drones and stuff, more near-term.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And then, of course, you could invite in some medium-term where they kind of overlap and

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: one evolves into the other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But I think both, yeah, the issues look kind of somewhat different depending on which of

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: these contexts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So I think it would be nice if we can talk about the long-term and think about a positive

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: impact or a better world because of the existence of the long-term super intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Do you have views of such a world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, I guess it's a little hard to articulate because it seems obvious that the world has

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: a lot of problems as it currently stands.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And it's hard to think of any one of those, which it wouldn't be useful to have a friendly

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: aligned super intelligence working on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So from health to the economic system to be able to sort of improve the investment and

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: trade and foreign policy decisions, all that kind of stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: All that kind of stuff and a lot more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, what's the killer app?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, I don't think there is one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I think AI, especially artificial general intelligence, is really the ultimate general

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: purpose technology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So it's not that there is this one problem, this one area where it will have a big impact,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: but if and when it succeeds, it will really apply across the board in all fields where

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: human creativity and intelligence and problem solving is useful, which is pretty much all

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: fields.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: The thing that it would do is give us a lot more control over nature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It wouldn't automatically solve the problems that arise from conflict between humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Only political problems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Some subset of those might go away if you just had more resources and cooler tech, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: some subset would require coordination that is not automatically achieved just by having

body.input: more technological capability.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But anything that's not of that sort, I think you just get like an enormous boost with this

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: kind of cognitive technology once it goes all the way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: current technology and sometimes things get over height, but those are perfectly consistent

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: views to hold, the ultimate potential being enormous.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And then it's a very different question of how far are we from that or what can we do

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: with near-term technology?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah.

body.input: So what's your intuition about the idea of intelligence explosion?

body.input: When you start to think about that leap from the near-term to the long-term, the natural

body.input: inclination, like for me, sort of building machine learning systems today, it seems like

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: growth, of exponential improvement, of intelligence explosion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, I think we don't know how explosive it will be.

body.input: I think for what it's worth, it seems fairly likely to me that at some point there will

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: be some intelligence explosion, like some period of time where progress in AI becomes

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And just how explosive does something have to be for it to be called an intelligence

body.input: explosion?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But overall, I guess, if you plotted the opinions of different people in the world, I guess

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I would be somewhat more probability towards the intelligence explosion scenario than probably

body.input: had one, people have different views, smart people have different views, there's some

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But it does seem, as far as I'm judging things based on my own impressions, it seems very

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: unlikely that there would be a ceiling at or near human cognitive capacity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And that's such a, I don't know, that's such a special moment.

body.input: And in fact, this is what a number of people are working towards, making sure that we could

body.input: And so I actually misspoke, I didn't mean control.

body.input: I meant, because the control problem is an interesting thing.

body.input: And I think the hope is, at least we should be able to maintain control over systems that

body.input: I think yes, a lot.

body.input: Well, so here it comes to the concept of intelligence and the scale and what human level means.

body.input: One is that we probably would need to make a fairly fundamental rethink of what ultimately

body.input: something that scores really high on the metric of say hedonism and then is like a zero by

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: other criteria, like kind of wireheaded brain synovat.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And it's like a lot of pleasure, that's good, but then like no beauty, no achievement.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Or pick it up, I think to some significant, not unlimited sense, but a significant sense,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: it would be possible to do very well by many criteria.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Maybe you could get like 98% of the best according to several criteria at the same time, given

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: this great expansion of the option space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And so-

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So have competing value systems, competing criteria as a sort of forever, just like our

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Democrat versus Republican, there seems to be this always multiple parties that are useful

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: for our progress in society, even though it might seem dysfunctional inside the moment,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: but having the multiple value systems seems to be beneficial for, I guess, a balance of

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So that's, yeah, not exactly what I have in mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, although it can be in an indirect way it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But that if you had the chance to do something that scored well on several different metrics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: our first instinct should be to do that rather than immediately leap to the thing, which

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: ones of these value systems are we going to screw over?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Like I think our first thing, let's first try to do very well by all of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Then it might be that you can't get the 100% of all and you would have to then like have

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: the hard conversation about which one will only get 97%.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Here's my cynicism that all of existence is always a trade off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But you say, maybe it's not such a bad trade off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Let's first at least try.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, this would be a distinctive context in which at least some of the constraints

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: would be removed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So there's probably still be trade offs in the end.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: It's just that we should first make sure we at least take advantage of this abundance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So in terms of thinking about this, like yeah, one should think I think in this kind of frame

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: of mind of generosity and inclusiveness to different value systems and see how far one

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: can get there first.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And I think one could do something that would be very good according to many different criteria.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: We kind of talked about AGI fundamentally transforming the value system of our existence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: the meaning of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But today, what do you think is the meaning of life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: The silliest or perhaps the biggest question, what's the meaning of life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: What's the meaning of existence?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: What gives your life fulfillment, purpose, happiness, meaning?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, I think these are like, I guess a bunch of different related questions in there that

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: one can ask.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yes, happiness, meaning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I mean, like you could imagine somebody getting a lot of happiness from something that they

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: didn't think was meaningful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Like mindless, like watching reruns of some television series, waiting junk food, like

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: maybe some people that gives pleasure, but they wouldn't think it had a lot of meaning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Whereas conversely, something that might be quite loaded with meaning might not be very

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: fun always.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Like some difficult achievement that really helps a lot of people, maybe requires self-sacrifice

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: and hard work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So these things can, I think, come apart, which is something to bear in mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Also, if you're thinking about these utopia questions that you might actually start to

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: do some constructive thinking about that, you might have to isolate and distinguish

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: these different kinds of things that might be valuable in different ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Make sure you can sort of clearly perceive each one of them and then you can think about

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: how you can combine them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And just as you said, hopefully come up with a way to maximize all of them together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Yeah, or at least get, I mean, maximize or get like a very high score on a wide range

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: of them, even if not literally all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You can always come up with values that are exactly opposed to one another, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: But I think for many values, they are kind of opposed with, if you place them within

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: a certain dimensionality of your space, like there are shapes that are kind of, you can't

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: untangle in a given dimensionality, but if you start adding dimensions, then it might

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: in many cases just be that they are easy to pull apart and you could.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So we'll see how much space there is for that, but I think that there could be a lot in this

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: context of radical abundance if ever we get to that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: I don't think there's a better way to end it, Nick.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: You've influenced a huge number of people to work on what could very well be the most

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: important problems of our time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: So it's a huge honor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Thank you so much for talking to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Well, thank you for coming by, Lex.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: That was fun.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Thank you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: And now let me leave you with some words from Nick Bostrom.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Our approach to existential risks cannot be one of trial and error.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: There's no opportunity to learn from errors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: The reactive approach, see what happens, limit damages, and learn from experience is unworkable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Rather, we must take a proactive approach.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: This requires foresight to anticipate new types of threats and a willingness to take

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: decisive preventative action and to bear the costs, moral and economic, of such actions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nick Bostrom: Simulation and Superintelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #83

body.input: Thank you for listening and hope to see you next time.

body.input: This is the Lex Friedman podcast

body.input: and here is my conversation with Jay McClelland.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: You are one of the seminal figures

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: in the history of neural networks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: At the intersection of cognitive psychology

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and computer science,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: what to you has over the decades emerged

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: as the most beautiful aspect about neural networks?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Both artificial and biological.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: The fundamental thing I think about

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: with neural networks is how they allow us to link

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: biology with the mysteries of thought.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And, you know, when I was first entering the field myself

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: in the late 60s, early 70s,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: cognitive psychology had just become a field.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: There was a book published in 67 called Cognitive Psychology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And the author said that, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: the study of the nervous system was

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: only of peripheral interest.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: It wasn't gonna tell us anything about the mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I didn't agree with that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I always felt, oh, look, I'm a physical being.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I, from dust to dust, you know, ashes to ashes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And somehow I emerged from that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So that's really interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So there was a sense with cognitive psychology

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: that in understanding the sort of neuronal structure

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: of things, you're not going to be able

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: to understand the mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And then your sense is if we study these neural networks,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: we might be able to get at least very close

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: to understanding the fundamentals of the human mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I used to think, or I used to talk about the idea

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: of awakening from the Cartesian dream.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So Descartes, you know, thought about these things, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: He was walking in the gardens of Versailles one day

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and he stepped on a stone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And a statue moved.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And he walked a little further,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: he stepped on another stone and another statue moved.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And he like, why did the statue move

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: when I stepped on the stone?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And he went and talked to the gardeners

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and he found out that they had a hydraulic system

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: that allowed the physical contact with the stone

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: to cause water to flow in various directions

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: which caused water to flow under the statue

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and move the statue.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And he used this as the beginnings of a theory

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: about how animals act.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And he had this notion that these little fibers

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: that people had identified that weren't carrying the blood,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: you know, were these little hydraulic tubes

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: that if you touch something, there would be pressure

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and it would send a signal of pressure

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: to the other parts of the system and that would cause action.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So he had a mechanistic theory of animal behavior

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and he thought that the human had this animal body

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: but that some divine something else

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: had to have come down and been placed in him

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: to give him the ability to think, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So the physical world includes the body in action

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: but it doesn't include thought according to Descartes, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so the study of physiology at that time

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: was the study of sensory systems and motor systems

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and things that you could directly measure

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: when you stimulated neurons and stuff like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And the study of cognition was something that, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: was tied in with abstract computer algorithms

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and things like that.

body.input: Yeah, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Well, obvious and not obvious at the same time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But he wanted to figure out how it could have worked.

body.input: but not knowing why,

body.input: that differ slightly from each other and so on, you know?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And it's a very simple little computational unit,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: that's engaged in chug, chug one step after another,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: we have a billion of these little computational units

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So at the time that's, I don't know, maybe you can comment,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Oh, cause it was from the sixties.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yeah, yeah, by the late seventies,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: it was kind of old fashioned and it hadn't really panned out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And people were beginning to recognize that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But, and Rumelhart was like, yeah,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: he's part of the recognition that this wasn't all working.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Anyway, so he started thinking in terms of

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: the idea that we needed systems that allowed us

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: to integrate multiple simultaneous constraints

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: in a way that would be mutually influencing each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So he wrote a paper that just really,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: first time I read it, I thought, oh, well, you know, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But is this important?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But after a while, it just got under my skin

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and it was called an interactive model of reading.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And in this paper, he laid out the idea that every aspect

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: of our interpretation of what's coming off the page

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: when we read at every level of analysis you can think of

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: actually depends on all the other levels of analysis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So what are the actual pixels making up each letter?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And what did those pixels signify

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: about which letters they are?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And what do those letters tell us

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: about what words are there?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And what do those words tell us about what ideas

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: the author is trying to convey?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so he had this model where, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: we have these little tiny elements

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: that represent each of the pixels of each of the letters

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and then other ones that represent the line segments in them

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and other ones that represent the letters

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and other ones that represent the words.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And at that time, his idea was there's this set of experts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: There's an expert about how to construct a line out of pixels

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and another expert about how which sets of lines

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: go together to make which letters

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and another one about which letters go together

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: to make which words.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And another one about what the meanings of the words are

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and another one about how the meanings fit together

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and, you know, things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And all these experts are looking at this data

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and they're updating hypotheses at other levels.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So the word expert can tell the letter expert,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: oh, I think there should be a T there

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: because I think there should be a word, the, here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And the bottom up sort of feature to letter expert

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: could say, I think there should be a T there too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And if they agree, then you see a T, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so there's a top-down bottom-up interactive process,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: but it's going on at all layers simultaneously.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So everything can filter all the way down from the top

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: as well as all the way up from the bottom.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And it's a completely interactive bi-directional

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: parallel distributed process.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: That is somehow because of the abstractions is hierarchical.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So like, so there's different layers of responsibilities,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: different levels of responsibilities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: First of all, it's fascinating to think about

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: it in this kind of mechanistic way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So not thinking purely from the structure

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: of a neural network or something like a neural network.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But thinking about these little guys that work on letters

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and then the letters come words and words become sentences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And that's a very interesting hypothesis

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: that from that kind of hierarchical structure

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: can emerge understanding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yeah, so, but the thing is though,

body.input: I wanna just sort of relate this

body.input: to earlier part of the conversation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: You know, I think that from the emergentist side,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I disagree with that.

body.input: So I think, you know, I would call myself

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Because I want to acknowledge that these higher level

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: used to use that I thought was helpful in this respect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: under the wind and, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: reforming itself in somewhat different ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And if we think about our thoughts as like sand dunes

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: as being things that, you know, emerge from

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: just the way all the lower level elements

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: sort of work together and are constrained

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: by external forces, then we can say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: yes, they exist as such, but they also, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: we shouldn't treat them as completely monolithic entities

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: that we can understand without understanding

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: sort of all of the stuff that allows them to change

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: in the ways that they do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And that's where I think the connectionist

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: It's like, okay, so if the substrate

body.input: isn't, you know, like abstract and symbolic

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and, but it's more fluid maybe than,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yeah, that's a heck of a sort of thing to put

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: at the top of a resume, radical, emergentist connectionist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So there is, just like you said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: also it seems like unfair to eliminate the magic

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: of that emergent, like eliminate the fact

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: that that emergent is real.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yeah, no, I agree.
