metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I'm not, that's why I got rid of eliminative, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Eliminative, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yeah, because it seemed like that was trying to say

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: that it's all completely like...

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: An illusion of some kind, it's not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Well, who knows whether there isn't,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: there aren't some illusory characteristics there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I think that philosophically,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: many people have confronted that possibility over time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: but it's still important to accept it as magic, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So I think of Fellini in this context,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I think of others who have appreciated the role of magic,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: of actual trickery in creating illusions that move us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And Plato was on to this too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: It's like somehow or other these shadows

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: give us a sense of what's happening.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Give rise to something much deeper than that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And that's, so we won't try to figure out what it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: We'll just accept it as given that that occurs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And, but he was still onto the magic of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yeah, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: We won't try to really, really, really deeply understand

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: how it works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: We just enjoy the fact that it's kind of fun.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Okay, but you worked closely with Dave, Rahmohardt.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: He passed away as a human being.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: What do you remember about him?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Do you miss the guy?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: You know, he passed away 15-ish years ago now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And his demise was actually one of the most poignant,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and relevant tragedies relevant to our conversation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: He started to undergo a progressive neurological condition,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: that isn't fully understood.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: That is to say his particular course

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: isn't fully understood because he was a human being.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: His course isn't fully understood because, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: brain scans weren't done at certain stages

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and no autopsy was done or anything like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: The wishes of the family.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So we don't know as much about the underlying pathology

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: as we might, but I had begun to get interested

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: in this neurological condition that might have been

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: the very one that he was succumbing to as my own efforts

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: to understand another aspect of this mystery

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: that we've been discussing, while he was beginning

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: to get progressively more and more affected.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So I'm gonna talk about the disorder

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and not about Rahmohardt for a second, okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: The disorder is something my colleagues and collaborators

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: have chosen to call semantic dementia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So it's a specific form of loss of mind

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: related to meaning, semantic dementia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And it's progressive in the sense that the patient

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: loses the ability to appreciate the meaning

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: of the experiences that they have, either from touch,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: from sight, from sound, from language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: They, I hear sounds, but I don't know

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: what they mean kind of thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So as this illness progresses, it starts with the patient

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: being unable to differentiate like similar breeds of dog,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: or remember the lower frequency, unfamiliar categories

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: that they used to be able to remember.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But as it progresses, it becomes more and more striking

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and the patient is able to understand

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: what's striking and the patient loses the ability

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: to recognize things like pigs and goats and sheep

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and calls all middle-sized animals dogs

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and all can't recognize rabbits and rodents anymore.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: They call all the little ones cats

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and they can't recognize hippopotamuses and cows anymore.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: They call them all horses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So there was this one patient who went through

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: this progression where at a certain point,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: any four-legged animal, he would call it either a horse

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: or a dog or a cat.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And if it was big, he would tend to call it a horse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: If it was small, he'd tend to call it a cat.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Middle-sized ones, he called dogs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: This is just a part of the syndrome though.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: The patient loses the ability to relate concepts to each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So my collaborator in this work, Carolyn Patterson,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: developed a test called the pyramids and palm trees test.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So you give the patient a picture of pyramids

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and they have a choice which goes with the pyramids,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: palm trees or pine trees.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And she showed that this wasn't just a matter of language

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: because the patient's loss of this ability shows up

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: whether you present the material with words or with pictures.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: The pictures, they can't put the pictures together

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: with each other properly anymore.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: They can't relate the pictures to the words either.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: They can't do word-picture matching.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But they've lost the conceptual grounding

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: from either modality of input.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so that's why it's called semantic dementia,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: the very semantics is disintegrating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And we understand this in terms of our idea

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: that distributed representation, a pattern of activation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: represents the concepts, really similar ones.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: As you degrade them, they start being, you lose the differences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So the difference between the dog and the goat

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: sort of is no longer part of the pattern anymore.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And since dog is really familiar, that's the thing that remains.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And we understand that in the way the models work and learn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But Rummelhart underwent this condition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So on the one hand, it's a fascinating aspect

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: of parallel distributed processing to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And it reveals this sort of texture of distributed representation

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: in a very nice way, I've always felt.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But at the same time, it was extremely poignant

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: because this is exactly the condition that Rummelhart was undergoing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And there was a period of time when he was this man

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: who had been the most focused, goal-directed, competitive,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: thoughtful person who was willing to work for years to solve a hard problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And he starts to disappear.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And there was a period of time when it was hard for any of us

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: to really appreciate that he was sort of, in some sense,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: not fully there anymore.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Do you know if he was able to introspect

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: the solution of the understanding mind?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I mean, this is one of the big scientists that thinks about this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Was he able to look at himself and understand the fading mind?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: You know, we can contrast Hawking and Rummelhart in this way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I like to do that to honor Rummelhart

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: because I think Rummelhart is sort of like the Hawking of cognitive science to me in some ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Both of them suffered from a degenerative condition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: In Hawking's case, it affected the motor system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: In Rummelhart's case, it's affecting the semantics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And not just the pure object semantics, but maybe the self semantics as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And we don't understand that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Concepts broadly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But I would say he didn't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And this was part of what from the outside was a profound tragedy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But on the other hand, at some level, he sort of did

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: because there was a period of time when it finally was realized that he had really become profoundly impaired.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: This was clearly a biological condition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And it wasn't just like he was distracted that day or something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So he retired from his professorship at Stanford.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And he lived with his brother for a couple of years, and then he moved into a facility for people with cognitive impairments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: One that many elderly people end up in when they have cognitive impairments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I would spend time with him during that period.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: This was like in the late 90s, around 2000 even.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And we would go bowling.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And he could still bowl.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And after bowling, I took him to lunch and I said, where would you like to go?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: You want to go to Wendy's?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And he said, nah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I said, OK, well, where do you want to go?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And he just pointed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: He said, turn here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So he still had a certain amount of spatial cognition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And he could get me to the restaurant.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And then when we got to the restaurant, I said, what do you want to order?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And he couldn't come up with any of the words.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But he knew where on the menu the thing was that he wanted.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So he couldn't say what it was, but he knew that that's what he wanted to eat.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so it isn't monolithic at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Our cognition is, first of all, graded in certain kinds of ways, but also multipartite.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: There's many elements to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And certain sort of partial competencies still exist in the absence of other aspects of these competencies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So this is what always fascinated me about what used to be called cognitive neuropsychology,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: the effects of brain damage on cognition, but in particular, this gradual disintegration part.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I'm a big believer that the loss of a human being that you value is as powerful as first falling in love with that human being.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I think it's all a celebration of the human being.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So the disintegration itself, too, is a celebration in a way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But just to say something more about the scientist and the backpropagation idea that you mentioned.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So in 1982, Hinton had been there as a postdoc and organized that conference.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: He'd actually gone away and gotten an assistant professorship, and then there was this opportunity to bring him back.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So Jeff Hinton was back on a sabbatical.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: In San Diego.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And Rumelhart and I had decided we wanted to do this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: We thought it was really exciting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And the papers on the interactive activation model that I was telling you about had just been published.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And we both sort of saw huge potential for this work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And Jeff was there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so the three of us started a research group, which we called the PDP Research Group.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And several other people came.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Francis Crick, who was at the Salk Institute, heard about it from Jeff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Because Jeff was known among Brits to be brilliant, and Francis was well connected with his British friends.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So Francis Crick came.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: That's a heck of a group of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Wow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And Paul Spolanski was one of the other postdocs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: He was still there as a postdoc.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And a few other people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But anyway, Jeff talked to us about learning and how we should think about how learning occurs in a neural network.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And he said, the problem with the way you guys have been approaching this is that you've been looking for inspiration from biology

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: to tell you what the rules should be for how the synapses should change the strengths of their connections, how the connections should form.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: He said, that's the wrong way to go about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: What you should do is you should think in terms of how you can adjust connection weights to solve a problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So you define your problem, and then you figure out how the adjustment of the connection weights will solve the problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And Rummelhart heard that and said to himself, OK, so I'm going to start thinking about it that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I'm going to essentially imagine that I have some objective function, some goal of the computation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I want my machine to correctly classify all of these images.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I can score that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I can measure how well they're doing on each image.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I get some measure of error or loss, it's typically called, in deep learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I'm going to figure out how to adjust the connection weights so as to minimize my loss or reduce the error.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And that's called gradient descent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And engineers were already familiar with the concept of gradient descent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And in fact, there was an algorithm called the delta rule that had been invented by a professor in the electrical engineering department at Stanford, Bernie Widrow, and a collaborator named Hoff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I never met him.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So gradient descent in continuous neural networks with multiple neuron-like processing units was already understood for a single layer of connection weights.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: We have some inputs over a set of neurons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: We want the output to produce a certain pattern.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: We can define the difference between our target and what the narrow network is producing, and we can figure out how to change the connection weights to reduce that error.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So what Muromahar did was to generalize that so as to be able to change the connections from earlier layers of units to the ones at a hidden layer between the input and the output.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so he first called the algorithm the generalized delta rule because it's just an extension of the gradient descent idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And interestingly enough, Hinton was thinking that this wasn't going to work very well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So Hinton had his own alternative algorithm at the time based on the concept of the Bolson machine that he was pursuing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So the paper on the Bolson machine came out in, learning in Bolson machines came out in 1985.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But it turned out that backprop worked better than the Bolson machine learning algorithm.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So this generalized delta algorithm ended up being called backpropagation, as you say, backprop.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And, you know, probably that name is opaque to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: What does that mean?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: What it meant was that in order to figure out what the changes you needed to make to the connections from the input to the hidden layer,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: you had to back propagate the error signals from the output layer through the connections from the hidden layer to the output to get the signals that would be the error signals for the hidden layer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And that's how Rumelhart formulated it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: It was like, well, we know what the error signals are at the output layer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Let's see if we can get a signal at the hidden layer that tells each hidden unit what its error signal is essentially.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So it's back propagating through the connections from the hidden to the output to get the signals to tell the hidden units how to change their weights from the input.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And that's why it's called backprop.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yeah. But so it came from Hinton having introduced the concept of, you know, define your objective function,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: figure out how to take the derivatives so that you can adjust the connections so that they make progress towards your goal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So stop thinking about biology for a second and let's start to think about optimization and computation a little bit more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So what about Jeff Hinton? What you've gotten a chance to work with him in that little.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: The set of people involved there is quite incredible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: The small set of people under the PDP flag is just given the amount of impact those ideas have had over the years, it's kind of incredible to think about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But, you know, just like you said, like yourself, Jeffrey Hinton is seen as one of the not just like a seminal figure in AI, but just a brilliant person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Just like the horsepower of the mind is pretty high up there for him because he's just a great thinker.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So what kind of ideas have you learned from him? Have you influenced each other on? Have you debated over what stands out to you in the full space?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: In the full space of ideas here at the intersection of computation and cognition?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Well, so Jeff has said many things to me that had a profound impact on my thinking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And he's written several articles which were way ahead of their time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: He had two papers in 1981, just to give one example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: One of which was essentially the idea of transformers and another of which was an early paper on semantic cognition which inspired him and Rummelhart and me throughout the 80s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And, you know, still I think sort of grounds my own thinking about the semantic aspects of cognition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: He also, in a small paper that was never published that he wrote in 1977, you know, before he actually arrived at UCSD or maybe a couple of years even before that, I don't know, when he was a PhD student, he described how a neural network could do recursive computation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And it was a very clever idea that he's continued to explore over time, which was sort of the idea that when you call a subroutine, you need to save the state that you had when you called it so you can get back to where you were when you're finished with the subroutine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And the idea was that you would save the state of the calling routine by making fast changes to connection weights.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And then when you finished with the subroutine call, those fast changes in the connection weights would allow you to go back to where you had been before and reinstate the previous context so that you could continue on with the top level of the computation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Anyway, that was part of the idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I always thought, okay, that's really, you know, he just, he had extremely creative ideas that were quite a lot ahead of his time and many of them in the 1970s and early 1980s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So another thing about Jeff Hinton's way of thinking, which has profoundly influenced my effort to understand human mathematical cognition, is that he doesn't write too many equations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And people tell stories like, oh, in the Hinton lab meetings, you don't get up at the board and write equations like you do in everybody else's machine learning lab.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: What you do is you draw a picture.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And, you know, he explains aspects of the way deep learning works by putting his hands together and showing you the shape of a ravine and using that as a geometrical metaphor for what's happening as this gradient descent process.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: You're coming down the wall of a ravine. If you take too big a jump, you're going to jump to the other side.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so that's why we have to turn down the learning rate, for example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And it speaks to me of the fundamentally intuitive character of deep insight, together with a commitment to really understanding in a way that's absolutely, ultimately explicit and clear.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But also intuitive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yeah, there's certain people like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Here's an example, some kind of weird mix of visual and intuitive and all those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Feynman is another example, different style of thinking, but very unique.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And when you when you're around those people, for me in the engineering realm, there's a guy named Jim Keller, who is a chip designer engineer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Every time I talk to him, it doesn't matter what we're talking about, just having experienced that unique way of thinking transforms you and makes your work much better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And that's that's the magic. You look at Daniel Kahneman, you look at the great collaborations throughout the history of science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: That's the magic of that. It's not always the exact ideas that you talk about, but it's the process of generating those ideas, being around that, spending time with that human being.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: You can come up with some brilliant work, especially when it's cross disciplinary as it was a little bit in your case.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yeah. Jeff is a descendant of the logician bull.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: He comes from a long line of English academics and together with the deeply intuitive thinking ability that he has, he also has, you know, it's been clear he's he's described this to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I think he's mentioned it from time to time in other interviews with that he's had with people. You know, he's he's wanted to be able to sort of think of himself as contributing to the to the understanding of.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Reasoning itself, not just human reasoning, like bull like is about logic, right. It's about what can we conclude from what else and how do we formalize that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And as a computer scientist, logician, philosopher, you know, the goal is to understand how we derive truths from other from givens and things like this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And the work that Jeff was doing in the early to mid 80s on something called the Bolton machine was his way of connecting with that Boolean tradition and bringing it into the more continuous probabilistic graded constraint satisfaction realm.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And it was it was beautiful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: A set of ideas linked with theoretical physics and.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: As well as with logic, and it it's always been, I mean, I've always been inspired by the Bolton machine, too. It's like, well, if the neurons are probabilistic rather than, you know, deterministic in their computations, then you know that that maybe this somehow is part of the.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Serendipity or, you know, adventitiousness of the moment of insight, right. It might not have occurred at that particular instant. It might be sort of partially the result of a stochastic process.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And and and that, too, is part of the magic of the emergence of.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Some of these things. Well, you're right with the Boolean lineage and the dream of computer science is somehow. I mean, I certainly think of humans this way that humans are one particular manifestation of intelligence that there's something bigger going on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And you're trying to you're hoping to figure that out. The mechanisms of intelligence, the mechanisms of cognition are much bigger than just humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yeah. So I think of I've I started using the phrase computational intelligence at some point as to characterize the the field that I thought, you know, people like Jeff Hinton and many of the of the people I know at DeepMind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Are are working in and where I feel like I'm.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: You know, I'm a I'm a kind of a human oriented computational intelligence researcher in that I'm actually kind of interested in the human solution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But at the same time, I I I feel like that's that's where a huge amount of the.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: The excitement of deep learning actually lies is in the idea that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: You know, we may be able to even go beyond what we can achieve with our own nervous systems when we build computational intelligence as that are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: You know, not limited in the ways that we are by our own biology, perhaps allowing us to scale the very mechanisms of human intelligence, just increase its power through scale.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yes. And and I think that that, you know, obviously that's the.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: That's being played out massively at Google Brain, at OpenAI and to some extent, a deep mind as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I guess I shouldn't say to some extent that this the massive scale of the computations that are used to succeed at games like Go or to solve the protein folding problems that they've been solving and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Still not as many synapses and neurons as the human brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So we still got we still still beating them on that we humans are being the AIs, but they're catching up pretty quickly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: You write about modeling of mathematical cognition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So let me first ask about mathematics in general.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: There's a paper titled Parallel Distributed Processing Approach to Mathematical Cognition, where in the introduction, there's some beautiful discussion of mathematics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And you reference there Tristan Needham, who criticizes a narrow form of your mathematics by liking the studying of mathematics as symbol manipulation to studying music without ever hearing a note.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So from that perspective, what do you think is mathematics?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: What is this world of mathematics like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Well, I think of mathematics as a set of tools for exploring idealized worlds that often turn out to be extremely relevant to the real world, but need not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But they're worlds in which objects exist with idealized properties.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And in which the relationships among them can be characterized with precision, so as to allow the implications of certain facts to then allow you to derive other facts with certainty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So, you know, if you have two triangles, and you know that there is an angle in the first one that has the same measure as an angle in the second one, and you know that the lengths of the sides adjacent to that angle in each of the two triangles,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: the corresponding sides adjacent to that angle are also have the same measure, then you can then conclude that the triangles are congruent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: That is to say they have all of their properties in common.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And that is something about triangles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: It's not a matter of formulas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: These are idealized objects.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: In fact, you know, we built bridges out of triangles, and we understand how to measure the height of something we can't climb by extending these ideas about triangles a little further.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And, you know, all of the ability to get a tiny speck of matter launched from the planet Earth to intersect with some tiny, tiny little body way out in way beyond Pluto somewhere,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: at exactly a predicted time and date is something that depends on these ideas, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And it's actually happening in the real physical world that these ideas make contact with it in those kinds of instances.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so, but, you know, there are these idealized objects, these triangles or these distances or these points, whatever they are,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: that allow for this set of tools to be created that then gives human beings the, it's this incredible leverage that they didn't have without these concepts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I think this is actually already true when we think about just, you know, the natural numbers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I always like to include zero, so I'm going to say the non-negative integers, but that's a place where some people prefer not to include zero, but...

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: We like zero here. Natural numbers, zero, one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yeah. And, you know, because they give you the ability to be exact about, like, how many sheep you have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Like, you know, I sent you out this morning, there were 23 sheep. You came back with only 22. What happened?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yeah. The fundamental problem of physics, how many sheep you have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: It's a fundamental problem of human society that you damn well better bring back the same number of sheep as you started with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And, you know, it allows commerce, it allows contracts, it allows the establishment of records and so on to have systems that allow these things to be notated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But they have an inherent aboutness to them. That's one at the one in the same time sort of abstract and idealized and generalizable, while at the other, on the other hand, potentially very, very grounded and concrete.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And one of the things that makes for the incredible achievements of the human mind is the fact that humans invented these idealized systems that leverage the power of human thought in such a way as to allow all this kind of thing to happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so that's what mathematics to me is the development of systems for thinking about the properties and relations among sets of idealized objects.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And, you know, the mathematical notation system that we unfortunately focus way too much on is just our way of expressing propositions about these properties.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Right. It's just like we're talking with Chomsky in language. It's the thing we've invented for the communication of those ideas. They're not necessarily the deep representation of those ideas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So what's a good way to model such powerful mathematical reasoning, would you say? What are some ideas you have for capturing this in a model?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Well, one of the insights that human mathematicians have had is a combination of the kind of the intuitive kind of connectionist-like knowledge that makes it so that something is just like obviously true,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: that you don't have to think about why it's true, that then makes it possible to then take the next step and ponder and reason and figure out something that you previously didn't have that intuition about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: It then ultimately becomes a part of the intuition that the next generation of mathematical thinkers have to ground their own thinking on so that they can extend the ideas even further.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I came across this quotation from Henri Poincaré while I was walking in the woods with my wife in a state park in Northern California late last summer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And what it said on the bench was, it is by logic that we prove, but by intuition that we discover.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so what for me the essence of the project is to understand how to bring the intuitive connectionist resources to bear on letting the intuitive discovery arise from engagement in thinking with this formal system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So I think of the ability of somebody like Hinton or Newton or Einstein or Rumelhart or Poincaré to Archimedes, this is another example, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So suddenly a flash of insight occurs. It's like the constellation of all of these simultaneous constraints that somehow or other causes the mind to settle into a novel state that it never did before and give rise to a new idea that then you can say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: okay, well now how can I prove this? How do I write down the steps of that theorem that allow me to make it rigorous and certain?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so I feel like the kinds of things that we're beginning to see deep learning systems do of their own accord kind of gives me this feeling of, I don't know, hope or encouragement

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: that ultimately it'll all happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So in particular, as many people now have become really interested in thinking about, neural networks that have been trained with massive amounts of text can be given a prompt and they can then sort of generate some really interesting, fanciful, creative story from that prompt.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And there's kind of like a sense that they've somehow synthesized something like novel out of all of the particulars of all of the billions and billions of experiences that went into the training data that gives rise to something like this sort of intuitive sense of what would be a fun and interesting little story to tell

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: or something like that. It just sort of wells up out of the letting the thing play out its own imagining of what somebody might say given this prompt as an input to get it to start to generate its own thoughts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And to me that sort of represents the potential of capturing the intuitive side of this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And there's other examples, I don't know if you find them as captivating, on the deep mind side with AlphaZero, if you study chess, the kind of solutions that has come up in terms of chess, there's novel ideas there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: It feels very like there's brilliant moments of insight. And the mechanism they use, if you think of search as maybe more towards good old fashioned AI and then there's the connectionist network that has the intuition of looking at a board, looking at a set of patterns, and saying how good is this set of positions, and the next few positions, how good are those?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And that's it. That's just the intuition. Grandmasters have this, an understanding positionally, tactically, how good the situation is, how can it be improved without doing this full, deep search.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And then maybe doing a little bit of what human chess players call calculation, which is the search. Taking a particular set of steps down the line to see how they unroll.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But there is moments of genius in those systems, too. So that's another hopeful illustration that from neural networks can emerge this novel creation of an idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yes. And I think Demis Hesavis, he's spoken about those things. I heard him describe a move that was made in one of the Go matches against Lise Adol in a very similar way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: It caused me to become really excited to collaborate with some of those guys at DeepMind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So I think, though, that what I like to really emphasize here is one part of what I like to emphasize about mathematical cognition, at least, is that philosophers and logicians going back three or even a little more than 3000 years ago

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: began to develop these formal systems and gradually the whole idea about thinking formally got constructed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And it's preceded Euclid, certainly present in the work of Thales and others. I'm not the world's leading expert in all the details of that history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But Euclid's elements were the kind of the touch point of a coherent document that sort of laid out this idea of an actual formal system within which these objects were characterized

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and the system of inference that allowed new truths to be derived from others was sort of established as a paradigm.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And what I find interesting is the idea that the ability to become a person who is capable of thinking in this abstract formal way is a result of the same kind of immersion

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: in experience thinking in that way that we now begin to think of our understanding of language as being.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So we immerse ourselves in a particular language, in a particular world of objects and their relationships, and we learn to talk about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And we develop intuitive understanding of the real world in a similar way we can think that what academia has created for us,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: what those early philosophers and their academies in Athens and Alexandria and other places allowed was the development of these schools of thought, modes of thought,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: that then become deeply ingrained and it becomes what it is that makes it so that somebody like Jerry Fodor would think that systematic thought is the essential characteristic of the human mind

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: as opposed to a derived and acquired characteristic that results from acculturation in a certain mode that's been invented by humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Would you say it's more fundamental than language if we start dancing, if we bring Chomsky back into the conversation? First of all, is it unfair to draw a line between mathematical cognition and language, linguistic cognition?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I think that's a very interesting question. And I think it's one of the ones that I'm actually very interested in right now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But I think the answer is in important ways, it is important to draw that line,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: but then to come back and look at it again and see some of the subtleties and interesting aspects of the difference.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So if we think about Chomsky himself, he was born into an academic family. His father was a professor of rabbinical studies at a small rabbinical college in Philadelphia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And he was deeply enculturated in a culture of thought and reason and brought to the effort to understand natural language this profound engagement with these formal systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I think that there was tremendous power in that and that Chomsky had some amazing insights into the structure of natural language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But that, I'm going to use the word but there, the actual intuitive knowledge of these things only goes so far and does not go as far as it does in people like Chomsky himself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And this was something that was discovered in the PhD dissertation of Lila Gleitman, who was actually trained in the same linguistics department with Chomsky.
