metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So what Lila discovered was that the intuitions that linguists had about even the meaning of a phrase, not just about its grammar,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: but about what they thought a phrase must mean were very different from the intuitions of an ordinary person who wasn't a formally trained thinker.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And well, it recently has become much more salient. I happened to have learned about this when I myself was a PhD student at the University of Pennsylvania.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But I never knew how to put it together with all of my other thinking about these things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So I actually currently have the hypothesis that formally trained linguists and other formally trained academics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: whether it be linguistics, philosophy, cognitive science, computer science, machine learning, mathematics, have a mode of engagement with experience that is intuitively deeply structured

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: to be more organized around the systematicity and ability to be conformant with the principles of a system

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: than is actually true of the natural human mind without that immersion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: It's fascinating. So the different fields and approaches with which you start to study the mind actually take you away from the natural operation of the mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So it makes it very difficult for you to be somebody who introspects.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yes. And this is where things about human belief and so-called knowledge that we consider private, not our business to manipulate in others.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: We are not entitled to tell somebody else what to believe about certain kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: What are those beliefs? Well, they are the product of this sort of immersion and enculturation. That is what I believe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And that's limiting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: It's something to be aware of.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Does that limit you from having a good model of cognition?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: It can.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So when you look at mathematical or linguistics, what is that line then?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So is Chomsky unable to sneak up to the full picture of cognition? Are you, when you're focusing on mathematical thinking, are you also unable to do so?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I think you're right. I think that's a great way of characterizing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I also think that it's related to the concept of beginner's mind and another concept called the expert blind spot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So the expert blind spot is much more prosaic seeming than this point that you were just making, but it's something that plagues experts when they try to communicate their understanding to non-experts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And that is that things are self-evident to them that they can't begin to even think about how they could explain it to somebody else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: It's just so patently obvious that it must be true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: You know, like when Kronacker said, God made the natural numbers, all else is the work of man, he was expressing that intuition that somehow or other,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: the basic fundamentals of discrete quantities being countable and innumerable and indefinite in number was not something that had to be discovered.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But he was wrong. It turns out that many cognitive scientists agreed with him for a time. There was a long period of time where the natural numbers were considered to be part of the innate endowment of core knowledge

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: or to use the kind of phrases that Spelke and Carey used to talk about what they believe are the innate primitives of the human mind. And they no longer believe that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: It's actually been more or less accepted by almost everyone that the natural numbers are actually a cultural construction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And it's so interesting to go back and sort of like study those few people who still exist who don't have those systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So this is just an example to me where a certain mode of thinking about language itself or a certain mode of thinking about geometry and those kinds of relations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: so it becomes so second nature that you don't know what it is that you need to teach. And in fact, we don't really teach it all that explicitly anyway.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222
